whole macadamia kernel and acute canine impaired movement — Weakness and ataxia followed kernel exposure in field cases, and four experimental dogs had marked weakness and trouble standing. This acute poisoning model did not test cold-pressed oil or Parkinson bradykinesia.

oral linoleic-rich oil and gait in Friedreich ataxia — Gait scores declined during both oil and lecithin periods, with less decline numerically during oil. No group difference or cold-press grade establishes Parkinson's walking slowness.

whole oral safflower and Huntington combined motor scale — In the blinded phase adjusted motor change was +0.7 on safflower and +1.3 on active oil. The gait item result and walking speed were unavailable. Processing grade is undisclosed.
safflower comparator and timed four-metre walk in older adults — Walk times fell in both arms alongside resistance training and had no group effect. Oil grade and oil-alone effect are unknown.

USP oil comparator and one-minute walking in Friedreich ataxia — Walking distance declined 220.42 inches in the oil arm and 193.83 inches on RT001 at month 11. Between-arm p=0.8061. Disease progression, comparator and oil grade prevent attributing decline to cold-pressed safflower.

registered safflower comparator in a progressive supranuclear palsy trial — Oral safflower is named in the US arm descriptions. The registered outcome is a PSP composite at 48 weeks. No walking speed, oil grade or published arm estimates were located.
Dietary safflower composition and gait speed in sarcopenia — Trial plans a 400 m outcome and two oil compositions. Registry excludes movement-limiting neurologic disease and has no results.

Randomized Parkinson multi-food diet includes tarragon recipes and a Part III motor examination containing a facial-expression item — The menu calls for tarragon but does not explicitly specify dried herb or species; actual individual intake is unknown, and only motor totals rather than facial-expression item or tarragon-specific results are reported.
canola oil and simulated bread bolus properties — Canola mixtures reduced several physical texture measures in an artificial bolus. Human swallowing was unmeasured.

canola in minced food and sensory swallowing qualities — Seven healthy adults rated the canola-containing food smoother than food with no added fat. No clinical swallow test or cold-pressed grade was reported.

rapeseed-containing texture-modified recipes and oral processing — Healthy-volunteer oral processing and simulated bolus mechanics. Oil and texture were not varied independently. No Parkinson swallowing severity result.

canola blend and subjective ease of swallowing in a patent example — Within one patent narrative a patient described the mixture as easy to swallow. There is no controlled impairment outcome or independently changed oil.
fresh extract and dream recall after menopause — Dream recall showed no clear change. No dream-enactment events were measured.

walnut oil in a Parkinson diet menu with composite motor score — Appendix A names walnut oil and the motor examination includes rigidity. The paper gives no oil preparation, isolated walnut oil arm or rigidity item estimate.

named unrefined cold-pressed walnut oil in a fly Parkinson model — Feeding walnut oil with rotenone improved climbing versus toxin alone. Fly climbing does not measure muscle rigidity and oil alone did not noticeably alter short-term locomotion.
crude green cardamom extract in isolated intestines — Contractions increased or relaxed depending on tissue and preparation. Bowel movements and Parkinson constipation were unmeasured.

green cardamom powder with digestive adverse-event reporting — Early diarrhea occurred in two cardamom recipients and constipation in one placebo recipient. The trial did not measure chronic constipation efficacy or Parkinson’s.

cardamom-containing mixture and composite IBS severity — IBS-SSS improved in the uncontrolled trial. The score includes dissatisfaction with bowel habits and does not isolate a validated constipation endpoint or cardamom.

cardamom-containing supplement, selected bowel comments and adverse-event reports — The supplement lists 13 and ten selected comments. No arm-level constipation prevalence or validated severity estimate. Cardamom species and grind unverified.

isolated constituent and rodent learning tests — The first paper reports favorable avoidance and object recognition at the highest dose. Clinical executive function and ground seed were untested. Cohort overlap and correction scope remain open.

anise aqueous extract and healthy-rat habituation — The highest extract group maintained peripheral movement and rearing across the open-field session, indicating reduced within-session habituation. Executive impairment and Parkinson disease were unmeasured.
total anise seed extract and animal memory tasks — In healthy mice, authors report no clear overall memory effect while describing an individual quadrant result. No clinical executive endpoint.

chromatographic anise fraction and animal maze tasks — A separated aqueous-extract fraction changed task behavior in scopolamine-treated mice. Formulation, outcomes and internal report inconsistencies limit transfer.

fish oil and gait-related beam outcome in rats — The oral fish oil alone comparison did not clearly improve narrow-beam performance in rotenone rats. The quercetin combination improved the beam outcome. Stride length was not measured.

fish oil and human stride length — Fish oil plus exergame training versus olive oil plus identical training gave time-by-group p = .753 for single-task stride length and .537 for dual-task stride length. Participants did not have Parkinson disease. The single-task time main effect was p = .774.
injected DHA and rat stride length — Purified injected DHA increased stride length in a toxin-lesioned rat model. The 2019 abstract reports the same line of work. No oral trout was tested.
oral tarragon extract and general maze locomotion — Maze arm entries do not quantify postural stability. The oral extract is distinct from the earlier injected essential-oil experiments.

tarragon essential oil and mouse motor impairment — Some anticonvulsant doses caused acute rotarod impairment. This is a concentrated preparation and the experiment did not measure postural instability after fresh tarragon.
injected sumac extract and mouse open-field activity — Open-field activity is a distinct locomotor outcome and did not significantly change after injected extract.
sumac fruit drink during exercise in healthy volunteers — The sumac drink arm had lower post-exercise pain. Clinical walking speed was not an endpoint.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — Dyskinesia severity was not reported by herb intake or preparation.

oral grapeseed oil cookie and registered grip strength — Registered secondary correlation analysis included grip strength. The published results report biomarkers without grip, dexterity or Parkinson outcomes. Oil pressing was unspecified.

oral grapeseed oil cookie and registered grip strength — The single-arm pilot plans grip-strength correlations with cardiolipin in healthy adults. No posted results. Grip strength differs from dexterity and no Parkinson cohort is enrolled.

hydroalcoholic grape seed extract and forepaw measures in Parkinson-model rats — Forepaw stride length increased (p < .05) and grid-descent latency fell (p < .01). The extract, rodent measures and model leave clinical hand dexterity after cold-pressed oil unresolved.

grapeseed oil wristband and hand motor tests — The patent reports 12% higher finger tapping speed, 15% higher precision speed and 14% higher steadiness after four weeks in its grapeseed wristband group. Study size was small, dispersion was unreported and exposure was topical in healthy men.

curry leaf extract and timed motor tasks in rotenone mice — The publisher figure shows shorter beam and pole times after leaf extract given before rotenone exposure. Approximate times were 7 versus 108 seconds for beam traversal and 10 versus 13 seconds for pole descent. Ground leaf and clinical bradykinesia were untested.

oral aqueous curry leaf extract and movement initiation in rats — The paraquat-exposed extract groups initiated movement faster and showed shorter bar-test immobility. No ground leaf or clinical bradykinesia outcome was tested.

curry leaf fractions and haloperidol catalepsy in mice — The fractions prolonged bar-test catalepsy and reduced apomorphine-associated movement. The extracts and tests differ from the paraquat study and from clinical bradykinesia after ground leaf.

methanol curry leaf extract and drug-induced catalepsy — At 120 minutes bar-test immobility averaged 110.0 seconds with the highest extract level versus 256.7 seconds with haloperidol alone. The 113.0-second extract value is from 150 minutes. The lead author's 2021 fractions produced an opposite signal under another protocol. Neither tests ground leaf or clinical bradykinesia.

curry leaf coingredients and IBS rather than motor outcomes — The official species-targeted registry hit links to one crossover with a composite bowel symptom result. It provides no bradykinesia estimate.

curry leaves in a Parkinson diet menu with composite motor score — The menu lists curry leaves and UPDRS III includes bradykinesia. The pilot gives no isolated curry leaf arm, verified ground preparation or separate bradykinesia estimate.

basil odor identification in Parkinson’s — Participants with Parkinson’s misidentified the basil item 74.3% of the time. Exposure was an odor identification stimulus with no basil ingestion or pre/post olfactory treatment comparison.

memory-care almond comparator and combined neuropsychiatric symptoms — The recovered model estimates total NPI at 7.97 for almond oil and 8.68 for lavender, difference .71 (p = .0022). Visual hallucinations were not reported separately and almond oil was topical and diffused.

coconut odor recognition and standing lightheadedness — Gaining recognition of coconut odor was associated with higher MDS-UPDRS item 1.12 scores (B = 1.147, nominal p = .003). The study used odor strips and no coconut oil intake.

Parkinson-related rat histology after leaf extract — Injected leaf hexane fraction preserved TH-positive neurons in the 6-OHDA experiment. The overlapping journal report contains no identified stride measure.
essential oil and nonspecific mouse motor impairment — The seizure-model report describes motor impairment and sedation under essential oil. It does not quantify stride length.

oral ethanol seed extract and motor assays in haloperidol mice — Highest extract group had better cylinder movement and rotarod latency. This is a pharmacological mouse model with no clinical bradykinesia measure.

seed extract and motor assays in rotenone-exposed rats — The author abstract reports better open-field, narrow-beam and hanging performance. Clinical bradykinesia and culinary ground nutmeg remain unmeasured.

oral nutmeg solvent extracts and general mouse locomotion — Three oral extracts increased general activity at 500 mg/kg. Higher dichloromethane and delipidated methanol did not show a clear locomotor effect. This is spontaneous movement in healthy mice rather than clinical bradykinesia.

Capsicum fruit fractions and mouse anxiety-like outcomes — A hexane fraction increased open-arm entries and time in a mouse maze. Muscle relaxation and induced sedation can affect behavior. The experiment provides no smoked paprika or Parkinson exposure.

repeated oral isolated capsaicin and anxiety-like behavior in intact rats — Open-arm entry and time decreased after oral capsaicin, and the stress corticosterone elevation lasted longer. Parkinson anxiety, smoke preparation and food dose were unavailable.

repeated oral isolated capsaicin after oral sensory denervation — Center activity and general locomotion increased, while elevated plus-maze outcomes did not clearly differ. Forced-swim immobility p=.0547. Both basal and stress corticosterone increased. The altered sensory model limits transfer.

isolated oral capsaicin and anxiety events in runners — Supplement anxiety was 5% in both capsaicin and placebo immediately after exercise and 15% versus 10% at 24 hours. Pooled OR 1.43 (95% CI .26–7.74). No smoked paprika or clinical severity comparison.
oral Capsicum pubescens and DASS anxiety — Different pepper species, inconsistent anxiety table and no valid between-group test. Reported within-group comparisons do not establish an effect.

leaf extract and gastric-emptying mechanism — An ethanol-loaded rat experiment linked isolated leaf sesquiterpenes to slower gastric emptying. The experiment did not administer levodopa or measure medicine OFF time.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S7.514 and S7.519 use apple tree material in branch testing or grafting. Separate references study fruit ripening optics. None administers baked apple or tests dystonia.

Baked apple in the low-fat menu of a randomized Parkinson diet trial — The supplement documents preparation and planned servings. Table 2 provides the Part IV aggregate without the painful OFF-state dystonia item or a baked-apple comparison. Individual baked-apple intake is unavailable.
red pepper decoction and mouse pole performance — Three oral aqueous decoction groups had shorter pole-test times in the MPTP mouse experiment. Freezing episode frequency was outside the study.
Parkinson case with formula and walking trajectory — Walking improved during combination therapy and daily rehabilitation. The clinical course contains no separate freezing-frequency measurement.
Japanese pepper distillate and motor performance — An intranasal related-species extract shortened mouse pole descent and prolonged rota-rod latency. The tasks do not count freezing.
mint-flavored gum and short walking tests in a Parkinson cohort — Gait composite improved but 10-meter walking and timed mobility comparisons were null. No brewed spearmint exposure.
brewed spearmint and six-minute walk in knee osteoarthritis — No significant walking-distance difference. Both groups received spearmint tea and no Parkinson cohort was included.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S1.97 proposes parsley as a possible dietary source of related Rubisco peptides while modelling spinach-derived rubiscolin. No parsley isolate, dose or Parkinson outcome is measured.

parsley root juice and cramps — Reported cramps decreased from 334 to 206 after root juice in an uncontrolled comparison. Reported percentages do not reconcile to one stated denominator. No dystonia was measured.

timed speech in oral safflower crossover in Friedreich ataxia — Small timed speech improvement during safflower periods was reported. The authors found no significant comparative effect on specific clinical features and report practice gains. The speech endpoint, disease and oil grade limit transfer to Parkinson.

safflower oil comparator and Huntington scale with dysarthria item — The UHDRS dysarthria score considers whether speech can be understood. The study paper reports only the total motor comparison without item estimates.

USP oil comparator and ALS items with speech — The full report gives overall ALSFRS-R and ALSAQ-40 changes. ALSFRS-R total declined 4.91 points with safflower oil and 3.00 with RT001. Baseline bulbar onset is separate from post-treatment speech and the paper gives no intelligibility result.

oral safflower comparator with singing acoustics in nonrandom alternating design — Max SPL fell 1.23 dB on oil with a CI spanning zero. Low-pitch energy range increased descriptively and the comparative test was nominal. Speaking intelligibility and cold-press grade are unresolved.

safflower comparator, phonation threshold pressure and voice effort — Professional voice users are planned and the sponsor lists no results. The outcome is sustained voice production effort and pressure rather than listener intelligibility.

RCT of oral safflower comparator and singer voice self-ratings — Singing voice handicap improved across groups. Nominal interaction p=0.046 exceeded the adjusted 0.017 threshold. A listener intelligibility assessment and product processing were absent.
sprouted chickpea composition — The study measured plant tissue chemistry by spectrophotometry. It did not test roasted chickpeas or dyskinesia.

cinnamon in both diets and daytime sleepiness by diet — The eight-week ketogenic comparison favored the ketogenic plan by 0.45 points on the daytime sleepiness item. Both plans included cinnamon, and the randomized comparison gives no ground-cinnamon effect.

Human clove-oil gargle trial with severe sore throat including hoarseness — The published sore-throat result used a composite grade. It provides no isolated hoarseness count or acoustic low-volume assessment in Parkinson disease.
Registered clove-oil lozenge arm and postoperative sore throat — The registry lists sore throat and pain, without vocal intensity or public results. Route and population differ from the frozen claim.

Human Parkinson multi-odor trial with matched motor scale components — Figure 6 reports total MDS-UPDRS and Parts I–IV. The report provides no component speech item result or acoustic sound-pressure level, and the eugenol exposure was inhaled.

plasma alpha-linolenic acid and finger tapping in early Parkinson’s — Age-adjusted finger tapping ρ = −.179 (p = .289) and hand movement ρ = −.232 (p = .167). These were ordinal exam scores, with no dexterity test or flaxseed oil intake contrast.

flaxseed table oil and learned motor sequence in healthy older adults — Frontal Assessment Battery motor series improved by 0.50 points with flaxseed oil and 0.10 with corn oil (p = .140). The task assesses learned sequences, not Parkinson manual dexterity, and the oil pressing method remains unverified.

acute nutmeg poisoning and descriptive attention impairment — The case reported poor concentration and lapses of attention after overdose. Prior LSD use and the acute exposure limit attribution and generalization.

seed extract and cognitive task performance in rotenone-exposed rats — Maze-task changes were reported. The measured tasks include learning, exploration and motor demands and give no isolated attention estimate.

multi-ingredient tonic and concentration complaints — The uncontrolled study reported concentration changes after a formula with several active ingredients. An effect specific to nutmeg was unavailable.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The Petroselinum crispum entry describes furanocoumarins and primary photosensitization. The broader common-name cross-reference includes other genera. No frozen culinary or Parkinson symptom result appears.

freeze-dried parsley in a combined rat diet and stool mass — Both soup mixtures contained 5 g parsley per 100 g. They differed from the control in many foods and diet components. Fecal mass was higher in both mixtures. Fresh parsley, Parkinson disease and clinical constipation severity were not isolated.

parsley seed extract and colon water absorption — Aqueous parsley seed extract significantly reduced water absorption in perfused rat colon. The study tested tissue transport, with no fresh culinary parsley consumption or clinical constipation measure.

mixed parsley sauce meal with unresolved report provenance — A 2014 education study describes this exact Christmas-edition publication as invented. The apparent uncontrolled bowel comparisons yield no reliable evidence for a fresh-parsley effect.

Inhaled or topical oil and patient-reported mobility in Parkinson disease — After massage and aroma massage, one of four reported less difficulty walking half a mile. Table 15 provides no standardized balance or postural instability test and no minced herb intervention.

Topical blended compress and exercises with formal balance scoring — One older adult with painful joints improved from 8 to 30 on the Berg scale after combined exercise, warming, and a ginger and lemongrass compress. No isolate, oral exposure, or Parkinson diagnosis.

Oral concentrated leaf extract in rodent Parkinson-like movement models — The ethanolic extract changed catalepsy and locomotor outcomes. The model does not estimate a food effect on human Parkinson postural instability.

oral lemongrass essential oil and accumulated rotarod duration in mice — Table 1 gives an inconclusive comparison of total time on the rod. The healthy animal actual preparation and duration metric differ from a clinical balance outcome.

oral lemongrass essential oil and mouse rotarod first-fall latency and count — The figure shows earlier and more falls at two doses and conflicts with the prose on latency direction. Clinical postural instability and minced herb were unmeasured.

injected caraway constituent and mouse sedation — Injected S-(+)-carvone reduced ambulation and prolonged pentobarbital sleep. Sedation and drug-induced sleep do not measure fatigue after ground caraway in Parkinson disease.
exact raw romaine in a randomized feeding comparison with unrelated outcomes — The authors measured postprandial metabolites and cytokines. Facial expression was outside the study.
red lettuce microgreen extract and fly climbing — Climbing improved in a paraquat model. Species-level overlap provides model context with no face measure or romaine identification.

roasted whole flaxseed and Epworth Sleepiness Scale — Epworth means 11.50 to 11.32 in a before-and-after study of students. Table 1 prints p = .023 and the Results text says no clear change. The study had no control group or oil exposure.

grape polyphenols and objective sleep duration in severe sleep apnea — Sleep time reduced with supplement. Epworth used for exclusion and no post-treatment sleepiness result identified. Duration is a distinct outcome.
grape juice and pre-exercise Epworth scores in runners — Pre-exercise scales describe earlier rest. No validated clinical effect of an intervention on daytime sleepiness.
juice plus exercise — The two papers describe one registered study. Juice supplied no clear added functional or cognitive benefit.

black lentils within a rectal mixed preparation and aggregate Parkinson motor measures — Original 2017 and repeated 2024 reports describe one 15-person cohort. The mixed rectal preparation contains oil, Mucuna, Withania and black lentils of unresolved species. There is no isolated oral lentil or rigidity-specific estimate.

lentils among Parkinson menu options and motor examination total — The plant menu group had a lower four-week motor total. The comparison does not isolate lentils or preparation, and rigidity was not reported separately.

injected red lentil extract and drug-induced posture persistence in rats — Higher injected doses lowered catalepsy scores after perphenazine. The experiment did not test boiled oral lentils or clinical Parkinson rigidity.
shared Parkinson vegetarian menu with lentils and motor composite — The two small groups improved on total UPDRS III. The study gives no lentil preparation, isolated intake or rigidity item contrast.

lentils among prebiotic menu options and composite motor score — A four-week menu and lactulose intervention produced an inconclusive motor total change. Published data do not isolate lentil preparation or intake and omit individual rigidity changes.

cooked chervil soup and allergy-associated voice changes — An allergy case reported a voice change with throat and uvular symptoms after cooked chervil soup. The report does not quantify voice volume or examine Parkinson disease.

chervil in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome — The menu lists chervil and the motor examination includes speech. Plant preparation, isolated chervil exposure and voice volume item changes are unavailable.

mixed pepper supplement and diary-recorded urgent voids — Urgent voids declined from 4.71 to 2.53 per day on a multicomponent treatment in an uncontrolled cohort. Pepper contribution and culinary smoked paprika effects remain unidentified.

oral Capsicum-containing combination and urgency intensity outside Parkinson disease — Urgency score improved in both groups with a lower post-treatment value in the mix arm. Enrollment figures conflict and pepper was not isolated. No smoked paprika or Parkinson estimate.

item-level self-attribution for chili and hot peppers in bladder pain syndrome — Original Table 2 rates chili at −1.51 and hot peppers at −1.44 on an attribution scale. The symptom rating aggregates bladder symptoms, with no smoked paprika or isolated urgency frequency.

case-crossover for grouped spicy foods and composite bladder pain flares — Spicy foods gave OR 0.99 (95% CI 0.81–1.22) overall and OR 1.67 in the suspected diet trigger subgroup. Urgency frequency and smoked paprika were unisolated.

hot pepper and grouped spicy food self-attribution in a veterans bladder-pain cohort — Symptom sensitivity to hot pepper was more commonly reported in bladder pain syndrome. The item combines urinary or bladder symptoms and does not quantify smoked paprika or urgency episodes.

grouped spicy foods and urgency urinary incontinence — The study did not report a statistically significant adjusted association for spicy foods. Urgency incontinence and episode frequency are distinct, and smoked paprika exposure was unavailable.

combined cruciferous vegetables and anxiety in healthcare workers — The combined food item had rho −.231 for DASS anxiety (p=.004). Consumption coding is unresolved and no specific roasted cauliflower estimate is available.

cruciferous vegetable recalls and estimated indole intake — The study includes broccoli, cauliflower and kale within a food inventory. Neither constituent exposure nor a symptom effect is established for a particular preparation.

combined cruciferous vegetable frequency and anxiety measured in a Parkinson cohort — The original dietary abstract pooled cauliflower and broccoli. The journal reports an anxiety scale without linking it to cauliflower. Preparation and direction remain open.

oral safflower seed oil and lying and standing pressure — Standing systolic means were 116 on safflower and 117 on placebo. The trial reported a difference in lying systolic pressure, with no lightheadedness score or confirmed refining grade.

cold-pressed safflower seed oil softgels and metabolic-syndrome blood pressure — The trial found greater reductions in measured systolic and diastolic pressure with cold-pressed safflower oil. It did not measure standing change or Parkinson orthostatic symptoms.
low — Powdered true cumin in rat feed shortened time to a marked stool. The result does not isolate gastric emptying and did not measure levodopa or Parkinson OFF time.

low — True cumin aqueous extract and a separate isolated cuminaldehyde intervention improved climbing in a toxin-exposed fly model. A separate cinnamon case accounts for a nearby OFF-time indexing result.

low — A Parkinson case used oral combination tablets containing confirmed Cuminum cyminum, plus Mucuna and other therapies. The OFF item remained 2 with a printed 50% to 25% change. Daily diary or hours, a ground preparation, ingredient dose and a comparator were absent, and the tablet was omitted from the discharge list.

coarse true cumin within a digestive symptom mix — Constipation favored the mixture at week one (p=.049) and was inconclusive at week two (p=.152). The comparator also included active mix. This was dyspepsia, without a Parkinson cohort or motor diary.

cumin-containing multicomponent tablet in constipation — Mean constipation scale 5.03 to 1.73 versus 5.77 to 5.60 at day 15. Stool-frequency between-arm p=.08. Three publisher copies use the same group sizes and outcomes. No cumin-specific, levodopa or OFF comparison.

low — Aqueous oral cumin seed extract slowed small-intestinal charcoal progression in rats. The exposure and transit endpoint differ from the earlier ground-cumin diet and did not measure levodopa or Parkinson OFF time.

low — Pharmaceutical camicinal reduced patient motor-diary OFF time versus placebo. This defines the appropriate clinical endpoint and how it can differ from gastric emptying and levodopa pharmacokinetics. It involved no cumin exposure.
low — Reports self-reported cumin intake among 139 people with Parkinson's. The paper gives neither ground versus other forms nor a cumin-linked diary or item-level estimate of daily OFF time.

low — Cumin extract capsules shortened time to postoperative flatus and defecation. Participants were recovering from abdominal operations and the protocol did not measure levodopa kinetics, gastric emptying, or Parkinson OFF time.

cumin extract and isolated glycoside with an unrelated drug in rats — Aqueous seed extract enhanced rifampicin exposure. The 35% maximum concentration and 53% area increase refer to isolated glycoside. No ground cumin or levodopa comparison or daily OFF outcome.

potential confounder in the cumin-containing Parkinson case — Acute ON duration was 221 versus 177 minutes for one Mucuna arm versus levodopa plus benserazide (p<.001). Matched levodopa and benserazide comparisons favored pharmaceutical levodopa instead. Cumin was absent, and no usual daily OFF was measured.

cumin extract combined with glyburide in diabetic rats — The abstract reports differing glyburide pharmacokinetics across different doses with and without ethanolic extract. This gives no clinical levodopa or daily OFF estimate.

combined tablet and uncontrolled bowel outcome — In 30 adults with functional constipation, spontaneous bowel movement score increased from 1.20 at day seven to 2.20 at day 30. The tablet included common cumin and other ingredients; no placebo, Parkinson disease or daily OFF outcome.

registered canola-containing comparator with fatigue measures — The protocol names canola in the comparator arm and measures fatigability. No posted results enable a food or Parkinson fatigue estimate.

shared collection original source context — Bot's rapeseed/MCT capsule and the Jazayeri rapeseed/fluoxetine comparator are separate families. Their depression endpoints and unverified oil processing supply no frozen effect estimate.

shared collection original source context — Rapeseed oil is a component of the multi-food SYSDIET comparison; ALA source discussion is supplementary. It is not an isolated grade-specific contrast for the frozen symptom.

canola oil in the low-fat menu and fatigue by diet — The low-fat menu names canola oil without a grade. The ketogenic plan had a 0.50-point greater reduction on the fatigue item. The randomized comparison concerns two entire menus.

canola oil in a mixed MS diet and Modified Fatigue Impact Scale — NICE lists canola and olive oil within the diet and gives an unadjusted difference of -0.70 MFIS points (95% CI -5.34 to 3.94). Original abstract reports a favorable p=.001. The original adjustment and precise refining grade remain unresolved. No canola-specific or Parkinson estimate.

rapeseed carrier in all randomized fatigue trial groups — Twelve-week fatigue changes describe comparisons among ubiquinol formulations. The groups lack a known oil-free arm or verified refined canola.

canola-containing comparator and exploratory physical fatigability — Physical fatigability scale and leg-press repetitions were inconclusive versus ketone ester. No oil-free comparison, refining grade or Parkinson subgroup was identified.

General speech difficulty during oil or massage exposure in Parkinson disease — Table 15 scores of 2, 2, 2 and 0 remained fixed across phases. General speech difficulty does not isolate hypophonia or objectively measured loudness, and the route was inhaled or topical.
lemongrass beverage co-exposure and dysphonia during suspected allergy — Potato sensitization and recurrence were reported. The case leaves lemongrass attribution and acoustic loudness unresolved.

Oral leaf infusion and a nonvoice clinical outcome — The comparison measured oral candidiasis in HIV infection, using leaf infusion, lemon juice or gentian violet. It gave no acoustic voice intensity, minced plant material or Parkinson cohort.

bedtime dried parsley tea comparator and morning refreshment — Forty-one healthy adults took each tea over seven nights, with a one-week washout. Table 1 gives morning refreshment means of 3.37 after parsley and 3.49 after passionflower. The crossover used an active comparison and left daytime sleepiness unmeasured.
raw carrot as a jaw-motion test food — Participants bit and expelled raw carrot during a study of deep brain stimulation and jaw velocity.
soybean oil feed and locomotion in rats — Hydrogenated fat and lard reduced locomotion relative to soybean feed. No untreated Parkinson group or human walking-speed measure.

soybean oil comparator and open-field movement in unstressed rats — Unstressed adolescent rats showed no detected crossing or rearing differences by fat, while the restraint response varied by fat. Open-field exploration, perinatal exposure and the rat population limit walking-speed applicability.

soybean oil in a mixed diet with beam and open-field locomotion — Soybean oil was 10 g/kg in control feed and absent in the other formulas. Pole and open-field patterns went in different directions. No independent oil or human walking-slowness comparison.

soybean oil versus interesterified fat across rat development — Rat offspring receiving interesterified fat were less active in adulthood than offspring receiving soybean oil. Neither the developmental exposure nor locomotor activity isolates human Parkinson walking speed.

soybean oil assigned in a rotenone mouse diet — Rotenone soybean and perilla groups differed in motor proxies, including rearing at equal diet-fat percentage. Walking speed and the soybean oil lot grade were unverified.

soybean oil in high-fat feed and beam coordination in a multiple system atrophy mouse model — The high-fat blend contains lard and soybean oil and differs from standard chow. The reported comparison is between genotypes under high-fat feed, with no isolated soybean oil or walking-speed estimate.

soybean oil in an enteral formula given during advanced Parkinson care — The regulator identifies soybean oil in the combined formula. Oil grade and walking speed were unreported, with medication and formula changes during care.

rice bran oil as a placebo and aggregate clinical scores — The trial compares cannabis oil with rice bran oil. The aggregate scale result was inconclusive and no speech intelligibility item estimate or oil grade was published.
pooled poultry item and total Parkinson symptom score — Preference for chicken, turkey, or rabbit was inconclusive against total PRO-PD. There was no attention or preparation-specific analysis.

original source context with different preparation, outcome, attribution or population — The Parkinson imaging comparison distinguishes attention-related tests from MRI topology. No roasted-turkey intervention.
Parkinson reaction and cueing tasks during amino-acid depletion — Short-interval reaction outcomes improved while delayed recall worsened. Depletion of tryptophan did not test consuming turkey.

plasma alpha-linolenic acid and Parkinson speech items — Examiner-rated speech had age-adjusted ρ = .014 (p = .936) and sex-adjusted ρ = −.116 (p = .493). Daily-living speech also showed no clear association. The study did not isolate intelligibility or compare oil ingestion.

time-sampled oral processing of cooked black beans — The abstract gives differences in chewed particle size at 18 and 24 seconds. No clinical swallowing measure is established. Overlap with the earlier 17-person study is unresolved.

boiled beans tolerated after surgery and dysphagia rehabilitation in a Parkinson case — One stage IV Parkinson patient resumed boiled beans in a right side-lying position ten months after surgery for dysphagia from concurrent Wallenberg syndrome. Bean species and any causal food effect were unreported.

human cooked black-bean oral processing and swallow-readiness task — Participants expectorated the boluses. Chewing time and particle size provide relevant food-texture context without an observed swallow or Parkinson dysphagia contrast.

black kidney bean protein fibrils and dysphagia-oriented texture tests — Hydrogel textures reached IDDSI levels 4–5 in material testing. No human swallowing result or boiled whole bean exposure follows from the texture level.
multi-ingredient tonic and subjective weakness — The uncontrolled study reported weakness changes. Weakness, Parkinson fatigue and an ingredient-specific effect were not separately estimated.

separately numbered conference member with preparation or outcome limits — P-03.2-20 uses nutmeg essential oil and isolated molecules in rat hepatoma cells. Its endpoints are cell conductance and growth without grated nutmeg or fatigue measurement.

author abstract of the same nutmeg Cx43 assay family — Brief conductance inhibition and longer Cx43 expression changes concern rat hepatoma cells treated with essential oil or three isolated terpenes. The report does not measure the frozen culinary exposure or Parkinson symptom.
Matched cultural or experiential record for nutmeg and fatigue severity; preserves community/traditional context without controlled efficacy weight.

Parkinson sleep reports during broccoli tea with white mustard — Six of eight symptomatic volunteers reported less broadly defined sleep impairment. The uncontrolled preparation combines broccoli with ground white mustard powder. It does not compare toasted mustard or measure validated insomnia severity.

prepared mustard plus Tabasco and overnight polysomnography — Within-person sleep efficiency was 0.90 versus 0.94 after mustard plus Tabasco versus a plain meal. Sleep onset was longer numerically with p between .05 and .10. Mustard contribution and toasted seed were not isolated.

isolated eugenol plus levodopa in lesion-model mice — Levodopa-related abnormal behavior did not improve and striatal dopamine depletion increased. The study supplies no ground allspice clinical comparison.

isolated oral eugenol and levodopa in a lesion rat model — The author abstract reports improved behavioral outcomes from eugenol alone or in combination. It does not identify dyskinesia scores and does not compare ground allspice.

extra-virgin olive oil comparator with oxybutynin in overactive bladder — The registered outcome was daily void count. Both groups received oxybutynin and the trial stopped with 31 participants and no posted results. There is no separately estimated oil effect or Parkinson cohort.
lycopene-enriched oil and prostate symptom score — The composite that includes urgency showed no clear within-arm change, with no separate urgency frequency and no oil-only control.

multi-food dietary pattern and general urinary complaints in Parkinsonism — In 1205 participants the MIND score was inversely associated with general urinary symptom severity. The Mediterranean score was inconclusive. The outcome is broader than urgency frequency, and neither score isolates extra-virgin olive oil.

olive oil food-frequency item and urinary dysfunction in Parkinson — The cohort measured olive oil use and MDS-UPDRS urinary dysfunction. The adjusted urinary OR is for total Mediterranean diet adherence; oil grade, independent exposure and urgency frequency are unspecified.

conflicting placebo identity in the saw palmetto urinary trial — The paper describes olive oil as comparator in a study of IPSS and OABSS totals. The exact linked registration instead specifies polyethylene glycol-400. Actual oil exposure remains unresolved and no separate urgency or frequency result is given.
macadamia oil comparator beverage and negative-affect outcomes — The registered oil serves as a comparator and its pressing grade is unverified. The terminated record has no posted results.

oral macadamia oil comparator and mood in military officers — The elated/depressed POMS subscale did not differ clearly between macadamia oil and krill oil (group p = .2103). There was no oil-free arm or Parkinson cohort.

isolated eugenol and abnormal motor observation in a mouse model — The official associated project report describes abnormal hind-limb extension after levodopa. The tested constituent treatments did not suppress it. This is not timed gait or ground allspice. The journal body remains unavailable and exact sample identity is unverified.

oral isolated eugenol and rodent motor testing — The journal abstract reports selected motor observations. The institutional companion describes open-field exploration, rotarod and rotational outcomes. Its methods do not establish clinical walking speed or a ground-allspice effect.

isolated eugenol and schedule-dependent beam comparisons in mice — The original figure reports shorter crossings with the earlier schedule and longer crossings with the later schedule. The experiment describes a single model-only comparator and different observation times, limiting causal interpretation. It supplies no result for ground-allspice intake and clinical walking speed.

Parkinson diet plans include uncooked spinach-or-kale preparations and assess aggregate MDS-UPDRS measures — Individual spinach choice and quantity are unknown; speech-specific item changes and listener-rated intelligibility are not reported. Whole-diet and medication changes cannot isolate an effect of raw spinach.

pearl millet cultivar and reaction-time tasks in adolescents — Response times favored iron-biofortified millet over conventional millet. The tests do not directly assess manual dexterity or Parkinson symptoms.

randomized pearl millet cultivar feeding and accelerometer activity — Light physical activity favored the iron-biofortified cultivar by 22.3 minutes per day. Hand dexterity, Parkinson disease and millet versus no millet were not tested.
pearl millet substitution and handgrip strength — Grip strength favored millet substitution in athletes. The test did not assess manual dexterity or a Parkinson subgroup.
black mustard seed extract in drug-exposed rats; activity and catalepsy — Extract and animal motor tasks do not measure fall frequency after ground mustard in humans with Parkinson disease.

PD self-selected broccoli and white mustard tea; balance observation; no fall count — Single participant balance rating and mixed uncontrolled exposure cannot establish effect of ground mustard seed on fall frequency; participant overlap across reports is unresolved.

seven inhaled oils including rosemary and laboratory gait measures — The patent gives rotarod and CatWalk results for a blend. The rosemary contribution, ground preparation and clinical gait speed remain unresolved.
injected rosemary extract and activity in a rotenone mouse model — Higher activity, rearing and bar performance in the highest group. Ground rosemary intake and walking velocity were unmeasured.

aqueous and hydroalcoholic rosemary leaf extract in antioxidant assays — Rosemary extract IC50 values differed by assay and extraction conditions. These are chemical endpoints without culinary oral administration, depression or gait observations.
isolated rosmarinic acid and Parkinson-model pole and open-field measures — Pole descent and open-field motor outcomes favored one or more pre-exposure groups. No ground rosemary or clinical gait.
isolated rosmarinic acid and a hyperlocomotor MPTP model — Rosmarinic acid reduced the abnormal increase in open-field movement. The model showed no clear deficit in pole or rotarod measures.

corn oil as the active comparison in a Parkinson depression trial — The paper reports UPDRS change at total scale level for the corn-oil and DHA groups, without a separate drooling rating, verified refinement or oil-free comparator.

oral corn oil comparator and unstimulated salivary flow — The six-month Sjögren trial reports no clear change in unstimulated whole sialometry or group difference in dryness. The study evaluates autoimmune hyposalivation and does not measure Parkinson drooling or report oil grade.
shared oral Parkinson trial carrier and UPDRS part II total — The treatment table provides an overall part II score. Salivation item changes are unavailable and all arms used corn oil.

topical oxidized corn oil derivative and dry-mouth symptoms — The randomized 24-person crossover used a topical active comparator derived from oxidized corn oil. Baseline hyposalivation and treatment-period symptom ratings do not estimate dietary corn oil or Parkinson drooling.

oral dietary corn oil and rat salivary flow — Corn oil was the base diet. After 30 days, cannulated submandibular flow was lower in the retained corn arm than in the chia replacement arm. The experiment measures secretion in healthy rats and does not measure clinical drooling.

curry leaf extract and motor tasks in rotenone mice — The publisher figure shows shorter beam and pole times and a partial increase in open-field distance after leaf extract. These tests do not measure clinical freezing episodes after cooked curry leaf.

isolated isolongifolene and toxin-model rat behavior — A separate isolated-compound study assessed open-field and rotarod performance. Neither cooked leaf nor clinical freezing episodes were measured.
curry leaf extract and fly climbing or jumping — Climbing and jumping favored an extract arm in the fly toxin model. The test does not measure human freezing events or cooked leaf.

intralaryngeal almond oil carrier and hoarseness — A laryngeal case reports hoarseness resolving after a course including menthol in almond oil and surgery; no oral exposure, cold pressing, Parkinson diagnosis or measured vocal intensity.

Rat leaf extract with contradictory charcoal transit direction — The authors interpret slower propulsion, while the extracted table shows larger charcoal travel after both extract treatments than the labeled control. The study supplies no separate gastric or Parkinson outcome.

Human mixed decoction and irritable bowel symptoms — The completed trial used three botanical ingredients and found an inconclusive bowel severity contrast. The registration and article did not measure OFF time or levodopa.

Diabetic rat intestinal transit and colon assay — Leaf extract was reported to improve small-intestinal charcoal transit and distal colon cholinergic response. The reported measures do not establish gastric emptying or OFF time.

Clinical iron tablet with levodopa drug exposure — Levodopa and carbidopa AUC fell, and the mean clinical response was inconclusive. The experiment does not contain ground curry leaf or daily OFF time.

Hydroalcoholic leaf extract and rat transit — The authors report slower transit after a castor-oil challenge in rats. Methods call the extracted powder bark in one sentence and describe leaves elsewhere. The study measured neither levodopa uptake nor Parkinson OFF time.

Measured iron in a ground curry leaf food formulation — The report gives compositional iron in finished idli, with no medication exposure or OFF measure. Food matrix and pharmaceutical iron are distinct exposures.

Ferrous-sulfate-fortified curry-leaf product in laboratory study — The formulation adds ferrous sulfate and reports in vitro iron handling. It does not test ordinary ground curry leaf use with levodopa or measure daily OFF time.

Overlapping mouse charcoal transit experiments — Five arm means and SDs match across the original reports. The full series adds distinct verapamil and atropine comparisons without gastric emptying, levodopa or OFF time.

oat bran in a multi-ingredient meal and mobility measures — The protocol includes balance and chair stands, and excluded diagnosed neurodegenerative disease. It supplies no Parkinson falls outcome for rolled oats.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S7.478 orally administers oat-stem lignin to irradiated mice and S6.415 studies oat seed germination. Neither is a prepared oat-grain or Parkinson motor comparison.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — P-14-021 studies oat globulin hydrolysates and P-15-007 applies isolated oat phenolics to keratinocytes. Oat-beverage fermentation is another member. OATS also names a semen phenotype.
shared collection original source context — The SYSDIET bundle includes whole grains including oats, and P422 measures dietary fiber in rolled oats. No isolated Parkinson fall result.

fortified oatmeal within a randomized nutrition package and falls — First-fall HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.19–0.86) for the program versus usual care. Oatmeal was part of a bundle with supplements, calcium-vitamin D and diet counseling. No isolated rolled-oat or Parkinson estimate.
cayenne frequency and combined anxiety and depression scores — The cohort gives a cayenne frequency item and no adjusted anxiety-specific result. Preparation is unspecified.

oral related pepper extract and DASS anxiety in students — The anxiety table has inconsistent visit totals and no valid between-arm change estimate. Distinct Capsicum pubescens extract, not ground cayenne or Parkinson.
oral cinnamon capsules and blood pressure in type 2 diabetes — Blood pressure fell with capsules relative to placebo. Symptomatic lightheadedness on standing was unmeasured.

ground cinnamon capsule and repeated post-meal supine blood pressure — Nine participants had inconclusive systolic and diastolic pressure contrasts. The protocol used supine measurements and supplied no orthostatic or Parkinson outcome.
dried cinnamon powder capsules and ambulatory blood pressure in hypertension — Day-90 24-hour pressure comparisons were inconclusive. No standing challenge or Parkinson symptom score.

cinnamon use and cardiovascular nonmotor domain in a Parkinson survey — The corrected exploratory comparisons found no clear clinical differences. Cinnamon-specific coefficients and the lightheadedness item are not reported.
ground cassia beverage and acute blood pressure in middle-aged adults — Reported pressure contrasts were inconclusive across the post-beverage times. No standing lightheadedness result was measured.

black soybean seed coat extract and drowsiness during a task — Contemporaneous author summary and likely same-study patent report lower task-day VAS at two time points in healthy adults. The baseline change comparison is inconclusive. Journal full text and trial identity remain open. Exposure is Glycine max extract.

randomized whole diet and daytime dysfunction in diabetes — Adjusted PSQI daytime dysfunction difference −0.41 (95% CI −1.00 to 0.18, p=.163). The diet analysis pools bean intake and measures neither black bean preparation nor Parkinson daytime sleepiness.

verified boiled black common bean meals in healthy adults — Registered crossover, dissertation and journal report describe one trial with vascular and metabolic measures. Sleepiness was outside the reported endpoints.

Parkinson diet scores and daytime sleepiness with pooled bean intake — Table 2 reports lower self-rated sleepiness per point of MIND score (−1.91), with a similar association for the Mediterranean diet. Supplemental Table S4 analyzes the pooled bean category against total symptom burden. The survey does not estimate black bean intake, preparation, or change in daytime sleepiness.

three arm soybean extract comparison and sleepiness on waking — The earliest verified patent source reports no statistically significant between-arm sleep factor differences, with 65 evaluable. It uses Glycine max extract and a waking-time measure in healthy adults. The different 2025 study design cannot establish participant independence.

black soybean seed coat extract and sleepiness on rising — In 64 healthy adults randomized to extract or placebo, immediate-on-waking OSA-MA scores favored extract at weeks eight and twelve. Extract species, population and outcome differ from the frozen claim.

topical piperine rinse and composite of pronunciation difficulty and worsened taste — Uncontrolled burning-mouth series reported a two-item composite improvement from 1.8 to 1.0. It did not measure intelligibility or isolate the pronunciation item. No PD cohort or ground-pepper exposure.
shiitake extract and cultured neuronal-cell outcomes — Viability and senescence changed after extract exposure. No dexterity was measurable in this design.

shiitake constituent in Parkinson models — Reported mouse behavioral improvement includes pole testing context. Isolated lentinan and mouse locomotion do not establish an effect of roasting on clinical hand dexterity.
coriander seed extract and drug-induced orofacial dyskinesia — The seed extract reduced induced excess orofacial movements in rats. Dried culinary leaf and reduced facial expression were not studied.

coriander in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome — The menu lists coriander without specifying the plant part and the motor examination includes facial expression. Dried cilantro exposure and facial expression item changes are unavailable.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S1.97 proposes parsley as a possible dietary source of related Rubisco peptides while modelling spinach-derived rubiscolin. No parsley isolate, dose or Parkinson outcome is measured.

Parkinson diet menu includes parsley and Table 4 reports medication — The report provides levodopa dose at follow-up and motor totals. It does not identify the parsley form, participant-specific parsley intake or hours in the OFF state.

low — An outbreak investigation identified atropine and scopolamine in boiled-spinach and pastry leftovers. Poisoning supplies a food safety context and no Parkinson visual hallucination frequency estimate.

low — Mandrake was detected among spinach and chard leaves. Hyperactivity or hallucination was reported jointly in acute poisoning. The source does not give a clean spinach exposure, visual modality, or Parkinson frequency.

spinach and okra intake history and oxalate nephropathy — More oxalate-rich vegetables were consumed before kidney injury in a post-bypass patient. No single-food comparator, spinach preparation, dyskinesia or visual hallucination endpoint was reported.

safflower oil comparator and Huntington bradykinesia scale component — The related motor examination includes body bradykinesia. Its separate outcome is unavailable, and the study population had Huntington disease.

original article and linked trial context — The original review describes dysphagia as a nutritional barrier in neurodegenerative disease. Its separate safflower-fed amyloid mouse comparison measured brain inflammatory gene expression and lipid mediators, with no swallowing or bradykinesia result.

safflower and spontaneous locomotion in developmental rats — Spontaneous locomotion did not differ. Novelty exploration was lower than on soybean oil or chow. Developmental fat composition and exploratory behavior differ materially from culinary oil and Parkinson's motor slowness.
safflower-derived flavonoids in a Parkinson rat model — A flavonoid extract differs from culinary seed oil. The correction is linked with the source. Its text remains to be inspected.

oral safflower oil comparator and episodic movements in Glut1 deficiency — The safflower period gave 11.8 disabling movement events per four weeks versus 14.3 in the drug period. These are episodic events in Glut1 deficiency. No bradykinesia or cold pressing was measured.

safflower and open-field movement in healthy adult rats — More exploratory movement appeared in the exercise-plus-water group. Safflower group means did not establish a general motor benefit. The study used healthy animals and did not measure Parkinsonian bradykinesia.
low — The human single-arm report applied commercial seed oil topically and measured aphthous lesions. It does not identify toasted oil or report salivary flow or drooling.

low — The rat experiment measured salivary-gland histology after oral ethanolic extract of pumpkin flesh. The investigators removed seeds and peel. Gland structure is not secretion or drooling, and no seed oil was administered.

low — Commercial oil administered orally reduced certain tongue tissue injury markers in rat paclitaxel groups. Pressing or roasting details were not verified and no saliva flow, drooling or Parkinson outcome was measured.

soy oil vehicle and mouse motor assays — Original Methods and Table 1 assign 50 mg/kg to curcumin. Soy oil was the vehicle in control groups. Refined grade and levodopa-induced dyskinesia were not measured.

food-related material in an imaging report — The original MR colonography study places excised pig colon specimens in soybean oil for imaging. This is a nonoral laboratory medium with no dose, grade or Parkinson symptom comparison.

review lineage for ground soybeans alongside levodopa and carbidopa — The public review groups outcomes under Glycine max and cites the ground-soybean crossover. It does not provide an independent refined soybean oil comparison or the study-level grade table.
soybean comparator and orofacial movements in rats — Hydrogenated fat increased orofacial dyskinesia relative to the soybean feed. This was neither a Parkinson model nor levodopa-induced dyskinesia.

long-duration diet comparison and rat orofacial movements — Older rats fed hydrogenated fat showed progressively greater orofacial movements in a study with soybean-oil and standard-chow groups. The oil grade and Parkinson treatment-related outcome were untested.
ground soybeans plus levodopa and dyskinesia — Seven participants with Parkinson had lower mAIMS during the acute ground-soybean condition. Refined soybean oil and chronic dyskinesia were untested.

distinct Prunus species and extract in cerebrovascular models — Two conference members describe Prunus cerasoides or prunetin and nonclinical outcomes. The model, species and forms differ from eating dried cherry and provide no apathy estimate.

separate Prunus species and oral extract or constituent in a mouse vascular model — The author abstract and publisher excerpts report behavioral and tissue outcomes after carotid stenosis. The species, preparation, model and outcomes differ from dried cherry and Parkinson apathy. Likely report-family overlap with 2025 Brain PET member 0634 precludes counting independent replication.

freeze-dried cherry powder in a formulated drink and self-rated mood — Some age groups reported improved mood or fitness items. The trial did not use an apathy scale and used a sweet cherry blend in healthy people.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S7.519 describes sweet cherry among fruit trees used for grafting work. No dietary cherry or measured neurologic symptom is present.

injected Prunus stem and leaf extract in a mouse focal stroke model — The complete paper separates injected extract before or after stroke from constituent cell experiments. Its short-term injury and sensorimotor outcomes leave Parkinson apathy open and do not transfer to consuming dried fruit.

sweet almond massage and depression in postmenopausal women — The reported depression score declined with almond-oil massage and stayed flat in the no-massage arm. The design did not isolate oil from massage and the BDI scale transformation is unclear.

oral and injected almond oil in rat forced-swim behavior — Oral oil increased climbing without a clear difference in immobility or swimming. The high injected dose reduced immobility. The study did not test cold-pressed oil or clinical depression.

measured comparison or exposure context with a different preparation, outcome or population — Almond oil forms an inhaled control and a vehicle for clary sage in an aromatherapy comparison. The outcomes are vital signs and salivary cortisol, with no ingested cold-pressed almond oil or Parkinson depression measure.

unfragranced almond carrier and HADS depression during radiotherapy — Randomized aromatherapy arms gave no clear depression difference. Carrier grade comes from secondary study description. No isolated oral oil contrast.

acute swallowing difficulty after mixed seasoned meals — A mixed sauce included cumin and the case describes acute oral symptoms. Toasting, ingredient-specific causation and clinical Parkinson dysphagia remain unverified.
healthy human salivary effect of three mixed cumin-ginger sprays — The study concerns spray formulation, salivation and safety. It supplies no swallowing test or isolated toasted-cumin exposure.

Parkinson survey recording cumin use with aggregate nonmotor measures — Cumin intake was recorded and exploratory nonmotor comparisons were inconclusive after correction. No preparation or cumin-specific dysphagia estimate is reported.

clinical salivary and dry-mouth response to a cumin and ginger spray — The crossover favored a mixed mouth spray for salivary flow. It did not compare oral toasted spice ingestion or assess a clinical swallowing endpoint.
case of acute allergy after fried mixed food containing ground cumin — The report records acute anaphylaxis and sensitization to cumin. It supplies no toasted-seed or Parkinson swallowing assessment.

repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking — Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.

rocket salad beverage and blood pressure in healthy adults — The post-beverage systolic pressure declined at 150 minutes. The beverage, posture, population, and endpoint leave fall frequency after raw leaves unmeasured.

vegetable-group intake and injurious falls in older adults — Two analyses of one cohort relate vegetable diversity or vegetable-group intake to hospitalizations after falls. Salad greens are pooled and arugula is unnamed. No Parkinson subgroup or fall-frequency estimate was reported.
rucola on an aggregate Parkinson diet menu — The article measures a global motor outcome without an arugula or fall-frequency contrast.

fresh arugula in a nitrate-rich vegetable crossover — Thirty healthy adults. Post-lunch pressure changed during both active dietary periods. No isolated arugula, standing pressure or fall frequency result.

chives on a Parkinson pilot diet menu and composite motor score — The Appendix A menu names chives. Both diet arms had lower UPDRS III scores over time without a chives-only contrast, a separately reported walking-speed outcome or a specified chive preparation.

oral dried dill aerial-part and black rice extract, open-field movement after stroke — Total crossings, rearing, grooming and licking showed no clear change. The potentially overlapping PMID31827714 reports lower composite stroke scores at all doses without component estimates. Neither used fresh dill or measured bradykinesia.

oral dill and black rice extract and aggregate stroke neurological score in adults — At one week high dose changed total NIHSS −87.50% vs −36.03% on placebo (p=.045). Later comparisons and the low dose were inconclusive. No isolated dill, motor subscore, fresh leaf or Parkinson comparison.

maternal oral dill extract and developmental motor reflexes in offspring — The abstract describes better developmental righting, rotation and cliff avoidance following maternal extract exposure. These motor reflexes provide no Parkinson bradykinesia or fresh-leaf comparison.

oral sowa extract and rotarod motor performance during withdrawal — The two extract arms had longer retention than withdrawal alone. This motor coordination task supplies no fresh leaf or clinical bradykinesia estimate.

safflower oil mixed-meal crossover with peripheral biomarkers — Healthy participants received meals containing safflower oil, cocoa butter or no added fat. The abstract does not give an isolated contrast for the safflower arm, specify pressing method or measure the frozen Parkinson symptom.

safflower oil and a Huntington psychiatric measure with an apathy item — Investigators report no clear comparative PBA-s change without numerical results or the apathy item. Its direction is unresolved.

developmental safflower exposure and novelty exploration — Lower exploration favored a motivational proxy in one condition, while spontaneous locomotion was unchanged. The model measured neither Parkinson nor clinical apathy.

isolated safflower pigment and depression-like measures in a Parkinson mouse model — Higher sucrose intake and lower immobility after the purified pigment are an opposite-direction clue at the level of depression-related measures. Neither the tested exposure nor endpoint is the frozen claim.

holy basil mixture and planned clinical falls outside Parkinson disease — The official registry explicitly excludes parkinsonism. It compares a mixed holy-basil product with standard care and has no posted fall results.

separately numbered conference member with preparation or outcome limits — P-05.2-64 tests swelling and surface structure of an alginate complex made from basil seed mucilage. It has no dried basil leaf ingestion or falls outcome.

oral sweet basil essential oil and induced rotarod falls in mice — The highest oral oil group fell more times and sooner on a rotarod than vehicle (p<.05), while the intermediate group showed no clear deficit. The study used oil distilled from dried leaves in mice without Parkinsonian induction. No culinary leaf or clinical fall frequency was tested.
sardines among options and anxiety score — Advice to eat fatty fish yielded a higher anxiety point estimate with an interval crossing zero. Sardines were one option in an angina cohort.

marine omega-3 capsule and Beck anxiety outside Parkinson disease — Table 5 log Beck difference −0.23 (95% CI −0.44 to −0.011). Commercial EPA-predominant blend, unknown fish species and no baked sardine comparison.
sardine oil and postpartum mood — The sardine-oil versus perilla-oil postpartum depression threshold comparison was inconclusive. No standalone anxiety endpoint or baked sardine exposure.

oily fish category and Parkinson anxiety instrument — The Parkinson clinical dataset contains a pooled oily-fish item that includes sardines and a HADS anxiety total. The publication has no sardine-specific estimate.

Parkinson baseline oatmeal frequency and dyskinesia — The oatmeal tile is extremely close to zero on the inverse side. The separate cooked-oats field is not shown in the graph. No numeric coefficient or uncertainty is reported.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S7.478 orally administers oat-stem lignin to irradiated mice and S6.415 studies oat seed germination. Neither is a prepared oat-grain or Parkinson motor comparison.

measured comparison or exposure context with a different preparation, outcome or population — Cooked Vicia faba increased plasma levodopa and produced severe dyskinesia in three susceptible Parkinson participants, with a separate motor score. The trial compared a different food and does not measure cooked oats.
oatmeal in Parkinson baseline food-frequency survey — The adjusted aggregate symptom estimate crossed zero. Dyskinesia severity and oatmeal preparation were not modeled separately.
oat-derived compound in cultured cells — Cellular oxidative-stress protection does not measure dyskinesia or cooked oats.

boiled soy tempeh and human walking distance — The tuberculosis trial found a larger change in six-minute walking distance with boiled tempeh and an inconclusive endpoint contrast. Neither stride length nor Parkinson was measured.

fermented velvet bean extract and rat forestride — The abstract reports inconclusive forestride changes and no clear separation of the paraquat model from controls. It used extracts of fermented Mucuna pruriens rather than cooked soy tempeh.
sage extract and mouse recognition or acute behavior — Vocalization and irritability at high extract doses do not measure reduced facial expressiveness.

low-fat mixed diet includes nutmeg in a baked recipe; aggregate motor exam — The apple crisp contains nutmeg of unspecified texture; intake is not individually verified. Composite speech and total motor scores do not establish listener-rated intelligibility or an isolated spice effect.
isolated piperine plus levodopa and rat pharmacokinetics — Adding piperine increased levodopa exposure in lesioned rats. The experiment did not measure daily off time or cracked black pepper.

optionally cranberry-flavored prebiotic bar in a Parkinson protocol — The cranberry flavor is an option and individual exposure and cooking are unspecified. No facial-expression motor item is identified in the posted outcomes or results.

cranberry concentrate and animal motor and tissue outcomes — The four-arm experiment used concentrated juice and measured postural stepping and midbrain histology. The study did not measure facial expressiveness.

dried basil tea and uncontrolled nocturia reports — Seven people reported fewer nocturnal voids after tea in an uncontrolled self-posted report, including the author. No fresh leaf or Parkinson urinary urgency outcome was measured.

purple leaf extract and bladder contraction — Extract made from dried purple basil leaves reduced electrically stimulated isolated mouse bladder contractions in Figure 2. No participant consumed basil and urinary urgency was unmeasured.

oral sweet basil extract and urogenital symptom composite — The menopausal trial's urogenital composite, which includes urinary symptoms, showed no clear between-group difference at one month (p=.114). It gave no urgency-specific result or evidence in Parkinson’s.

Fear of falling item in Parkinson disease during nonoral oil exposure — Fear of falling in public remained 1, 0, 0 and 0 in the four participants across conditions. The source gives no observed or diary-confirmed falls frequency.

Seated blood pressure following tea, with no falls measure — Blood pressure measurements were made seated in normotensive adults with an uncontrolled baseline comparator. The formulation was brewed leaf tea and no incident falls were counted.

Fall-risk assessment context in an older adult with mobility impairment — The BBS improved under a mixed warm compress and balance exercise. The study did not prospectively count falls or verify Parkinson disease or ingestion.

spearmint ethanolic leaf extract and urine production in rats — Five-hour urine output was higher in the extract arms. No urgency or void-by-void diary was assessed, and the unit may be pooled cage output.
aqueous spearmint leaf preparation and rat urine volume — The project reports increased short-term urine volume at one extract concentration. It did not measure urinary urgency or Parkinson’s.

isolated caraway constituent inhalation and subjective alertness — In healthy adults, (+)-carvone inhalation had no significant alertness, calmness or mood difference across study trials. The short-term odor exposure did not measure apathy or intake of toasted caraway.

oral caraway fruit fraction and behavioral activity — The oral polyphenol fraction increased open-field crossings and reduced immobility under forced tasks in healthy mice. Motivation and apathy remained unmeasured, and no toasted preparation was administered.

inhaled caraway essential oil and fasted mouse food intake — Food intake rose at two tested concentrations. The preparation was an inhaled, hydrodistilled essential oil, and the outcome was a specific feeding response rather than an apathy or effort scale.
allergic oral swelling after food exposure — The case report documents acute allergy after pepper-containing food. It contains no assessment of Parkinson’s hypophonia.
topical commercial pepper and perceived lip vibration — Participants sensed tingling near the equivalent of 50 Hz following local lip exposure. Speech loudness was outside the experiment.
Sichuan pepper oil and subjective oral symptoms — Single-arm mixed-oil capsule study reported improved subjective difficulty conversing and swallowing saliva. Acoustic voice volume was not measured.

cod processing-derived protein and metabolic effects — Presscake results concern NEFA and metabolic markers. The processed supplement and study population do not supply an isolated grilled-cod fatigue effect.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The pneumonia entry describes lipid aspiration after cod-liver oil in cats. The parasite entries also describe risk from eating infected raw fish. These are distinct veterinary and food-hazard contexts.
cod meal and dietary protein comparator — The actual cod-versus-beef meals and mixed dietary allocation addressed fasting and postmeal lipids. No dose-matched grilled cod or fatigue outcome.

shared collection original source context — PO2.144 compares lean-seafood and nonseafood diets and uses cod and lean beef test meals for lipid outcomes. Fish cooking grade and Parkinson fatigue are not established.

shared collection original source context — P126 gives the registered cod and lean-beef test meals, and P482 gives cod processing byproduct tablets. Other reports measure liver oil or intake. No grilled cod and Parkinson fatigue comparison.

fatigue scale and cod pooled in a seafood survey — The reported fatigue contrast applies to a high-mercury category excluding isolated cod. No grilled cod, Parkinson subgroup, or cod-specific fatigue response.

cod fillet hydrolysate and exercise exhaustion — Fourteen cyclists had no clear time-to-exhaustion difference. The drink contained cod fillet hydrolysate and the endpoint was exercise performance rather than Parkinson fatigue severity.

Parkinson dietary recalls and fatigue measurement — The Parkinson study measured fatigue and reported higher overall fat intake among participants with fatigue. No separate cod estimate or preparation was published.

diet patterns and probable REM sleep behavior disorder before Parkinson diagnosis — The study used a probable RBD questionnaire and pattern scores. It gives no raw-carrot contrast or dream-enactment frequency in diagnosed Parkinson's.

overall diet quality and questionnaire-defined probable REM behavior — Chinese cross-sectional sample free of diagnosed Parkinson disease. Overall diet-score contrasts and probable REM behavior screens do not estimate raw carrot intake or dream-enactment frequency.

ultraprocessed food exposure and later probable REM behavior screening — Original Figure 2 separates questionnaire-defined probable REM behavior. The exposure is overall ultraprocessed food and the cohorts overlap earlier diet work. Raw carrot and clinical dream enactment frequency are unresolved.
raw carrot identified in Parkinson case-control questionnaire — Raw carrot contributes to the salad factor. The case-control endpoint does not measure dream enactment.
injected celery leaf fractions and ketamine-induced sleep — Several fractions prolonged anesthetic sleep. REM dream enactment and Parkinson’s were unmeasured.

chervil in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome — The menu lists chervil and the motor examination includes gait and bradykinesia. Plant preparation, isolated chervil exposure and walking speed are unavailable.
inhaled lemon balm oil and self-reported dry mouth during dialysis — Dry mouth was less frequently reported after aromatherapy. Salivary flow, drooling and fresh leaf intake were unmeasured.
registered eugenol odor exposure and Epworth outcome — Daytime sleepiness is specified, but the exposure is part of smell training rather than culinary ingestion, with no posted result.
mixed snack contains cloves and registers sleep quality — The recipe lists cloves among several ingredients and leaves ground status and daytime sleepiness unresolved. No posted results.

concentrated clove oil and acute poisoning drowsiness — A child was initially drowsy and progressed to coma after accidental concentrated oil ingestion. Acute poisoning and daytime sleepiness after culinary clove differ in exposure, population and outcome.

green kiwi juice and spontaneous activity in mice — Oral A. deliciosa juice reduced movement counts in ordinary mice. Sedation and spontaneous activity differ from freezing episodes in Parkinson disease.

hardy kiwi juice and preclinical motor tests — The investigator follow-up reports improved motor tests after previously frozen hardy kiwi juice in MPTP mice. It gives group sizes and a p < .01 motor comparison, without a freezing outcome.

optional bell pepper in a whole diet and planned Epworth outcome — Torres San Miguel and colleagues planned a whole-diet comparison for adults with obstructive sleep apnea. The Mediterranean adaptation lists bell pepper as an optional vegetable and includes an Epworth Sleepiness Scale. The body identifies NCT06782737 and matches its official ethics code and study team. The abstract prints NCT06278571, a different mobile-app study in type 2 diabetes. The official apnea reco...

repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking — Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.

purified nonpungent Capsicum and acute sleepy and alert ratings — The crossover in 13 healthy men measured sleepy, alert and tired after single extract doses. Overall adverse-event comparison was p=.09, with item-specific estimates unavailable. Extract, preparation and population differ.

repeated symptom checklist during a 28-day dihydrocapsiate trial — A 78-participant trial collected symptom reports at repeated laboratory and interim visits. It reports dry mouth and leg cramps between-group differences, without separate sleepy, alert or tired estimates.

whole sweet pepper in two Parkinson diet menus and specific daytime sleepiness item — Both arms included capsicum in cooked recipes, and the daytime sleepiness item decreased 0.45 points more with the ketogenic diet. A separately grilled pepper exposure and an independent pepper effect were unavailable.

daytime sleepiness measured within a Parkinsonism symptom scale and grouped vegetable frequency — The daytime sleepiness item contributed to the overall symptom scale. The study relates grouped vegetable questions to total symptom burden and supplies no separate pepper exposure or daytime sleepiness coefficient.
reduced responsiveness after concentrated infant infusions — Cases describe hyporeactivity or lethargy after infusions. These are acute events in infants, with no REM diagnosis or sleep recording.
rodent sedation after essential-oil exposure — Sedation accompanied motor impairment during seizure research. REM sleep and dream enactment were outside the test.

oral crude peanut oil and acute upper-airway symptoms — Among 60 people with verified peanut allergy, crude oil elicited six reactions including one each of throat itch and wheeze. Oil processing was not established as cold pressing and speech intelligibility was unmeasured.

labial oil challenge and pooled hoarseness in children — Three oil tests were positive. Hoarseness was a pooled all-food adverse reaction without an oil-specific tally. Oil processing, acoustic outcome and Parkinson cohort were absent.

oral peanut oil challenge and individual upper-airway allergy signs — Fourteen of 62 oil challenges were positive. Table 2 describes adverse allergic signs without intelligibility measurement, Parkinson diagnosis or explicit cold pressing.
