acute hoarseness after oral kernel with prior topical macadamia oil — A child who chewed and spat out a macadamia kernel became too hoarse to speak. Macadamia oil exposure was cutaneous. No oil consumption, measured vocal loudness or Parkinson hypophonia was reported.

historically contaminated seafood and examiner-rated dysarthria — The 2023 reanalysis uses the same 197 government survey exposed participants and a selected group of 130 controls. It reports dysarthria in 24.9% versus 1.6%. Species, preparation and clinical Parkinson speech outcomes were unmeasured.

contaminated preserved sardines and dysarthria — Four of eight ICU patients had dysarthria in a botulism outbreak linked to contaminated home-preserved sardines. No grilled exposure, Parkinson subgroup or speech-intelligibility score.

fresh coriander leaf in mouse dietary memory tests — Fresh leaves were fed to mice and memory scores improved in aging and induced amnesia models. This study does not estimate attention impairment after dried leaf in people with Parkinson disease.

coriander fruit extract and passive avoidance in mice — The mouse study included passive avoidance. The task measured learned avoidance, and the extract used fruit. A dried-leaf effect on clinical attention remains open.

soybean oil capsules and measured affect or impulsivity — The 272-person trial found inconclusive group-by-time affect and impulsivity comparisons. The endpoints do not estimate apathy severity, and the population did not have Parkinson disease.

whole-blood fatty acids and separate Parkinson motivation items — DHA and the omega ratio showed nominal item associations that attenuated with cognitive adjustment. The biomarker models have no identifiable soybean oil exposure, and the report is a preprint.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — P1018 describes intravenous soybean oil in propofol or Intralipid and P1121 compares intragastric soy milk with cow milk. These are distinct preparations and neither tests culinary soybean oil in Parkinson disease.

corn or soy oil placebo and total NPI in Alzheimer disease — The total NPI contrast had p=.11. Placebo oil was pooled, and the same-cohort item reanalysis measures aggression. There is no separate apathy or Parkinson result.

soybean-oil capsule placebo and total NPI in Alzheimer disease — The vitamin E placebo used soybean oil. Later analysis of the same cohort reports distinct baseline apathy outcomes. Public arm comparisons give total NPI only. Processing grade and a Parkinson-specific outcome are unavailable.

Parkinson apathy item and a diet instrument capable of coding soya oil — The item 1.5 analysis used three whole-diet indices and all adjusted overall sample p values exceeded .05. The FETA instrument has a named soya oil code, without preparation grade or any published oil-specific estimate.

oral soybean oil emulsion preload and reward-directed lever presses in mice — The counterbalanced prefeeding comparison gave a main effect (p<.001) for milk reward devaluation. The food-directed behavioral task, formulation and mouse population do not approximate the full clinical claim.

personalized plant-rich program and Starkstein Apathy Scale in Parkinson disease — Reported time-by-group analysis favors the dietary program while post-treatment arm comparisons conflict. Apathy is absent from the public registry outcome list. No soybean oil assignment, intake or preparation was reported.

Parkinson survey recording cumin use with aggregate nonmotor measures — Cumin intake was recorded and exploratory nonmotor comparisons were inconclusive after correction. No preparation or cumin-specific apathy estimate is reported.

animal vehicle or flavored-milk preference outside the frozen preparation — PT080 and another member report injected corn oil as vehicle or control in a perimenopause model. The oil route, associated interventions and measures differ from oral corn oil.

corn oil comparator and aggregate symptom scores in a Parkinson trial — The accessible author abstract reports inconclusive treatment-group differences in total UPDRS and Hoehn and Yahr changes. Individual rigidity outcomes, oil processing and primary numerical tables remain unverified.

sequential enteral formulas and aggregate motor outcomes — The single-patient comparison reports motor observations and total UPDRS changes with different feeding products. Neither the formula table nor the observed outcomes establish corn-oil exposure grade or a separate rigidity estimate.

separately numbered conference member with preparation or outcome limits — P-07.1-14 gives corn oil to the control in a malathion rat study. Its liver outcomes and pesticide comparison do not isolate refined oil or assess clinical rigidity.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — Corn oil is used in rat lipid comparisons, feeding paradigms and a toxicant vehicle. No Parkinson clinical endpoint was measured.

shared corn oil and aggregate Parkinson motor change in a CBD trial — Table 2 Part III changes were 2.17, 3.85 and 3.00 in the corn-oil placebo and two CBD arms (p=.675). The trial gives no rigidity item or oil-free group.

corn oil as high-fat diet control and partial marine-lipid substitution — Corn oil was one base formulation, with and without different marine PUFA fractions. Adiposity and lipids were measured. The possibly overlapping article concerns the same broad research and a refined corn oil symptom effect is unresolved.

shared collection original source context — P233 is appended in the complete PMC HTML for this oral-key record and separately printed in the poster supplement. It compares corn and fish oil during shared exercise for strength and mechanistic outcomes. One study family.

shared collection original source context — Printed P233 reports an omega-3 versus corn-oil comparator during shared resistance training. Its strength findings are distinct from the frozen clinical outcomes. The other PMC key reproduces this member.

corn-oil control during exercise training — The final isometric interaction is p=.015 and the corn arm changed −1.4%. P233 uses −0.3%. Body strength during shared training does not measure any frozen Parkinson endpoint in these claims.

corn oil in historical tube-feed formulas and case rigidity — Rigidity improved after feed formulation, timing, protein and levodopa timing changed. The 2006 guide lists corn oil in both Nutren variants, with exact patient batches and refining unverified. The case cannot isolate corn oil.

separate gastrointestinal conference member and ingredient context — A tumor experiment incorporates corn oil in control or combined diets involving EPA and aspirin. The study does not assign the frozen preparation and clinical endpoint.
pharmaceutical compound and composite cognition — Celery historically relates to the compound. Trial formulation and cognitive scale do not isolate the frozen preparation and outcome.
pharmaceutical compound and composite cognition — The placebo-controlled comparison favored butylphthalide on global cognition. Full report and executive function estimate remain unavailable.

oral celery extract and spatial and non-spatial memory in healthy mice — The study reports improved memory tasks. It did not measure executive function in Parkinson’s or administer dried celery leaves as food.
pharmaceutical combination and a mixed cognitive subscore — A four-drug regimen reported a visuospatial and executive MoCA subscore. The comparison did not isolate dried celery leaf or the compound.
pharmaceutical compound and composite cognition — Retrospective comparison favored the compound for global cognition. The study did not isolate an executive-function effect.
pharmaceutical compound and composite cognition — Retrospective comparison found higher MoCA and lower composite motor scores with the pharmaceutical adjunct.
pharmaceutical comparison and overall cognition — Table 1 reports MoCA and MMSE totals without an executive-function domain. The exposure is a pharmaceutical.

pharmaceutical adjunct and visuospatial executive domain — The 30-person trial abstract describes a favorable MoCA domain result. It gives no scores or unambiguous comparison and does not test dried celery leaf.

fermented red cabbage with beetroot and caraway in healthy adults — The preprint reports general adverse symptom capture and no standing endpoint or symptom counts. No individual ingredient or Parkinson estimate.

mixed vegetable diets with assigned red-cabbage amounts — The higher and lower diets provide 800 and 152 g per week of red cabbage with four additional vegetables. The report gives no pressure or standing symptom result.

mixed red-cabbage and root vegetable diets in type 2 diabetes — The bitter/strong arm had lower 24-hour diastolic change than control, while the systolic comparison was inconclusive. Eating preparation and amount of red cabbage were unspecified, and no standing symptom was measured.

fermented or pickled cabbage and cucumber with six-week clinic pressure — The between-arm week-six systolic comparison was inconclusive and registry versus paper food-arm denominators differ. Cabbage cultivar and standing symptoms remain unreported.
cooked mixed cruciferous soup and 24-hour pressure — Systolic pressure was lower than after the control soup. Cabbage type was unspecified and no standing lightheadedness measure was included.
red cabbage microgreens and resting pressure in adults — Brachial and central pressures were unchanged. The study did not assess standing symptoms, mature red cabbage or Parkinson.

registered fermented versus unfermented red cabbage in allergic rhinitis — The planned safety assessments may provide a general adverse-event follow-up. No prespecified standing procedure, symptom comparison or observed results are available.
filtered marjoram tea and motor examination in Parkinson — Only an aggregate motor estimate is accessible. No isolated speech item, acoustic loudness or fresh leaf exposure.

Rubus ulmifolius extract confection and self-reported menstrual-cramp severity — 20 volunteers, no concurrent control or blinding. The authors report 75% perceived benefit. The exact extract content is unspecified and the formulation descriptions and figure denominators are inconsistent. No PD or frozen fruit.

frozen blackberry drink and exercise recovery biomarkers — 14 athletes received 200 g frozen fruit in water or red-colored water. No significant between-arm CK differences. The paper did not measure reported pain and identifies only the Rubus genus.

freeze-dried blackberry purée milk and quantified post-exercise muscle soreness — The exercise challenge trial favored freeze-dried blackberry in milk on immediate perceived soreness. There was no pre-exercise soreness baseline, calories and carbohydrate differed, treatment-by-time p=.914 and separate 24–72h comparisons were inconclusive. Registry and thesis are one non-Parkinson study.

Morus nigra (black mulberry, mislabeled blackberry) juice in MPTP levodopa-induced dyskinesia mice — Botanical identity check: title calls the fruit blackberry, but methods explicitly specify Morus nigra (black mulberry, Moraceae), not Rubus blackberry (Rosaceae), and the outcome is mouse AIMS dyskinesia rather than pain.

Parkinson pain odds and overall Mediterranean diet adherence — OR 0.86 (95% CI 0.75–0.98) for higher pattern adherence and pain presence. No separate blackberry intake or preparation contrast and no estimate on severity after frozen berries.
grapeseed as a shared massage carrier and psychiatric symptom scores — Both groups received grapeseed massage. Difference concerns added scents. Original body and refining grade unverified.

topical grapeseed oil mixture in Gua Sha and depression scores — Lower depression scores accompanied the bundled procedure. The trial did not test ingestion or determine the contribution or processing grade of the oil.
grape seed extract and clinical depression scores in migraine — Adjusted DASS depression p=.95. The extract is not the fixed oil and no participants were studied for Parkinson depression.

mixed Parkinson diet and composite motor score — Appendix A lists both herbs in a multicomponent diet. Composite UPDRS III scores improved. The examination includes speech, but no item-level result, individual herb amount or preparation, or herb-specific contrast was reported.

oral Parkinson trial corn vehicle and seated cardiovascular monitoring — The trial measured seated wrist blood pressure and found no significant contrast. Standing changes and symptoms were not measured as an endpoint.

self-reported cooking corn oil and seated blood pressure — Predominant corn-oil users had lower seated pressure than people mainly using animal fats. Self-reported exposure, seated monitoring and absence of a symptom endpoint limit the finding.
Parkinson CBD trial dizziness reporting with oral corn vehicle — The associated thesis reports dizziness in the active arm. Posture and an oil-specific comparison are unavailable.

oral corn oil comparator and blood pressure in seated treated hypertensive adults — Seated pressure is a distinct outcome from standing lightheadedness. The study neither specifies refining nor compares corn oil against randomized no-oil use.

Scrambled egg offered within both Parkinson diet plans; one visual hallucination event occurred in the ketogenic arm — Individual intake and event timing are unknown. Hallucinations resolved after pramipexole reduction. The trial did not compare egg-specific visual hallucination frequency.

Mixed diluted Avena formulation with measured sleep efficiency planned — Completed 81-person short-term insomnia trial with no posted results. It tests a combination tablet and does not isolate oat grain.
Mixed oat-based beverage protocol with sleep quality secondary — The planned trial in older adults has no posted results. The formulation, comparison and outcome do not identify a rolled-oat effect.

Oat-milk products and planned toddler sleep outcomes — The recruiting study compares different dairy and oat product regimens. The sleep records are pending and the exposure and population differ from the frozen claim.

Mixed oat straw extract and adult sleep complaints — Final PSQI favored the combination containing oat straw extract, melatonin, valerian and other ingredients. No separate oat arm or Parkinson cohort.

Whole grains and prevalent versus incident insomnia in a cohort — Fully adjusted odds ratio for highest versus lowest whole-grain quintile was 0.93 for prevalent insomnia and 1.00 for incident insomnia. Whole grains were pooled and no rolled-oat or Parkinson effect was estimated.

Mixed granola and inconsistent subjective versus EEG sleep outcomes — In the uncontrolled UMIN000053189 cohort, subjective insomnia scores fell from baseline at weeks four and eight and EEG sleep outcomes did not change significantly. The test recipe does not establish rolled oats.

Personalized granola and uncontrolled insomnia scores — Overall Athens Insomnia Scale change was inconclusive. A subgroup of 19 improved from baseline. The recipe supplement and any isolated oat contrast remain unavailable.

Breakfast oat products with glycemic outcomes — The published UMIN000048192 breakfast experiments report glucose and no sleep results. Their relationship to the registry's oatmeal lunch and sleep narrative is unresolved.

Extracted oat fiber doses and exploratory daily sleep duration — Two-week NCT06739941 study found no significant change in sleep duration over time or between three open doses. No inactive control, rolled-oat preparation or clinical Parkinson insomnia endpoint.

Oat flour and bran products with a sleep item inside GHQ-12 — NCT06393114 randomized 56 analyzed adults with mild metabolic deterioration to crossover oat gurt and porridge periods. Both used oat flour, bran and faba protein. Supplement Table 11 reports an inconclusive direct GHQ-12 comparison (P=.569). No sleep item estimate, plain rolled oat contrast or Parkinson population. The journal and EPO6_170 describe one trial.

Oatmeal challenge shared by both randomized enzyme periods — In NCT06628869, sleep quality did not differ significantly between fructanase and placebo (P=.91). Both periods used the same oatmeal and inulin. The trial estimates an enzyme effect rather than an oat effect.

rolled oats as the food comparator in chronic insomnia — For rolled oats the diary mean sleep time changed from 359 to 376 minutes in one week. Within-arm changes and the week-by-condition comparisons were inconclusive. There was no randomized no-oat control and no Parkinson cohort.
Parkinson insomnia and diet-pattern scores — The pattern analysis reported no significant insomnia association and no individual rolled-oat comparison.

wild green oat extract and actigraphic sleep in smokers — Wake after sleep onset changed by −0.7 minutes versus +5.4 with placebo at eight weeks (p=.047). The preparation, population and outcome differ from rolled oats and Parkinson insomnia severity.

Oatmeal-rice lunch with numerical sleep estimates unavailable — The registry and DOI 10.11402/ajscs.36.0_58 report OSA-MA measurement with discordant sample counts. The sleep estimates and participant overlap remain open.

oral lemon balm extract and general motor performance in MPTP mice — Rotarod and activity improved at the two higher tested levels. Dystonic posturing was unmeasured and the intervention was ethanolic extract.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — PDF page 23 identifies Melissa as a source of phenolic acids. The experiment tests isolated acids in perfused rat liver rather than brewed leaf tea.

lemon balm tincture and temporal muscle contraction categories — Final categories gave an inconclusive arm comparison (p=.551). Children with bruxism, no fresh leaf, dystonic posture or Parkinson disease.

chives in a mixed Parkinson diet and a facial-expression item in UPDRS III — The motor total improved at one year in both groups. The article names the facial item but does not report its change. Chive preparation, participant amounts, and a chive-free comparison were unavailable.
injected sumac extract and mouse open-field activity — The open-field activity test did not score dystonia.
sumac extract applied to Parkinson donor skin cells — Donor-derived fibroblasts cannot measure a clinical dystonia change.

cassia-containing formula and composite oral function in older adults — The clinician composite included unclear pronunciation and dysarthria and improved over time. The study gives no separate speech item or ground-cinnamon comparison.

hazelnut-spread carrier and measured digit movements — IBB cereal manipulation improved with combined drugs. The study used a shared hazelnut spread with sunflower oil after spinal injury, without a cold-pressed oil contrast or handwriting measurement.

oral avocado oil in a rat model of induced prostate hyperplasia — The 2023 report found thinner epithelium in oil-fed induced rats. Related 2020 methods specify 7% cold-pressed avocado oil versus soybean oil and the 2014 abstract uses a different timing description. These reports do not measure voiding or urgency.

oral almond lipid preparations and gastric emptying in growing rats — The abstract gives an intermediate gastric half-emptying time of 172 ± 11 minutes for almond oil. This is a physiological proxy upstream of oral drug absorption. No cold-pressed specification, levodopa response or Parkinson daily OFF outcome is measured.

Parkinson meal patent and safflower recipes without paired patient measurements — The patient example used canola and sunflower oil. Safflower recipes were separate examples with no measured medication OFF time, and the oil grade is unstated.

pooled legume or bean intake and whole-diet insomnia scores — Table 2 reports insomnia against whole diet scores. Table S4 evaluates pooled bean or legume intake against aggregate symptom burden and does not identify species or preparation.

MIND dietary intervention, combined legume category and sleep quality — The adjusted sleep quality comparison favored the dietary pattern. Lentils and their preparation were not isolated, and clinical Parkinson insomnia was unmeasured.

corn-oil capsules and post-hoc constipation event counts — Asian and non-Asian strata gave opposite signed numerical comparisons versus omega-3 and wide uncertainty. The parent trial gave no oil-free control or Parkinson severity result.
high-dose corn oil and reported bowel habits — Three high single-bolus participants reported loose stools and cramping. No formal constipation comparison or exact exposed denominator.

corn-oil high-fat rodent comparison — Muscle molecular markers differ across high-fat oils. The active comparator and molecular outcome do not estimate an isolated refined corn oil and Parkinson endpoint effect.

separately numbered conference member with preparation or outcome limits — P-07.1-14 uses corn oil in controls and measures liver markers after malathion. It reports no bowel transit, stools, or refined oil comparison.
shared collection original source context — P210 compares EPA/DHA-enriched high-fat chow against corn-oil high-fat chow for muscle transcriptome and proteins. No separate frozen patient outcome.

corn oil as high-fat diet control and partial marine-lipid substitution — Corn oil was one base formulation, with and without different marine PUFA fractions. Adiposity and lipids were measured. The possibly overlapping article concerns the same broad research and a refined corn oil symptom effect is unresolved.

corn oil changes alongside multiple assigned rat diet changes — Corn oil was 10.00, 8.76 and 8.74 g per 100 g of the three diets. Fecal mass was 1.16, 2.46 and 2.42 g/day. Olive oil, soup components, casein, starch and cellulose also changed. The comparison cannot assign an effect to refined corn oil.

shared collection original source context — P233 is appended in the complete PMC HTML for this oral-key record and separately printed in the poster supplement. It compares corn and fish oil during shared exercise for strength and mechanistic outcomes. One study family.

shared collection original source context — Printed P233 reports an omega-3 versus corn-oil comparator during shared resistance training. Its strength findings are distinct from the frozen clinical outcomes. The other PMC key reproduces this member.

corn-oil control during exercise training — The final isometric interaction is p=.015 and the corn arm changed −1.4%. P233 uses −0.3%. Body strength during shared training does not measure any frozen Parkinson endpoint in these claims.

measured comparison or exposure context with a different preparation, outcome or population — All study-one groups used corn oil in the shared cooking diet. The cholestyramine group had two withdrawals for constipation or acidity. Occasional constipation elsewhere was reported without an oil contrast, and oil refinement was not given.

corn oil versus extra-virgin olive oil and adverse-event reporting — Three constipation events reported during olive treatment. Corn reporting was thresholded and exact count unavailable. No measurement of clinical constipation severity.
corn-oil capsules as fish-oil comparator with bowel events — Constipation in 1 of 18 corn-oil starters and 2 of 35 fish-oil starters. Both groups received oils and population differs.

corn oil in mixed oral feeds and mouse intestinal transit — Corn oil fell from 2.2 to 1.7 or 1.2 g per 100 g as several ingredients changed. Diet 2 also added prebiotic fibers and improved the dye-distance measure. No independent corn oil grade or human constipation estimate.

corn versus coconut oil feeding and adverse-event reporting — One corn-period constipation event judged treatment-related. The paper gives no full arm-specific constipation counts, severity or oil-grade estimate.

separate gastrointestinal conference member and ingredient context — A tumor experiment incorporates corn oil in control or combined diets involving EPA and aspirin. The study does not assign the frozen preparation and clinical endpoint.
combination and constipation — The case report tested a multi-ingredient formula without separating individual constituents.
combined botanical formula and intravenous levodopa — Case with fecal impaction improved under multiple cointerventions. Contribution of Japanese pepper was not isolated.

perioperative multi-component Zanthoxylum intervention and bowel timing — First defecation and flatus are recovery endpoints after major abdominal surgery. No isolated Zanthoxylum intervention, culinary processing or Parkinson constipation outcome.

Japanese pepper in a mixed extract and constipation — Six Parkinson’s participants reported improved bowel frequency and defecation. The before-and-after study used a formula with a related Zanthoxylum species and did not isolate toasted Sichuan pepper.

placebo-controlled full Daikenchuto formula and chronic constipation — Overall treatment-effect rating favored the complete formula after four weeks. The trial does not isolate pepper, toasting or a Parkinson-specific effect.

Pediatric infection fatigue incidence after dried Ataulfo by-product — Official Table 3S shows control 3 versus mango 0 children with fatigue at two months (p=.1823). The material is dried peel and pulp remnant, the endpoint an incidence count, and the measurement context infection.

Randomized mixed smoothies with a prespecified patient fatigue measure — The mixed product group compared with usual opioid agonist treatment had a reported FSS-3 change of −0.1, with 95% CI −0.6 to +0.4. Only some options contained mango. The comparison identifies neither raw mango nor the Parkinson population.

Mango-specific intake frequency in people with diagnosed Parkinson disease — The FFQ names mango, without culinary preparation or cultivar. Motor decrement within examination items is not independently measured patient fatigue. The study does not publish a mango-specific fatigue contrast.

Mango-containing options in one arm of an uncontrolled mixed-food pilot — The 24-participant feasibility study measured FSS-3 before and after. In 14 paired observations the median change was +0.33, with IQR −0.67 to +2.33. No control, mango-specific dose or Parkinson cohort was present.

Fresh fruit and pulp challenge in an exercise-associated allergy case — Fresh pulp skin test was positive. Oral challenge without exercise was negative. The case measured allergic reactions, without fatigue severity or PD.

Ataulfo fruit pulp and pulp plus peel crossover during exercise — Registration reports 19 healthy students and specifies exercise biomarkers. It has no posted results or registered fatigue-severity outcome.

Previously frozen mango pulp and measured cycling output — Cycling watts, distance and speed did not show a clear difference in the prescribed exercise test. No independently measured fatigue severity or Parkinson population.

Adult fatigue complaint with liver injury after boiled mango beverage — The author poster documents one month of fatigue in a suspected liver injury case. Exposure was a whole-fruit decoction with an additional potential medication exposure. No fatigue-severity scale or PD cohort.

acute concentrated mango leaf extract and POMS fatigue in healthy volunteers — Study-1 POMS fatigue p=.015 compares before and after extract. Placebo had a larger printed mean decline, with no between-condition test reported. Study 2 gave no clear POMS result for extract.

oral mango leaf extract and separate visual fatigue ratings in healthy adults — The 70-person crossover found no clear effect on mental fatigue during the task battery. Dose formulation is distinct from raw mango flesh.

oral mango leaf extract and registered subjective fatigue measures in healthy adults — Supplementary File 4 reports mental fatigue treatment p=.309 and POMS Fatigue–Inertia treatment p=.354, with inconclusive treatment-by-time terms. Parkinson disease and fruit flesh were untested.

mango stem-bark blend and exercise performance in healthy men — Bench-press maximum and repetitions improved in some comparisons. Day-56 adjusted differences versus one-set placebo were +10.6 and +13.8 kg. Stem bark was combined with a flower extract; no mango fruit or validated fatigue scale. The 2021 conference member is likely the same study.

soluble mango leaf extract and POMS in healthy students — The initial published soluble-extract trial found changes on selected mood domains and gave no clear fatigue effect, as the later replication explicitly notes. The exposure was leaf extract.
mango pulp consumption and exercise recovery biomarkers — The fruit trial measured inflammation, muscle damage and other biomarkers, without a fatigue severity score or Parkinson population.

Verified fresh mango contrast in healthy adults — The crossover separately tested fresh mango and measured glucose and satiety. Those endpoints do not provide fatigue severity or a Parkinson comparison.

Controlled leaf extract and a separately reported mood-fatigue subscale — The 100 mg soluble leaf extract led to lower exploratory POMS fatigue compared with placebo in healthy university students. A distinct formulation and context preclude inference to raw fruit and fatigue in Parkinson disease.

cinnamon-containing combined treatments and reported voice clarity — A case describes improved subjective clarity after several concurrent therapies. Voice amplitude and the cinnamon contribution were unmeasured.

Older adults took a multi-component formula including cinnamon bark extract; clinician oral-condition composite — Composite includes speech problems but does not report separate speech change or acoustic amplitude; no PD-specific ground-cinnamon comparison.

Cinnamon appears in both multi-food PD diet plans; Part II and III composite scales — Published totals do not provide acoustic voice volume or a cinnamon-only contrast; individual cinnamon consumption and species are unreported.

sunflower capsules and measured fine hand coordination in mild cognitive impairment — Age- and sex-standardized dominant-hand Coin Rotation scores changed from −0.25 to −0.12 in the sunflower arm, with no clear treatment difference (p=.38). The oral oil grade was unspecified and the study reported no Parkinson subgroup.

sunflower food frequency and composite Parkinson symptom burden — The poster reports +2 total PRO-PD points per intake frequency category (95% CI −10 to 13, p=.787). The cross-sectional exposure did not specify an oil grade. It gives no individual voice estimate.

cold-pressed sunflower rinse and perceived talking ease — Four participants reported easier talking with oil versus eight with water, with no clear difference (p=.250). They spat out the oil. Loudness, refined oil consumption, and a Parkinson-specific estimate were not measured.

safflower oil comparator in a crossover with registered clinical anxiety — No untreated arm, cold-press specification or Parkinson cohort. The later 47-person publication remains a provisional linkage to registry accrual of 60.

safflower oil mixed-meal crossover with peripheral biomarkers — Healthy participants received meals containing safflower oil, cocoa butter or no added fat. The abstract does not give an isolated contrast for the safflower arm, specify pressing method or measure the frozen Parkinson symptom.

safflower and fish-oil crossover with lipid and inflammatory endpoints — The later publications and official protocol represent one study family. Some biomarker directions differed by oil, with no swallowing, falls or anxiety measure and no verified cold-pressed grade.

safflower oil comparator period and adult PROMIS anxiety in Glut1 deficiency — Changes +0.5 on safflower and +3.1 on triheptanoin; between-period contrast p=.1138. No oil-free comparison, Parkinson cohort or oil grade.

combined oil placebo and secondary Hamilton anxiety in bipolar outpatients — The registered placebo includes both olive and safflower oils. The published anxiety coefficient and confidence interval disagree on the sign. No standalone effect or processing specification.

safflower-containing placebo and anxiety questionnaire — Completed without posted results in the screened registry. An oil-containing placebo in a synbiotic trial cannot isolate a cold-pressed-oil effect in Parkinson anxiety.

maternal safflower oil and elevated plus maze in rat offspring — Offspring of oil-fed dams spent more time on open arms. Developmental exposure and animal exploration differ from culinary intake and Parkinson anxiety.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S1.97 proposes parsley as a possible dietary source of related Rubisco peptides while modelling spinach-derived rubiscolin. No parsley isolate, dose or Parkinson outcome is measured.

common parsley in historical discussion of fits — Pages 557–558 identify garden parsley and relay historical concern about aggravated fits. Individual exposure and measured outcome are absent. A fit is a distinct outcome from Parkinson muscle rigidity.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The Petroselinum crispum entry describes furanocoumarins and primary photosensitization. The broader common-name cross-reference includes other genera. No frozen culinary or Parkinson symptom result appears.

mixed Parkinson diet and composite motor score — Appendix A lists both herbs in a multicomponent diet. Composite UPDRS III scores improved. The examination includes rigidity, but no item-level result, individual herb amount or preparation, or herb-specific contrast was reported.
parsley root juice and cramps — Reports of cramps decreased in an uncontrolled comparison with inconsistent denominators. The paper did not assess rigidity or Parkinson symptoms and used root juice.

combined Parkinson diet program and apathy ascertainment — The qualitative report describes pre-existing apathy as a barrier. The same trial registered Starkstein apathy and reported baseline prevalence but no post-intervention arm estimates. No analyzed chervil intake.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — Apathy was not an endpoint of the intervention report.
individual Parkinson symptoms and diet scores — The diet-index study did not find a significant apathy association or estimate a fresh-chervil effect.

personalized plant-rich diet and time-restricted eating with apathy outcomes — Apathy rating changed 13.65 to 9.0 with the program and 13.05 to 13.6 with control. The time-by-group and post-treatment comparisons are distinct, with conflicting post-treatment statements. There is no chervil-specific exposure or estimate.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — No depression severity result by preparation or individual herb was reported.
individual Parkinson symptoms and diet scores — The Healthy Diet Indicator association cannot determine a dried lovage leaf symptom effect.

summer savory topical gel trial and oral clinical outcomes — Topical essential-oil gel was tested against placebo in denture stomatitis. The stated outcomes were palatal erythema and Candida colonies, without listener intelligibility or fresh-herb ingestion.

pooled fresh vegetables and Parkinson motivation — Higher pooled vegetable frequency was associated with greater motivation (absolute r = 0.166368). The baseline analysis supplies no cucumber-specific estimate or uncertainty interval.

cucumber extract protocol and mood or fatigue outcomes in healthy adults — The completed status gives no directional outcome. Registered POMS-2 and fatigue measures do not isolate raw cucumber or Parkinson apathy.
aqueous marjoram extract and motor tests in haloperidol mice — Rotarod retention was longer at the higher extract dose. Preparation, population and endpoint differ from the exact claim.
filtered marjoram tea and motor examination in Parkinson — Inconclusive within-arm UPDRS III comparison. Separate postural-stability estimate unavailable.

flaxseed oil contrasted with fish oil and dizziness events — Three of 60 per group reported dizziness. The observational exposure and unmeasured posture or severity leave orthostatic lightheadedness open.

tube-feeding timing and low blood pressure in one Parkinson case — Blood pressure rose during a feeding schedule change. Flaxseed oil was given in a separate case without Parkinson diagnosis. No oil identity for P-046 or standardized orthostatic symptom result.

Rapeseed blend comparator and insomnia scores in nurses — Table 2 reported a higher Week 13 insomnia score with the blend than fish oil and inconclusive later contrasts. There was no isolated rapeseed arm, pressing method, Parkinson cohort or dream outcome.

canola-containing diet in shift workers with sleep-disturbance label — The registry lists melatonin and cardiometabolic endpoints. No dream enactment outcome, cold-pressed grade or posted results are reported.

clove oil odor detection during an oxytocin crossover — Clove oil was a detection probe in a schizophrenia study of oxytocin. The abstract reports no clear clove threshold change. The later journal report has no clove threshold. Neither route nor endpoint matches the frozen culinary comparison.

oral clove capsule adjunct and Beck depression — Week-six Beck scores favored extract with citalopram. Apathy, motivational items, culinary preparation and Parkinson disease were not measured. Registry ID was reported by the article only.

injected clove oil and immobility and locomotion in mice — Immobilities and movement tests changed under injected oil. The concurrent change in locomotion limits psychological interpretation and the experiment supplies no oral clove apathy result.

Ground cloves were consumed in a controlled mixed-food comparison — The authors tested immediate consumer emotion and liking with a four-spice blend. They did not measure sustained clinical apathy or separately manipulate clove.

Apathy measured with olfactory associations in diagnosed Parkinson — Parkinson apathy was associated with composite odor outcomes. No isolated clove odor association or dietary exposure was verified in the accessible source.

Human Parkinson randomized multi-odor trial with a nonmotor composite — The study evaluated depression and anxiety instruments and Part I composite scores. No separate apathy score or isolated clove consumption result was reported.

Huntington total motor comparison includes dystonia item — The six-month active-minus-safflower total motor difference was +0.6 (95% CI −1.0 to 2.5). The separate dystonia result is unreported. The repeated 2025 records share this cohort.

safflower oil comparator and paroxysmal movement events in Glut1 deficiency — The trial’s difference in grouped paroxysmal events was inconclusive. No no-oil group, isolated Parkinson dystonia measure or refining grade was reported.

original article and linked trial context — The TRIHEP3 row uses safflower oil against triheptanoin in Huntington disease. Its motor total includes dystonia but no separate estimate is reported. The dysphagia rows are distinct tablet and swallowing skill trials without a safflower arm.

original article and linked trial context — The repeated TRIHEP3 row identifies the same whole oil comparator. It supplies no separate dystonia or swallowing outcome. The two swallowing studies elsewhere in the table use a drug or training, with no safflower allocation.

macadamia oil in rat diet during experimental SCD inhibitor pharmacology — The oil was in mixed chow and grade and individual intake were unreported; biochemical fatty-acid outcomes do not measure Parkinson or levodopa-induced dyskinesia.

freeze-dried cranberry powder and attention in healthy older adults — The group-by-time interaction for Addenbrooke attention was inconclusive (p = .467). Delayed recall improved, a separate endpoint. No cooked cranberry or Parkinson arm was included.

cranberry juice crossover with cognitive performance and planned attention context — Registration lists beverage and placebo arms, planned COMPASS composites and no posted results. It does not identify a cooked whole cranberry exposure or Parkinson cohort.

The randomized parallel cranberry juice trial did not find a clear effect on computerized attention. Two separate short-term memory measures favored juice. The ITT sample of 72 comprised healthy final-year students, and the frozen exposure is cooked cranberry.

cranberry beverage and attention-related tests in healthy older adults — Trail Making and Stroop test changes were inconclusive over six weeks. The intervention was a beverage and the participants did not have Parkinson disease.

shared collection original source context — PO1.165 summarizes genuine quinoa, rice and quinoa-flake comparisons for intake, satiety and metabolic markers. No Parkinson gait or rigidity result is shown.

red quinoa ethanol extract and fly movement measures — The public dissertation and 2025 abstract report the same study. Extract co-exposure attenuated rotenone-related changes in climbing and crossings. The exposure was an extract and the study did not measure human walking.

acute allergic hypotension after pepper exposure — Chinese case report documents blood pressure around 60/45 mmHg during an allergic reaction. It supplies adverse-event context without an orthostatic assessment.

formula comparator and resting blood pressure — The randomized crossover detected higher mesenteric flow with formula, with no significant resting blood pressure change. Standing symptoms were unmeasured.
fruit extract and isolated vascular relaxation — Nepalese pepper fruit extract relaxed rabbit aortic rings. The assay did not measure standing pressure or human symptoms.

low-fat mixed diet includes nutmeg in a baked recipe; aggregate motor exam — The total exam includes a multidimensional speech item, but no separate loudness or nutmeg comparison is reported; grated preparation and actual intake are unverified.

roasted pressed kernel oil and skeletal muscle cell development — Sections 2.2–2.4 verify roasted-then-pressed kernels. Figure 7 distinguishes Ordu oil with larger myotube diameter from cuticle-oil-related length. The exposed cells did not undergo rigidity assessment.

whole hazelnuts offered and Parkinson motor composite includes rigidity — Appendix A lists whole hazelnuts separately from the supplied oils. The full motor score includes rigidity, with no separate rigidity values or hazelnut oil contrast.
exceptionally bitter zucchini and acute gastrointestinal toxicity — The source links poisonings to unusually bitter fruit. Dream enactment and preparation were outside the comparison.
zucchini ingestion challenge in selected allergy patients — Oral and gastrointestinal reactions establish a separate acute adverse outcome. No sleep measures were reported.
whole Parkinson diet including unspecified zucchini — The intervention grouped ingredients and the publication did not measure dream enactment.

rat motor behavior during injected clove essential oil — The rat study reports actimetry and cylinder posture outcomes after injected essential oil. It did not measure muscle rigidity or oral ground clove.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — Abstract 65 identifies eugenol in clove oil and tests the oral isolated compound or its labeled analogue, without a tested clove food.

isolated oral eugenol and levodopa-related behaviors in toxin model — Isolated oral compound did not improve lesion-model abnormal behaviors induced by levodopa. Different motor measures and no clinical rigidity or ground clove.
oral isolated eugenol and catalepsy in MPTP mice — Higher pretreatment exposures lowered catalepsy while post-treatment had no clear benefit. Clinical rigidity and ground clove were untested.
clove essential oil and cell oxidative outcomes — Hydrodistilled oil was tested in a cellular stress model. No behavioral rigidity measure or oral ground clove.
celery stalk reactions after ingestion — The selected cohort reported oral allergy and swelling. No motor swallowing measurement or Parkinson population.
healthy participants chewing celery — The study measures parotid secretion and does not test dysphagia severity.
cooked mixed-vegetable ratatouille containing celery — Ready-to-swallow bolus properties and mastication measured in healthy adults. No raw-stalk comparison or Parkinson dysphagia measure.

celery stalk in the airway after a meal — Choking and direct visualization establish an adverse food event in stroke/vascular dementia. Preparation was unstated and no Parkinson dysphagia comparator was available.

contaminated carrot-millet dish and acute auditory hallucination — Investigators identified a Jimson weed contaminant in millet. The report does not implicate carrot or examine recurrent visual hallucinations in Parkinson's.
raw carrot identified in Parkinson case-control questionnaire — Raw carrot was a questionnaire item. No hallucination-frequency comparison was reported.

thyme oil used as an EEG biometric odor stimulus — The indexed conference abstract describes odors used to identify individual EEG responses. It supplies no clinical olfaction or ingested thyme comparison.
thyme among mixed odorants in long COVID smell rehabilitation — The protocol uses thyme as one of several scent stimuli and measures olfaction after COVID-19.
thyme and cinnamon among inhaled spices in post COVID smell training — The completed protocol identifies thyme among smell training stimuli and does not supply an isolated dietary effect.

thyme sniffing in multi-odor postinfectious smell rehabilitation — A separate postinfectious cohort had better combined smell scores after rotating odors. The schedule placed thyme in one of three blocks with other scents. The groups were allocated in order, and the contrast estimates the whole training schedule.

thyme-containing multi-ingredient product and measured olfaction in acute rhinosinusitis — An indexed study abstract reports better smell outcomes for a multi-ingredient sinusitis treatment containing thyme extract. The isolated effect of fresh thyme remains unmeasured.

inhaled thyme extract in a fixed four-odor post-traumatic regimen — Original Methods identify Thymus vulgaris extract and three other odors. Follow-up composite smell scores were 18.35 in the trained arm versus 13.06 in controls, p<.033. No isolated or oral thyme effect in Parkinson disease. Cohort overlap with Rezaeyan is unresolved.

confirmed thyme odor in multi-odor post-traumatic training — The 2024 original Methods confirm thyme in fixed training and in the first rotating month. They explicitly identify the same cohort as the 2021 report. The whole sniffing program does not estimate an isolated or oral thyme effect in Parkinson disease.
thyme odor within a 12-scent post-COVID protocol — The nonrandomized comparison favored the odor program on total smell function. The study does not isolate thyme or test fresh thyme by mouth.

chamuangone-enriched rice bran oil and rat locomotion — Stride, ladder and open-field outcomes generally improved in haloperidol-treated rats. Enrichment and the absence of plain oil and human gait-speed arms limit interpretation.

isolated rice-bran constituent and fly locomotion — The gamma-oryzanol diet reduced rotenone-related climbing and mobility deficits in flies. The 2016 thesis and 2015 article describe the same experiment. No whole oil or clinical walking-speed comparison.

extracted rice bran oil and rat open-field movement — Pairwise open-field and home-cage locomotion differences were inconclusive. Rotarod coordination improved in a haloperidol model. Grade and Parkinson walking speed are unverified.
hexane rice bran extract and rat movement — Oral bran extract partly reversed locomotor changes in a rotenone model. Refined rice bran oil and human walking speed were untested.
oatmeal and total self-reported Parkinson symptoms — The oatmeal coefficient was inconclusive and the paper gives no small-handwriting estimate.
green oat capsules and computer-based tracking task — Some tracking and working-memory results favored extract. There was no handwriting or micrographia assessment.

topical capsaicin and human thumb tracking accuracy — Healthy adults tracked visual targets more accurately in the capsaicin group after skin exposure and before and after training. No handwriting or consumed smoked paprika was measured.

local hand capsaicin and precision pinch performance in humans — The pain group had better overall composite skill and similar training improvement in a cursor task. Pinch force and speed–accuracy do not estimate writing size after smoked paprika.

isolated eugenol and gait-related tasks in MPTP mice — Eugenol pretreatment improved narrow-beam crossing and post-treatment worsened it. The rodent task and constituent provide no estimate for ground allspice in people.

injected allspice leaf extract and gross motor depression in rats — High-dose intraperitoneal leaf extracts caused motor depression and reduced reflexes in general toxicology observations. Oral fraction study measured other outcomes. Ground fruit and clinical bradykinesia remain unresolved.

lovage in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome — The menu lists lovage and the motor examination includes speech. Leaf and drying are unconfirmed and individual voice-volume change was not reported.

filtered dried-marjoram tea and aggregate motor examination — The tea arm motor score decreased by 2.24 points, with within-arm p = .069. The available results omit walking-slowness and directly consumed dried leaf estimates.
marjoram in a honey mixture evaluated in people with Parkinson disease — The Methods give a named marjoram exposure and follow-up in 35 patients. Leaf preparation and walking speed were unreported.
reported marjoram use and broad motor symptom frequencies — Marjoram appears once in the use table. It cannot be linked to walking measures, dried preparation or an individual response.
corn oil capsule comparator for cannabis use disorder pharmacotherapy — The protocol records sustained attention as a secondary outcome in a drug-versus-corn-oil comparison.

corn oil ethyl esters as comparator with cognitive testing in deployed adults — The published abstract gives overall cognitive comparisons, using corn oil ethyl esters as the comparator. Attention-specific results and culinary refining are unverified.

corn oil emulsion comparator and attention tasks in older adults — The corn oil comparator had a small, inconclusive within-phase attention change. The design has no oil-free arm, processing grade or Parkinson cohort.

oral corn oil comparator and sustained-attention task — No clear performance difference emerged against two DHA doses in healthy children. Neuroimaging and fatty acid correlations do not estimate an oil-induced change in attention in Parkinson disease.
oral Parkinson trial vehicle and aggregate cognition — All arms had corn oil and the aggregate cognition endpoint offers no attention task or attention-specific item result.

reported pediatric exposure to product coded allspice oil — The proceedings list 234 exposures, with oral irritation, cough and vomiting most frequently reported for the oil. The source has no individual results for visual hallucination frequency, confirmed ground-fruit exposure or Parkinson cohort.

Adults without diagnosed PD; multicomponent diet score with legume component; binary probable dream-enactment screen — The authors found no association between alternate Mediterranean diet adherence and probable RBD. This is not an isolated chickpea or canned preparation contrast, does not measure episode frequency, and is not a Parkinson cohort.

101 people with isolated polysomnography-confirmed RBD; general legumes and estimated prodromal Parkinson probability — Observed legume associations concern estimated prodromal Parkinson probability and marker count rather than dream-enactment episode frequency; no canned chickpea intake or diagnosed Parkinson cohort is established.

Video-PSG isolated RBD vs controls; generic legumes on prior-year frequency questionnaire; prospective clinical conversion — The adjusted generic-legume frequency difference between iRBD and controls was inconclusive; RBD status and clinical conversion are not dream-enactment frequency, and canned chickpea exposure is unspecified. Food-group supplement is inaccessible.

whole sweet pepper in two Parkinson diet menus and overall Part III motor examination — Capsicum occurred in both menus. Part III score changes were −8.58 and −6.27 (between p=.055). The report gave no gait-speed result or independent exposure to grilled peppers.

oral Capsicum fruit extract and rearing in a rat motor model — Rats given two higher extract doses and extract with levodopa showed improved rearing. The tested Capsicum fruit cultivar was unspecified, contained capsaicinoids and was extracted. The outcome was not walking speed.

purified nonpungent Capsicum and accelerometer-recorded activity — Ten-meter walking was a baseline eligibility measure. Light-to-moderate activity was measured after treatment, with a subgroup difference favoring extract (p=.050 in prose, p<.05 in Table 4) and no walking-time follow-up contrast in the report. The trial excluded motor disorders and walking aids.

paprika vegetable in a Parkinson diet with gait in the motor examination — The intervention group improved on total UPDRS III (p=.0004). Diet alone p=.033 and diet plus bowel cleansing p=.005 were within-group comparisons. Gait-item results and paprika preparation were unavailable.

isolated capsiate and timed short or middle distance running — After 12 mg capsiate, healthy active men completed 400 m in 66.4 versus 67.1 seconds (p=.046) and 3,000 m in 893.9 versus 915.2 seconds (p=.015). No whole pepper exposure or Parkinson gait measure.

isolated capsiate and timed 10 km running — After two 12 mg doses of capsiate, the 10 km running time comparison was 45.07 versus 45.13 minutes (p=.828). The primary paper lists running and total 24 mg. No whole pepper or Parkinson gait measure.

sweet pepper food frequency and timed 4 m walk within composite sarcopenia — The 2021 journal report adjusted OR at ≥2–3 times per week was 0.66 (95% CI 0.45–0.95) for sarcopenia, while the likely related 2019 abstract gives a nonsignificant sweet pepper result. Neither supplies a separate pepper coefficient for gait or a grilled exposure.

patient-reported walking and slowness within overall Parkinsonism symptoms — The cohort included patient-reported difficulty walking and slowness and grouped vegetables showed an association with total symptom burden. The published questionnaire supplies no named pepper exposure and results give no walking-specific estimate.

Thai Parkinson mobility and original vegetable questionnaire — The bilingual survey separately lists chili powder and records grouped vegetable intake. Mobility outcomes were analyzed without named bell pepper intake or a pepper-specific coefficient.

cold-pressed turnip rapeseed oil and resting blood pressure — A 37-person crossover found the same mean resting systolic pressure after oil and butter. Postural change and lightheadedness were not evaluated.

conventional canola in provided foods and resting pressure in peripheral arterial disease — The dissertation reports no clear treatment effect on blood-pressure change. The study did not use confirmed cold-pressed oil or report postural lightheadedness.

canola and coconut mixed meal crossover with resting pressure and vascular measures — Kienēs and colleagues randomized the order of four mixed meals, each containing canola or coconut oil at one of two fat amounts. Twenty-nine participants with cardiometabolic risk completed all visits. The paper calls the coconut oil virgin cold-pressed and names Brölio canola without specifying a pressing grade. Resting blood pressure appears as a screening measure. Post-meal tests repor...

ungraded canola menu and lightheadedness in Parkinson disease — Low-fat group lightheadedness was 2/23 and 4/23 across the two intervals, versus 2/24 in each ketogenic interval. Standing was not the prespecified trigger and the oil dose and grade were unavailable.

pooled legumes in a sample menu and gait testing in a Parkinson nutrition cohort — The example dinner lists legumes and the cohort measured gait speed. The paper gives no canned lentil consumption or analysis linking intake to gait speed.

lentils among Parkinson menu options and motor examination total — The plant menu group had a lower four-week motor total. The comparison does not isolate lentils or preparation, and walking speed was not reported separately.

injected hydroalcoholic red lentil extract and cataleptic posture in rats — The source records persistence of an imposed posture after a perphenazine challenge. Walking speed and ordinary canned lentils were not tested.

shared Parkinson vegetarian menu with lentils and motor composite — The two small groups improved on total UPDRS III. The study gives no lentil preparation, isolated intake or walking speed item contrast.

lentils among prebiotic menu options and composite motor score — A four-week menu and lactulose intervention produced an inconclusive motor total change. Published data do not isolate lentil preparation or intake and omit individual walking speed changes.

shiitake in a mixed-diagnosis choking series — Five of 15 patients had Parkinson disease and one obstruction involved shiitake. The abstract gives no patient-to-food attribution, preparation, or swallowing severity comparison.

independent earlier referred population and combined diagnostic code — Table 1 lists seven Parkinson disease or parkinsonism cases among 51 older patients with sepsis and dysphagia. The 2013–2014 referral sample differs from the 2022–2023 admissions cohort. No ingredient-specific comparison.

direct Parkinson comorbidity context without assigned exposure — Table 4 identifies higher odds of incident recorded dysphagia in hospitalised people with Parkinson disease. PP0011 reports the same cohort and result. No ingredient allocation, preparation or symptom severity contrast is measured.

uncut shiitake and human small-bowel obstruction — Two people without teeth or dentures developed downstream obstructions. The report did not identify roasted shiitake or measure Parkinson swallowing.

shiitake texture testing for dysphagia diets — Some formulations met IDDSI Level 5 criteria and some did not. Printed puree and food texture tests are distinct from a clinical swallowing outcome after roasted mushroom.
shiitake variety and printed dysphagia texture — Selected printed material reached IDDSI Level 5 in food tests. The study did not compare the severity of patient swallowing difficulty.
enzyme-softened shiitake in food texture tests — Vacuum- and enzyme-treated samples reached IDDSI Level 6 criteria without any Parkinson swallowing measure.

rice bran oil comparator and aggregate motor examination — The trial prespecified Part III and reports total MDS-UPDRS. No facial expression item, oil-grade specification, or independent oil exposure effect was available.

mixed seed extract and rat locomotor activity — Figures 1 and 2 report less catalepsy and higher activity with a mixture of almond, peanut and watermelon seed extracts. No arm tested watermelon alone or raw flesh. Animal locomotion differs from measured bradykinesia in patients.

isolated oral lycopene and locomotor tasks in MPTP mice — The source reports timed beam crossing and open-field activity in mice. Only an isolated constituent was administered and neither task establishes clinical bradykinesia after raw watermelon.

watermelon intake frequency in a descriptive Parkinson cohort — Among 40 participants, 15 reported weekly watermelon, 9 monthly, 16 rarely or never and none daily. Preparation and an intake-linked bradykinesia contrast are absent.

watermelon juice and open-field activity in an anemia model — The university project reports increased activity after juice in phenylhydrazine-exposed rats. Arm accounting and figure details were incomplete. Clinical bradykinesia was outside the study.
fish group and composite symptom score — Nonfried fish frequency associated with lower aggregate symptom scores. It did not estimate a canned sardine fatigue effect.

canned sardines and processed sardine products — The sardine-enriched diet included canned sardines and foods made from them. The diabetes trial measured metabolic and microbiota outcomes rather than fatigue.
canned sardine feeding and metabolic outcomes — The 152-person trial assigned canned sardines in olive oil. Fatigue severity was absent and tiring of the intervention was a withdrawal reason.

canned sardine botulism and acute fatigue — A child with clinical foodborne botulism had fatigue after reported canned sardine exposure. Child-specific laboratory confirmation and a fatigue severity score were absent.

fish-meat peptide tablets and fatigue VAS in healthy adults — The registry reports a favorable fatigue contrast without exact arm data. Fish species remains unverified. The processed tablet and healthy population do not test canned sardines or Parkinson fatigue.
dried summer savory infusion and awake rat activity — Open-field squares crossed declined after seven days. The animals were awake and the study measured neither sleepiness nor Parkinson disease.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The poisoning entry names chives among foods hazardous to dogs and cats. This is veterinary species-specific source context with no observed Parkinson falls.

purified oral compound and rotarod latency in MPTP mice — Purified ferulic-acid groups generally stayed on the rod longer than the MPTP-only group. Rotarod latency and spontaneous fall frequency differ. The study used no dried chives.

measured ferulic acid in common chive tissue — Ferulic acid was measured at 22.22 to 28.79 mg/kg fresh weight in green tissue. This establishes constituent presence under the study conditions. The study measured no dried exposure or falls.

Parkinson case with narrative insomnia outcome — The clinical timeline reports improvement at about one week with daikenchuto and rehabilitation. Different pepper species and combined treatment limit attribution.

hydroalcoholic fruit extract and drug-induced loss of righting in mice — The high extract dose shortened drug-induced loss of righting. The onset cell and narrative disagree on significance. The assay, plant preparation and population limit transfer to insomnia after eating toasted Sichuan pepper.
planned healthy-gamer sleep-disturbance measure — PROMIS Sleep Disturbance was registered for a Nepalese pepper extract. No results were posted.

PD saffron capsule; Part III motor total; no speech-item or voice-volume estimate — Registered Part III contains a speech item incorporating volume, but accessible composite result cannot determine a direction for low voice volume; ground preparation is unverified.

PD Sargol powder tablet; planned composite MDS-UPDRS; no speech-item estimate — Part II and III speech items address broader speech than volume; no item-level data available and tablet regimen differs from ordinary culinary use.
injected carvacrol and drug-elicited vacuous chewing — Carvacrol prevented increased oral movements after reserpine. The preparation and dyskinesia model differ from dried savory and Parkinson.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — Total UPDRS III and the menu do not estimate individual freezing frequency after chervil.
shared sesame oil vehicle and composite neuropsychiatric results in Parkinson disease — The registry reports NPI totals and the trial does not isolate hallucination frequency or oil exposure.

Parkinson dyskinesia diary during broccoli and ground white mustard tea — The single illustrative Table 1 self-rating remained 2 across all weeks. There was no controlled comparison or mustard-only arm. Whether cohort members overlap an earlier case series remains open.
cabbage-derived fibers and Parkinson fecal fermentation ex vivo — The investigators measured SCFAs in samples. No sauerkraut ingestion or salivary outcome.
fresh versus pasteurized sauerkraut in healthy adults — Actual fermented food was consumed. Gut microbiota and metabolites were measured; drooling and cultivar were unreported.
shredded sauerkraut compared with nonfermented pickles in dysphagia-risk adults — Gut outcomes and feasibility were reported. No Parkinson subgroup or clinical drooling assessment.

baseline olfaction in a post-stroke inhaled pepper trial — Olfactory identification appears only among baseline characteristics. The trial measures subsequent swallowing and related outcomes, with no oral pepper or clinical olfaction change.

isolated piperine and mouse odor-guided behavior — Oral isolated piperine shortened buried-pellet search latency and changed odor preference in Thy1-SNCA mice. Ground black pepper and human smell impairment were outside the comparison.

ground black peppercorn used as an experimental odor — Food odors were presented in bottles to young adults for perceptual discrimination. Participants did not consume pepper and olfactory impairment was screened out.

practitioner survey with authenticated sumac fruit and voice indications — Fifty-six of 100 practitioners cited fruit infusion. The survey contains no patient-level symptom change or intelligibility assessment.

adult suspected allergy after a sumac-containing meal — Throat itching and breathing difficulty were recorded during suspected acute food allergy outside Parkinson disease. Speech intelligibility was not measured.
oral caraway polyphenols and open-field activity in healthy mice — Open-field tile crossings increased. The experiment measured neither freezing episodes nor toasted caraway in Parkinson disease.

retrospective pharmaceutical registry and gait-inclusive motor measurement — The published follow-up counts match retrospective target counts. The listed motor scale does not isolate walking slowness or raw celery stalk exposure.

celery suggested in a multimodal lifestyle program and a walking testimonial — One Parkinson participant described better walking, without individual celery consumption, timed walking, a raw stalk exposure or a comparison group.

oral solvent extract of whole celery and narrow-beam crossing in MPTP mice — Beam crossing latency fell in the 250 and 375 mg/kg groups. The task reflects balance and speed in a toxin model. It did not measure human walking slowness.
raw celery stalk in a human mixed-salad crossover — The trial measured vascular outcomes. There was no Parkinson or gait-speed measure.

pharmaceutical butylphthalide and an off-medication non-tremor subtotal — The subtotal includes gait alongside 11 other items. No isolated gait score or timed walk and no culinary raw celery stalk exposure.
celery included on a Parkinson vegetarian menu — Composite UPDRS III improved. Neither celery stalk preparation nor gait speed was reported separately.
aqueous parsley seed extract and arterial pressure — The extract lowered arterial pressure in anesthetized rats. No dried leaf meal, standing pressure or orthostatic lightheadedness was assessed.

dried parsley blood pressure trial, withdrawn — Registration planned blood pressure and urine comparisons in adults with hypertension. The withdrawn trial enrolled zero and specified no standing measure or orthostatic symptoms.

dried parsley leaf and asparagus clinical surveillance — In six-week surveillance of 163 patients, a dried parsley leaf and asparagus root product had no clinically useful antihypertensive effect. Seven withdrew with renal complaints. No standing pressure or orthostatic lightheadedness was reported.

aqueous aerial extract and arterial pressure — Oral extract lowered pressure in normotensive and induced-hypertensive rats. Parkinson lightheadedness, standing response and dried culinary parsley were outside the study.

other species model; methanolic leaf extract; motor tests; no human OFF duration — Haloperidol rat rotarod and catalepsy outcomes are not daily OFF time in people consuming dried basil. Reports are likely duplicate publications of one study; group-size and timing reporting unclear.

other species model; injected hydroethanolic aerial extract; motor tests; no human OFF duration — Rotenone rat motor tasks do not measure daily OFF time or ordinary dried basil consumption; abstract combination claim is not supported by displayed five-group tables and methods conflict on sex and formulation.

abdominal pain in two acute hazelnut food allergy cases — Both described abdominal pain during identified hazelnut-food anaphylaxis. The cake and cookie do not verify isolated oil or cold pressing, and the cases provide no pain severity or Parkinson comparison.

oral cold-pressed hazelnut oil and measured gastric tissue injury — The lower and higher oil arms had smaller ulcer areas than ethanol alone, with reported p<.001. The experiment measured injury area and histology without pain behavior or a Parkinson pain outcome.
celery named in a Parkinson diet with aggregate speech-inclusive motor scale — The celery plant part and preparation are unspecified and speech intelligibility was not separately reported.

mixed Parkinson diet and composite motor score — Appendix A lists both herbs in a multicomponent diet. Composite UPDRS III scores improved. The examination includes facial expression, but no item-level result, individual herb amount or preparation, or herb-specific contrast was reported.

Pinta sprout extract and rat melatonin biomarker — In Experiment 1, fasted rats given Pinta sprout extract had plasma melatonin about 16% higher than the chow control and 2.9 times the fasting group at 90 minutes. Neither sleep behavior nor insomnia was measured. The treatment was an extract from sprouted beans, with no boiled-pinto or Parkinson comparison.

student sleep-quality cross-section with legume preference — Table 2 OR 1.59 (95% CI 1.22 to 2.08) refers to dislike of grouped beans, chickpeas and lentils. The pooled rice, pasta or beans meal item cannot identify pinto or an isolated ingestion effect. The study does not test Parkinson insomnia.

parallel bean and sleep measures with fecal bacterial comparisons — Tables 3 and 4 compare fecal Akkermansia with sleep category and canary bean frequency separately. Supplement S1 names no pinto and gives no bean-by-sleep or preparation data. The older-adult cohort does not establish a Parkinson-specific insomnia effect.

uncontrolled kidney bean yogurt and sleep quality — The conference report and article describe one 17-person older-adult cohort. PSQI fell from 8.06 to 4.88 over two weeks without a control. The fermented kidney bean preparation, population and global sleep outcome differ from the frozen pinto and Parkinson claim.

whole MIND diet contrast and grouped bean score in diabetes — The sleep paper favors the diet assignment for adjusted PSQI. Companion reports concern grouped bean score, cardiometabolic markers and quality of life. All share one trial. Actual pinto-specific records and an ingredient-specific insomnia effect remain unverified.

registered pinto crossover with vascular and metabolic outcomes — The thesis describes boiled pinto consumption. The official registration lists phytochemical, arterial stiffness and satiety measures. The trial completed without posted results and does not register insomnia or enroll Parkinson participants.

PD pooled bean category and whole-diet insomnia association; no pinto exposure estimate — The cross-sectional whole-diet insomnia association does not identify boiled pinto consumption or its independent effect.

registered Mucuna and soybean beverage with planned sleep measure — The randomized comparison plans sleep-quality assessment in healthy adults. Each drink includes soybean and the active beverage adds Mucuna. No results are published, and neither genus or preparation matches boiled pinto beans.

canola-containing diet in shift workers with sleep-disturbance label — The registry lists melatonin and cardiometabolic endpoints without daytime sleepiness, verified refining grade or posted results.

canola oil supplement comparator and caregiver daytime sleepiness in preterm toddlers — The secondary sleepiness comparison between omega 3-6-9 and canola was imprecise. The trial used an unspecified-grade oil in toddlers and had no oil-free control.

canola oil in the low-fat menu and daytime sleepiness by diet — The ketogenic group improved more on the daytime sleepiness item. The low-fat plan names canola oil of unspecified grade, with no separate exposure estimate.

canola comparator and PSQI daytime dysfunction in healthy older adults — Preprint daytime component changes were +.09 canola versus +.08 ketone ester. The peer-reviewed report gives no clear PSQI or subdomain difference. No grade, oil-free arm, dedicated sleepiness result or PD cohort.

unspecified vegetable oil test food and no separately named daytime sleepiness outcome — Healthy adults compare test food with no test food. The public record gives no oil identity or separately specified daytime sleepiness, and no results are posted.
pharmaceutical compound and composite motor outcome — A retrospective adjunct study assessed motor scores. It did not test culinary celery or isolate the named symptom.

pharmaceutical adjunct and total UPDRS — Dai and colleagues reported lower total UPDRS under the pharmaceutical adjunct in Parkinson dementia. The accessible report gives no separate bradykinesia estimate.
pharmaceutical adjunct and total UPDRS — Liu and colleagues reported a favorable UPDRS total with the pharmaceutical adjunct. The public abstract gives no bradykinesia item.

whole dried celery methanolic extract in an MPTP motor model — Beam latency and grid-walk faults improved at some doses. The preparation was whole-plant extract and human bradykinesia was not measured.

synthetic drug adjunct with off-medication non-tremor motor subscore — Table II reports -7.14 +/- 5.81 versus +0.50 +/- 9.48 at week 24 (p < .001, n=43 and 60). This subscore combines bradykinesia, rigidity, speech, face, gait and other items. It gives no isolated bradykinesia or culinary celery leaf effect.
celery named in a Parkinson diet with composite bradykinesia-inclusive motor scale — No isolated celery arm, fresh leaf detail or separate bradykinesia change was published.
pharmaceutical compound and composite motor outcomes — Retrospective comparison found lower composite motor scores with the adjunct and reported no separate bradykinesia estimate.
pharmaceutical comparison and total UPDRS — Wang and colleagues compared butylphthalide with donepezil. Table 1 gives the UPDRS total without a bradykinesia item.

formulated thyme drop and perceived talking comfort — Half reported greater talking comfort with the drop versus 16.7% with placebo after vocal loading. No listener-rated intelligibility or Parkinson’s participants.

formulated thyme lozenge and voice measures — Subjective hoarseness and dryness improved while objective voice measures did not clearly change. The study did not measure listener-rated intelligibility.

patient- and physician-rated pain during diclofenac withdrawal — Table 2 assigns the 0.37-point physician pain change to fish oil. Corn oil shows +0.58 patient-rated (p=.007) and +0.47 physician-rated (p=.06) during diclofenac withdrawal. Between-oil changes were inconclusive; refining and Parkinson pain were unverified.

animal vehicle or flavored-milk preference outside the frozen preparation — PT080 and another member report injected corn oil as vehicle or control in a perimenopause model. The oil route, associated interventions and measures differ from oral corn oil.

corn-oil high-fat rodent comparison — Muscle molecular markers differ across high-fat oils. The active comparator and molecular outcome do not estimate an isolated refined corn oil and Parkinson endpoint effect.

separately numbered conference member with preparation or outcome limits — P-07.1-14 uses corn oil in controls of an acute malathion rat study. It measures liver markers and supplies no pain outcome or refined oil contrast.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — Corn oil is used in rat lipid comparisons, feeding paradigms and a toxicant vehicle. No Parkinson clinical endpoint was measured.

shared collection original source context — Carney 2009 combines sertraline with corn oil; other original or protocol records use different lipid mixtures and symptom scales. The review cannot isolate the oil or a Parkinson endpoint.
shared collection original source context — P210 compares EPA/DHA-enriched high-fat chow against corn-oil high-fat chow for muscle transcriptome and proteins. No separate frozen patient outcome.

corn oil as high-fat diet control and partial marine-lipid substitution — Corn oil was one base formulation, with and without different marine PUFA fractions. Adiposity and lipids were measured. The possibly overlapping article concerns the same broad research and a refined corn oil symptom effect is unresolved.

shared collection original source context — P233 is appended in the complete PMC HTML for this oral-key record and separately printed in the poster supplement. It compares corn and fish oil during shared exercise for strength and mechanistic outcomes. One study family.

shared collection original source context — Printed P233 reports an omega-3 versus corn-oil comparator during shared resistance training. Its strength findings are distinct from the frozen clinical outcomes. The other PMC key reproduces this member.

corn-oil control during exercise training — The final isometric interaction is p=.015 and the corn arm changed −1.4%. P233 uses −0.3%. Body strength during shared training does not measure any frozen Parkinson endpoint in these claims.
oral corn oil emulsion in Sjögren trial — The abstract reports no clear muscle or joint pain difference against gamma-linolenic acid. Both arms used active oils and the grade is unspecified.

locally instilled corn oil and colonoscopy procedure pain — Procedure pain favored adding oil as local lubricant. The route, cause of pain, and unspecified grade leave the frozen oral hypothesis unresolved.
corn oil as a shared carrier — Physical discomfort did not clearly differ. The trial had no independent oil or pain-specific contrast.

oral corn oil comparator, osteoarthritis pain trial — VAS and WOMAC comparisons were inconclusive. The oil arm averaged 4.5 to 4.6 on VAS. There was no oil-free control and no specification of refining grade.

separate gastrointestinal conference member and ingredient context — A tumor experiment incorporates corn oil in control or combined diets involving EPA and aspirin. The study does not assign the frozen preparation and clinical endpoint.

injected bromelain and rat stepping and forelimb movement — Pretreatment improved rat motor performance without clear dopamine preservation. The enzyme was injected. Raw pineapple and clinical dexterity were untested.

mixed Parkinson diet with pineapple and composite motor examination — The diet lists pineapple and the composite motor examination contains finger and hand tasks. No pineapple intake, preparation, arm or individual hand-item result was reported.
