mixed garden produce distribution — The garden reported distribution of green beans, kale, chard and watermelon within a mixed harvest. The evaluation concerns program delivery without an ingredient-specific intake or clinical symptom measurement.

oral safflower crossover and standing stability in Friedreich ataxia — Timed static stability was largely unchanged and had no significant comparative effect. Cold-press grade and Parkinson-specific reactive balance are unverified.

safflower oil and Huntington tandem and retropulsion scale components — The scale contains relevant balance items. The publication gives no separate comparative outcomes and the oil processing method is unknown.
safflower comparator and standing balance in older adults — All participants attained the maximum time for three balance positions, so the measure could not discriminate change at that level.
standing-balance component in a sarcopenia safflower trial — Balance is a planned test component with no posted results. The registry avoids movement-limiting neurological disease.
exact baked food in one anaphylaxis case — The case describes an acute allergic reaction with respiratory and circulatory symptoms. Olfaction was unmeasured.
eggplant extract in a rotenone cell model — Cell survival and oxidative measures cannot establish baked eggplant's effect on an olfactory symptom.
Parkinson handwriting diary during broccoli and mustard tea — The illustrative handwriting rating remained 1 in Table 1. Letter size, toasted seed and a mustard-only effect were not measured.

cold-pressed walnut kernel oil in a mouse demyelinating disease model — Eight mice per group. Reported disease scores were 2.38 versus 3.00 with saline, with unclear averaging window. The scale rates weakness, paralysis and death. Dystonia and Parkinson disease were not tested.
cold-pressed walnut oil in a rotenone fly model — Oil with rotenone improved fly climbing compared with rotenone alone; this is not human dystonia severity.

cold-pressed walnut oil in rotenone-treated cell cultures — Viability and oxidative measures varied by preparation concentration and time. Cell viability and fly climbing come from separate experiments. Neither measures dystonia after walnut oil consumption.

encapsulated black pepper and Bunium persicum formulation and an unquantified concentration result — The primary abstract reports reduced impaired concentration in the active group. The item-level assessment and arm contrast remain unverified. The Alzheimer trial combined powdered ingredients and does not isolate cracked pepper.

mixed bark and pepper extracts with a planned timed working-memory task — Registry plans Numeric Working Memory and Cognitive Failures Questionnaire scores in mild cognitive impairment with insulin resistance. Capsule instructions conflict. No posted results or isolated pepper arm.

turmeric with black pepper and timed cognitive tests — Both groups receive a multidomain program, with turmeric plus pepper or placebo. Registered measures include Trail Making and Digit Symbol. The protocol supplies no results, standalone pepper contrast or verified culinary preparation.

oral isolated piperine and two spatial memory outcomes in an AF64A rat model — Original Results 3.1 and Figs. 1–2 report improved escape latency and retention across piperine doses against the injury vehicle group (p<.001). The preparation, species, experimental injury and spatial tasks leave culinary pepper and sustained attention in Parkinson disease unresolved.

five-ingredient extract cocktail and spatial attention in aged dogs — Variable-distance landmark errors favored the cocktail in 7 treated and 6 placebo dogs. Pepper was present as a standardized extract and the tested combination supplies no separate pepper estimate.

oral dried black pepper fruit and validated sustained attention performance — 40 young completers took pepper fruit 2 g or rice flour in crossover. Primary reaction time means moved in opposite directions, with all cognitive condition-by-time comparisons p>.05. Cracked preparation and PD unmeasured.

oral isolated piperine added to resveratrol and digit vigilance — 23 healthy adults in three-way crossover. No significant cognitive-task effect. Combination altered cerebral blood flow. No peppercorn or PD exposure contrast.

injected isolated piperine with distinct dose and timing contrasts in an STZ rat radial-arm task — At 2.5 mg/kg after injury, the original report shows 1.66 versus 5.66 mean reference errors (p<.05). Higher post-treatment doses did not significantly alter those errors, and selected comparisons favored other arms against the 5 mg/kg pretreatment group. The rat memory findings leave the frozen exposure and attention outcome open.

four botanicals with honey and memory after experimental hypothyroidism — Author abstract reports better spatial and avoidance memory in treated rats. Details and exact contrasts remain unavailable. It does not isolate the pepper, verify the preparation or measure attention in Parkinson disease.

cold-pressed pepper oil in rat memory and uncertain comparator provenance — Maze and avoidance memory effects are reported. The earlier Bombax paper has matching comparator percentages and is cited in figures, leaving comparison independence unclear. No sustained-attention outcome or cracked culinary pepper comparison.

dried black pepper fruit as one of three botanicals and total MoCA in MCI — 40 randomized and 38 completed. Month-3 total MoCA contrast −0.207 (95% CI −1.96 to 1.54), p=.817. No separate attention subscore, cracked pepper contrast or identified PD subgroup.

inhaled essential oil during a cognitive stressor — 20 men with no identified PD group. No significant arithmetic performance difference. Autonomic stress response and perceived concentration do not establish the claimed effect of ingestion.

concentrated ethanolic pepper fruit extract and spatial memory in mice — After experimental sleep interruption, a concentrated extract group spent more time in the former platform quadrant. Crossing counts gave no clear contrast in the report. One control description differs in the figure context. No sustained attention task, culinary dose or Parkinson cohort.

whole almond chewing and stimulated salivary flow outside Parkinson disease — Table 3 reported mean salivary-flow increases of 0.21 mL/min in caries-free and 0.17 in carious participants after chewing whole almonds, compared with 0.43 and 0.30 after chewing wax gum. Mechanical stimulation, oral whole almonds, salivary flow and drooling severity are distinct exposures and endpoints.

almond-oil dentifrice and stimulated salivary flow in adolescent brushing — In 80 young men brushing for 28 days, almond-oil dentifrice and low-abrasive dentifrice did not differ significantly in stimulated salivary flow. Oral topical dentifrice is a different preparation and route from swallowing cold-pressed oil. No Parkinson population or drooling rate was measured.

oral aqueous bay leaf extract and locomotion in an intoxication model — Open-field distance and duration increased against the ethanol control. General locomotion, acute intoxication and extracted leaves limit relevance to walking slowness.
Parkinson model after injectable leaf hexane fraction — The rat model reports histological preservation and the cell model measured cellular outcomes. It provides no gait speed.
essential oil and motor impairment in mice — Mouse seizure work reports motor impairment under essential oil. No walking-speed result was reported.
inhaled whole leaf and animal exploratory activity — A scopolamine experiment reported altered Y-maze entry counts with incense. It measured exploratory activity and no walking speed in Parkinson’s.
enriched oil and rat hang and ladder performance — Enriched oil groups performed better in hang and ladder tests. These do not give community fall frequency, and there was no plain oil arm.

sunflower oil comparator and fatigue in NAFLD — The 12-week trial reported fatigue improvement in the sesame arm relative to the sunflower comparator during a hypocaloric diet. The same-cohort companion identifies both oils as refined and odorless. Arm-specific sunflower values remain unavailable in the mood abstract.

sunflower food frequency and composite Parkinson symptom burden — The poster reports +2 total PRO-PD points per intake frequency category (95% CI −10 to 13, p=.787). The cross-sectional exposure did not specify an oil grade. It gives no individual fatigue estimate.
pooled vegetable cooking oils and Parkinson fatigue — Positive plotted sign, with sunflower pooled with safflower, canola and vegetable oil. No oil-specific sign, coefficient or interval.

sunflower oil comparator and fatigue ratings after prostatectomy — Fatigue Symptom Inventory severity was 8.3 at baseline and 8.0 at 12 months in the sunflower group. There was no clear treatment-by-time interaction for this measure. The trial used high-oleic capsules, reported no oil grade and had no no-oil group or Parkinson cohort.

high-oleic sunflower meal crossover and premeal or late fatigue assessment — Registry specifies premeal and follow-up MFSI-SF and has no posted results. The related published postmeal experiment analyzed attention. Oil refining is unclear.

separately numbered conference member with preparation or outcome limits — P-04.3-06 lists sunflower oil in a reference casein diet for animal toxicology. No refined oil effect or fatigue outcome is isolated in the proposed diet substitution.

sunflower oil original source context — Included depression families use sunflower oil with a small fish-oil admixture. The Australian registration planned a sunflower comparator. Review entries do not provide a separate oil effect or executive comparison.

sunflower oil original source context — PO2.161 lists refined sunflower oil in a mixed adolescent diet survey and gives no oil-specific IQ estimate. PO2.229 includes sunflower oil in a calorie-plus-probiotic menu and measures body composition.

sunflower oil original source context — Reference 79 traces emulsified and nonemulsified sunflower oil in the same rat metabolic study. Endotoxemia and triglycerides do not measure the frozen clinical outcome.
high-oleic sunflower oil in mouse feed and adipose gene expression — The report evaluates gene expression by age and diet duration. It offers no culinary grade or Parkinson symptom estimate.

sunflower oil original source context — P169 appears in the complete PMC HTML for the oral record and separately in the printed poster supplement. The original oral PDF omits it. This is a duplicate sunflower capsule exposure family, with no separate oral-section result.

sunflower oil original source context — P169 reports similarly measured sedentary time and steps for resistance-exercise groups with sunflower or fish oil capsules. The oil pressing grade is unspecified, no separate Parkinson outcome, and one comparison family with the duplicated HTML.

physical performance and resistance training in sarcopenia — Groups performed the same resistance exercise. Fish oil produced larger torque and six-minute walk improvements than sunflower oil; no isolated refined-oil fatigue rating.

sunflower oil comparator and symptoms in chronic fatigue syndrome — Fifty adults were assigned to essential fatty acids or a sunflower-oil comparator. The trial found no clear physical-symptom difference. Comparator identity comes from a university study extraction. There was no oil-free arm or Parkinson cohort.

oral high-oleic sunflower comparator and local muscle fatigability — Eight weeks of sunflower oil versus conjugated linoleic acid gave no clear treatment difference in handgrip fatigue. The study measured local fatigability and did not measure Parkinson fatigue or verify refining grade.

ground seed in an external fumigation blend and a pediatric communication scale — The uncontrolled program included ground nigella in a fumigation blend. A communication subscore was higher, with an invalid printed probability. It supplies no isolated nigella consumption or measured Parkinson speech intelligibility.

qualitative OFF-time report after a high-fat Parkinson meal — One participant described prolonged OFF after a high-fat meal. The interview did not identify a grapeseed-oil exposure or quantify daily OFF time. The other intervention used coconut-derived MCT.

mixed breakfast and levodopa pharmacokinetics in healthy adults — High-fat breakfast delayed the initial levodopa rise by 1–2 hours, lowered peak concentration 21% and increased total estimated exposure 13% versus fasting. The mixed breakfast used butter and provided no grapeseed oil comparison or Parkinson OFF diary.

powdered rosemary leaf infusion and resting pressure outside Parkinson disease — Pressure declined over time in the grade 1 hypertension group. Both cohorts took the infusion. No orthostatic symptoms were assessed.
inhaled rosemary oil and autonomic measures in healthy adults — Heart rate increased in the rosemary group. The study did not evaluate symptomatic pressure change on standing.

inhaled rosemary oil and acute pressure in healthy adults — Resting systolic and diastolic pressure increased in an acute comparison. The fresh culinary route and clinical orthostatic lightheadedness were unmeasured.

rosemary essential oil and pressure in primary hypotension — Pressure rose during treatment in a 32-person cohort with primary hypotension. The report does not establish an effect on lightheadedness on standing.

oral dry rosemary extract and resting pressure in nursing staff — Resting pressure declined by about 4 mm Hg in each measure among 36 completers. The thesis and papers share a cohort and the study is uncontrolled.

earlier dissertation in probable primary-hypotension cohort lineage — The thesis abstract describes pressure reversal with treatment withdrawal. The reported sample differs from the later article, and standing-triggered symptoms were not isolated. Count as companion evidence pending participant reconciliation.

processed seed-derived glucoraphanin; registered nonmotor and sleep scales — A PD arm is assigned bioactivated glucoraphanin, not steamed kale leaves. A companion cell paper identifies seed extracts intended for the trial; no participant outcomes or dream-enactment frequency results are posted.

Parkinson testimonial; kale possible juice ingredient — A Parkinson participant reported improved sleep and no longer screaming at night after a combined program. Her kale intake, steamed preparation, dream enactment and event counts were unreported.

ethanolic whole-plant lemon balm extract and motor endpoints in MPTP mice — Original Tables III and IV give longer rotarod latency and more locomotor activity in the highest extract group versus the MPTP model. The lowest dose contrasts are inconclusive and the reported group size is internally inconsistent. The study tests an extracted dried whole plant and supplies no freezing episode measurement.

hydrodistilled lemon balm oil and healthy-mouse rotarod — Figure 4 shows shorter latency in the highest oil group. The Results prose gives a conflicting direction. The endpoint is rotarod coordination.
cinnamon twig decoction in a patent disclosure — Patent reports symptom frequencies under a multi-component regimen. A culinary cinnamon effect was not isolated.

cinnamon flavor gum and baseline compared with chewing saliva rates — Cinnamon-flavored gum co-occurred with increased salivary flow during chewing. Gum without flavor and ground cinnamon intake were not compared.

isolated cinnamaldehyde mouth rinse versus vehicle and salivary flow — Cinnamaldehyde provided no clear incremental flow above vehicle. Increased flow from baseline occurred in both conditions. Clinical drooling was unmeasured.

shrimp listed before and during a mixed diet in a schizoaffective case — The initial case describes auditory and visual hallucinations and later global resolution at six weeks. It gives neither distinct visual frequency follow-up nor shrimp preparation or a separate exposure effect.

different mint species essential oil and controlled daytime Epworth comparison — The adjusted between-group estimate spans improvement and worsening. It is specific to peppermint oil in hypertension, not brewed spearmint.

spearmint-flavored gum, gum base and no chewing — Reported alertness changed with chewing without a detected flavor-specific effect. There was no brewed exposure or Parkinson daytime sleepiness scale.
aqueous spearmint extract and pentobarbital-induced sleep — Drug-induced sleeping time increased. The study gives no measurement of waking sleepiness in people with Parkinson’s.
spearmint and green tea extract blend and morning sleepiness — Morning-sleepiness comparison spanned zero. The population did not have Parkinson’s and the intervention was not brewed spearmint.
steamed sprouts compared with raw and boiled sprouts — The study measures glucosinolates and volatile composition. There is no ingestion or dyskinesia measure.
analytical sulforaphane in steamed Brussels sprouts — Measured sulforaphane varies with steaming time. The food profile is separate from injected-compound outcome experiments.

indexed injected sulforaphane with mouse levodopa-induced dyskinesia and separate transgenic groups — The indexed abstract contains an indirect directional lead. Original thesis results are needed to verify the drug-treated wild-type comparison and the timing separately from the transgenic comparisons.

sulforaphane capsules with cognitive and clinical composite outcomes — Official November 16, 2026 recheck reports unknown recruitment status and no results. There is no steamed Brussels sprout arm or specifically registered dyskinesia outcome.
Brussels sprout fiber tested with Parkinson-derived fecal samples — Ex vivo SCFA comparison. No sprouts were administered to participants and no dyskinesia outcome was measured.

isolated sulforaphane and motility in Parkinson-model nematodes — Thrashing rate increased in the model. This motility proxy and isolated compound differ from levodopa-related dyskinesia and steamed sprouts.

acute drooling during suspected seed allergy in a child — The author preprint reports excess drooling during an acute allergic reaction to a mixed snack containing watermelon seed paste. Previous flesh was tolerated and the suspected culprit lacks challenge confirmation. The clinical context and preparation do not establish a Parkinson symptom effect.
watermelon-flavored gum and salivary flow during mastication — Saliva output rose during chewing for all five flavors. Fruit material was unverified and drooling was not measured.

mixed garden produce distribution — The garden reported distribution of green beans, kale, chard and watermelon within a mixed harvest. The evaluation concerns program delivery without an ingredient-specific intake or clinical symptom measurement.
watermelon and acute oropharyngeal reactions in an allergy-selected group — The case group was selected for watermelon sensitivity. The report gives no separate drooling severity or Parkinson result.
Parkinson diet menu includes parsley and a motor scale composite — UPDRS Part III and individual total changes do not isolate handwriting, letter size or actual dried parsley intake.

Dried powdered parsley leaves administered in a controlled human kinetics study — The intervention verifies oral dried leaves and a plasma exposure timeline. There was no Parkinson cohort or handwriting outcome.

ground sumac powder with discrepant spontaneous drowsiness reports — The narrative records one drowsiness event with sumac and Table 3 lists none. No daytime sleepiness instrument or Parkinson population.

fermented unpolished rice germ GABA and PSG REM share and latency — Four-week trial reported no clear REM share or latency interaction. General sleep latency improved. Dream enactment and REM tone were not measured.

oral rice bran extract and PSG REM share and latency — REM share changes +1.4 versus +0.5 percentage points (adjusted p=.450). REM latency was also inconclusive. No dream enactment, steamed grain or Parkinson cohort.
lower-dose unpolished rice germ GABA and PSG REM share — The differential REM share change was p=.9173. Periodic limb movements were also inconclusive (p=.9442). Neither measures dream enactment.

fermented rice germ and EEG stages in pentobarbital-treated rats — Ye and colleagues orally gave GABA-rich fermented rice-germ material to pentobarbital-treated rats and assessed EEG-defined sleep states. Figure 3 reports reduced wake time and more NREM sleep under the extract conditions. The highlighted REM increase compares pentobarbital-treated controls with untreated rats. The report gives no extract-related REM-atonia or observed dream-enactment estimate. It used germ...

brown rice protein hydrolysate and wearable REM duration estimates — An exploratory subset reported a largest change contrast of 11.63 minutes of wearable-estimated REM, with no clear group differences. No dream enactment, REM tone, steamed grain or Parkinson comparison.

consumed hazelnut oil in an older-adult feeding pilot and psychiatric screening — Twelve were randomized and ten completed. The high-oleic supplement was all hazelnut oil and the control blend also contained it. Depression and anxiety were recorded at screening. There was no reported hallucination monitoring or symptom attribution for the nonspecified medical withdrawal. No Parkinson cohort or verified pressing grade.

whole or blended canned lentils and three-hour anxiety ratings — Anxiety grouped with unfavorable mood time-course descriptions. AUC main and interaction effects inconclusive. No exact anxiety estimate, no Parkinson cohort.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — P1018 measures lentil sensitization in eosinophilic esophagitis. The exposure of the sedation cohort is intravenous propofol and no lentil feeding or Parkinson outcome is measured.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The low-purine diet definition lists lentils among foods limited in dietary management of canine urate or xanthine stones. It gives no standalone lentil comparison.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — ABS341 measures lentil seed protein fibril morphology by extraction pH, with no consumed lentils or patient endpoint.

pooled legume or bean intake and whole-diet anxiety scores — Table 2 reports anxiety against whole diet scores. Table S4 evaluates pooled bean or legume intake against aggregate symptom burden and does not identify species or preparation.
oral fruit methanol extract and mouse bar test — Less imposed catalepsy is a motor signal. Spontaneous dystonic contractions and clinical dystonia severity were not measured.
roasting chemistry only — Analytical roasting data establish preparation-dependent exposure. The direction of clinical dystonia remains open.

low-fat mixed diet includes nutmeg in a baked recipe; aggregate motor exam — The total exam includes facial expression, but no separate facial result or nutmeg effect is reported; preparation and intake are unverified.

visual hallucination case with multiple supplements including a labelled holy basil extract blend — The patient stopped five supplements while starting psychiatric treatment. The case does not isolate holy basil, use fresh sweet basil, count visual hallucination frequency, or involve diagnosed Parkinson disease.

sweet basil infusion in a survey of psychiatric outpatients with psychosis in remission — The only basil user reported using it for anxiety. A reported symptom change is neither a visual hallucination frequency estimate nor Parkinson evidence.

fresh basil recipes in both arms of a Parkinson diet pilot; one visual hallucination case — The case resolved after pramipexole reduction. Its basil consumption and hallucination frequency are unreported, and the comparison changes multiple foods.

combined rosemary and daylily trial with dream complaints among enrollment options — Bad dreams were considered only at eligibility. Reported outcomes give no dream enactment or rosemary-specific contrast.
oral rosemary capsules and subjective sleep quality in university students — Self-reported sleep quality and dream enactment measure different outcomes. The trial enrolled students.
rosemary hydrosol and chemically induced rat insomnia — The study measured sleep and serotonergic endpoints in a rat model. It gives no REM-related dream enactment data.
dry rosemary extract and subjective sleep in nursing staff — Subjective sleep improved in a single-group cohort. The thesis and papers are the same study and give no dream-enactment count.

allowable spearmint in a combined intervention with Parkinson testimonials — Protocol allows spearmint and case descriptions discuss medication and mobility. Individual intake, fresh preparation, a timed OFF diary and a separate spearmint arm are unavailable.

mixed-meal challenge in Parkinson autonomic failure — Measured pressure while seated with feet elevated and reported mixed-meal macronutrients. The protocol did not isolate baked turkey or orthostatic symptoms.

post-meal supine and standing blood pressure in Parkinson disease — Supine pressure fell after lunch and the orthostatic pressure drop was smaller after the meal. Neither baked turkey nor a lightheadedness score was identified.
turkey and chicken ingestion allergy cases — Cross-reactive IgE and ingestion history concern allergy. Preparation and Parkinson-related orthostatic lightheadedness are unresolved.
injected fresh celery leaf fractions in mice — The fractions lengthened drug-induced sleep, and the study did not measure waking sleepiness after eating fresh leaves.

randomized dry celery extract before bedtime with planned global sleep score — The original bilingual registry reports recruitment complete and global PSQI, without posted results or an isolated daytime effect. Plant part and culinary transfer are unverified.

lovage in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome — The menu lists lovage and the motor examination includes speech. The paper does not establish dried leaf exposure or report individual speech intelligibility change.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — P1018 describes intravenous soybean oil in propofol or Intralipid and P1121 compares intragastric soy milk with cow milk. These are distinct preparations and neither tests culinary soybean oil in Parkinson disease.
soybean oil versus butter and measured gastric retention — The report gives an inconclusive 90-minute gastric retention difference in dyspepsia. Neither oil-free control nor Parkinson OFF diary.
ground soybean and acute levodopa on-period — Ground soybeans given with levodopa and carbidopa prolonged the acute on-period. Refined oil and daily off time were unmeasured.

Parkinson recorded OFF time and levodopa in water — The same patent and registry cohort used an aqueous dispersion. Soybean oil appears only in a generic possible ingredient list and was not administered. OFF result concerns an eight-hour window.
soybean emulsion and early emptying after vagotomy — Short-term gastric emptying decreased versus water after surgery. Daily OFF and Parkinson disease unmeasured.

Parkinson OFF time after intraoral levodopa in medium-chain triglyceride paste — The separate open study used Miglyol 812 N, not soybean oil. Drug schedule and delivery changed concurrently. The comparison cannot assign a culinary oil effect.
soybean oil as a dietary comparator for perilla or fish oil in mice — The model uses 5% soybean oil control chow, different treatment oils and dosage, and no participant or daily OFF measure.

oral soybean-oil meal and gastric emptying in non-Parkinson participants — Oil delayed emptying by about 50%. Lack of clinical OFF timing, refining grade, medication or Parkinson cohort limits this to physiological context.

standard meal timing and controlled-release levodopa pharmacokinetics in Parkinson disease — Drug absorption was delayed after the standard meal. Oil identity and a daily OFF diary were unavailable; this cannot combine with an unrelated gastric study to establish an oil effect.

separate gastrointestinal conference member and ingredient context — P0635 groups recipients by intravenous soybean or other lipid emulsion. A different member reports soybean sensitization. Neither uses the frozen culinary preparation or Parkinson outcome.

analytical composition of press extracted walnut oil — The analysis verifies ALA is retained in cold-pressed walnut oil. Chemical similarity by one constituent does not identify the trial grade or clinical direction.

whole walnut dietary intervention and academic stress anxiety measures — The study measures anxiety domains in an examination context. Time trends and the whole-food exposure cannot isolate cold-pressed oil or motor-disease anxiety.

whole walnut bread randomized crossover with tension anxiety subscale — The two sex strata had opposite point estimates and no conclusive anxiety comparison. The intervention contains walnuts rather than an isolated cold-pressed oil.

whole walnut crossover and significant total mood disturbance difference — Total mood favored whole walnuts. Primary item-level anxiety, culinary oil equivalence and Parkinson transfer are unverified.

oral walnut oil and experimentally learned fear — The author abstract reports faster extinction of learned fear. The secondary acute Total Mood Disturbance difference was -4.99 (95% CI -10.75 to +0.07). The recovered supplement has no POMS component scores, and the original body, clinical symptom measure and oil processing remain open.

walnut oil within an oral placebo blend and measured anxiety in fibromyalgia — HADS anxiety means were 9.40 and 9.60 before and after the MCT, walnut and avocado placebo. The comparison was inconclusive. The trial cannot isolate walnut oil, its processing grade or clinical Parkinson anxiety.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — Sesame oil acts as an injected vehicle in rat corticosteroid or AF64A experiments, with no oral oil comparison.
original source context with different preparation, outcome, attribution or population — The experiment uses an injected sesame-oil vehicle. It does not measure falls or a toasted culinary exposure.

shared sesame oil vehicle and reported falls in Parkinson disease — Falls were reported in 4 of 31 cannabinoid recipients and 3 of 30 placebo recipients. Both arms used oil and the processing grade is unknown.
sesame oil and rotarod performance in manganese-exposed rats — Model locomotion and rotarod performance improved. This assay did not measure falls in people or identify toasted oil.

tongue-surface capsaicin and human tongue-movement task — Healthy volunteers performed worse in a tongue-protrusion task under capsaicin cream than vehicle. Speech intelligibility and smoked paprika consumption were untested.

intraoral capsaicin and human tongue force tracking — Pain during the isolated compound experiment reduced gains in tongue force tracking. There was neither spoken intelligibility testing nor ingested paprika.

nebulized capsaicin and clinician-rated wet voice after stroke — Wet voice improved during some sessions in an uncontrolled post-stroke dysphagia case. The report used inhalation and qualitative wet voice, with no test of intelligibility.
whole salmon versus meat and daytime function — Different fish, preparation and nighttime sleep or daytime-function outcomes. No Epworth sleepiness measure or grilled trout exposure.

other whole oily fish and childhood sleep — Herring and mackerel meals did not clearly affect parent-reported sleep in preschool children. The outcome was nighttime sleep and no trout or Parkinson exposure was tested.
fish oil and Parkinson daytime sleepiness — After eight weeks in 37 completers, fish oil versus mineral oil was inconclusive on the Epworth Sleepiness Scale. Fish species was unspecified.

consumed hazelnut oil and scheduled urine sampling — The 12-person study scheduled hourly voiding after exposure and reports only pooled urine output and contaminant excretion. The oil was contaminant-rich and the study gives no pressing or roasting history or urgency measure.

cold-pressed seed oil and pole descent in rotenone mice — Two higher seed oil diets shortened mean pole descent time relative to rotenone controls. Seed oil and mouse movement do not identify a clinical effect of fresh leaves.

purified perillaldehyde and movement timing in Parkinson mouse models — The paper reports improvements in pole and beam times in the toxin models. The lower level had no clear effect on two timing measures in the 6-OHDA model. No fresh leaf or human bradykinesia outcome was tested.

basil seed extract and working memory in mice — The authors reported improved Y-maze and other memory tasks in a haloperidol amnesia model. The seed extract differs from dried leaves, and the experiment did not measure Parkinson executive function.

fresh leaf homogenate in oven-dried chow and memory tasks in aged mice — Aged supplemented mice performed better on object recognition. The water-maze comparison reached nominal significance only in a subset reaching the platform, with no clear all-animal difference. The final chow was oven-dried after fresh leaves were incorporated. The study did not test dried culinary leaf or Parkinson executive function.

cumin seed extract and rat cystitis and bladder strip response — Inflammation, nociception and ex vivo muscle tone changed. The administration route and voiding comparisons need primary full-text verification.

Parkinson survey recording cumin use with aggregate nonmotor measures — Cumin intake was recorded and exploratory nonmotor comparisons were inconclusive after correction. No preparation or cumin-specific urinary urgency estimate is reported.

cold-pressed hazelnut oil and pentobarbital sleep duration in liver-injured mice — Pentobarbital sleep was 8.8 and 10.6 min with oral hazelnut oil in the injured mice, versus 14.9 and 21.5 min with injury alone. The study measured a hepatic drug-response proxy. It tested no spontaneous insomnia, toasted oil or Parkinson cohort.

fresh basil listed in both arms of a Parkinson diet trial with a daytime sleepiness item — The ketogenic arm had a reported 0.45-point greater item reduction. Intake is unreported and the contrast is between diets, so neither the cause nor an independent basil direction is established.

air from living sweet basil and essential-oil inhalation in mice; spontaneous locomotion outcome — Lower activity followed exposure to headspace from nine plants. Inhalation, locomotion and healthy mice do not match eating fresh basil and Parkinson daytime sleepiness.

shared collection original source context — PO1.165 summarizes genuine quinoa, rice and quinoa-flake comparisons for intake, satiety and metabolic markers. No Parkinson gait or rigidity result is shown.
red quinoa ethanol extract and preclinical motor outcomes — The fly experiment assessed survival, climbing, crossings and memory. There was no culinary quinoa exposure or muscle rigidity measurement.

suspected injected rice-bran oil and acute altered consciousness — Single acute fat embolism case describes apathetic consciousness. Injected material identity and refining are unconfirmed. Clinical Parkinson apathy after food oil was not measured.

rice bran extract and depressive symptom scales — A non-Parkinson adult trial of rice bran extract reported lower per-protocol PHQ-9 at eight weeks. No dedicated apathy measure or refined rice bran oil intervention.

registered combination spray containing eugenol and planned saliva flow — The combined spray and mint-water comparator do not isolate eugenol. The primary outcome is secreted saliva rather than clinical drooling. Registry results were absent.
nasal eugenol spray and salivary secretion — No clear eugenol salivary-flow increase in 12 healthy adults. Drooling, Parkinson’s and ground clove ingestion were untested.
nasal eugenol inhaler and salivary secretion — Paired salivary flow and stretchiness changes were inconclusive in 12 healthy adults. Cohort overlap with the spray study is unverified.
Matched cultural or experiential record for clove and drooling severity; preserves community/traditional context without controlled efficacy weight.
raw romaine meal in healthy adults — No dyskinesia outcome was assessed.
red lettuce microgreen extract in a Parkinson fly model — Improved climbing is distinct from dyskinesia, and the cultivar was not verified as romaine.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — P1473 reports improvement of pediatric orofacial granulomatosis on elemental feeding followed by a diet avoiding both cinnamon and benzoates. It does not separate cinnamon from the other dietary changes.
cinnamon-containing Kampo formula and apathy in an uncontrolled dementia pilot — Apathy improved from baseline in a 20-person open pilot. The formula and population differ from the frozen claim.
cinnamon consumption and mood-apathy domain in a Parkinson survey — The report gives no estimate for cinnamon and the individual apathy item.
cinnamon-containing Kampo and NPI apathy — Median NPI apathy remained zero at week 24 in an uncontrolled cohort. Baseline floor and mixed treatment prevent cinnamon-specific inference.
cinnamon-containing Kampo formula and apathy in Alzheimer or Lewy body dementia — Apathy improved within the active arm but the between-group comparison was inconclusive. No separate cinnamon arm.

oral perilla leaf extract and rat REM and NREM duration — The rat EEG experiment found no clear duration difference in either stage separately. REM duration is not dream enactment and the experiment did not use a Parkinson model.
marjoram infusion and composite nonmotor symptom score — The tea arm improved on aggregate NMSS. No separate urinary urgency comparison or fresh-leaf exposure was verified.

oral cold-pressed avocado oil and open-field crossings in obese mice — Figure 3B does not mark a clear direct effect on crossings with oil. Crossing counts measure activity, not walking speed, and the mice did not have parkinsonism.

maternal oral avocado oil and offspring open-field activity — Adult offspring in the oil arm showed lower overall locomotion. Maternal exposure, unverified oil processing and the animal activity outcome do not establish clinical walking slowness.

oral avocado oil and movement asymmetry in a Huntington model — A matching conference report recorded roughly 89% fewer ipsilateral turns in lesioned rats. The exposure's pressing method and clinical walking-speed effect are unresolved.

summer savory topical gel and dental outcomes — The original placebo comparison measures palatal erythema and Candida, without a recorded acoustic volume outcome, Parkinson cohort or ingestion of fresh savory.

flaxseed oil in an omega-3-adequate rat diet and odor discrimination — Second-generation rats on the deficient diet made more errors in two-odor learning than rats receiving the flaxseed-oil-containing diet. The result tests developmental omega-3 adequacy without a Parkinson population or documented cold-pressing.

ALA-varied developmental diets and olfactory behavior in mice — The lower-ALA blend reduced electroolfactogram amplitudes but did not clearly change olfactory behavior. The blends did not include flaxseed oil and the mice had no Parkinson model.

EPA and DHA with olfactory training and postviral odor threshold — Odor threshold favored adding long-chain omega-3 to training. The product does not test alpha-linolenic acid or cold-pressed flaxseed oil.
turmeric-containing formula and speech fluency — A combined Parkinson granule improved a secondary nonfluent speech rating. It did not isolate ground turmeric or measure acoustic volume.
nanomicelle curcumin and composite Parkinson scale — The accessible MDS-UPDRS results do not separate speech from other motor findings. Acoustic loudness was not reported.
reported use of turmeric products for voice care — The survey records turmeric use among 69 of 253 responding herbal users. It gives no ground specification or acoustic voice-volume change.

oral mustard rice and short-term whole-saliva collection in healthy volunteers — Author abstract reports approximately fourfold fasting secretion with mustard rice versus threefold with unspiced rice in five participants. Exact mustard form and Parkinson drooling outcomes are unavailable.

unstimulated salivary flow in Parkinson disease without a food intervention — Parkinson participants had reduced unstimulated secretion compared with matched controls. Salivary flow and patient complaints about excess saliva do not provide a food-specific drooling result.

rat salivary secretion after perfusion of a mustard constituent — Arterial allyl isothiocyanate reduced carbachol-induced saliva secretion in the rat preparation. Drooling severity after dietary mustard and Parkinson disease were not studied.

injected thyme extract in a rat brain ischemia balance test — Two extract doses improved rotarod balance in the reported comparison. No dried culinary leaf, oral exposure or Parkinson postural-instability assessment.

isolated carvacrol and coordination tasks in lesioned rats — Published July 2019 online. The study reports motor task improvement after carvacrol in 6-OHDA rats. Clinical postural instability after dried thyme was untested.

isolated thymol injection and rat motor tasks — Rotarod retention was inconclusive, with greater distance in one test setting. The experiment did not test culinary thyme or clinical postural instability.

thyme extract and coordination tests in paraquat mice — Ladder, footprint and wire-hanging tests were included in the reported broad behavioral improvement. Task-specific contrasts and clinical postural instability were not reported in the public abstract.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S7.478 orally administers oat-stem lignin to irradiated mice and S6.415 studies oat seed germination. Neither is a prepared oat-grain or Parkinson motor comparison.
oatmeal and total Parkinson symptom burden — The aggregate estimate is inconclusive and apathy severity was not analyzed against oatmeal alone.
diet-pattern scores and measured Parkinson apathy — The cross-sectional study did not report a significant apathy association or isolate an oat item.

meal timing and Parkinson levodopa concentration variability — With and without lunch differed in levodopa concentration variability in ten people with Parkinson disease. The meal data supply no sumac attribution or diary-based daily OFF duration.
sumac extract applied to Parkinson donor skin cells — No oral exposure, levodopa coadministration or medication-state outcome was included.
marjoram infusion and composite nonmotor symptom score — The tea arm improved on aggregate NMSS. No separate drooling comparison or fresh-leaf exposure was verified.

mixed fermented garlic and ginger capsules using grapeseed oil — The filing reports combined diarrhea-and-constipation improvement among 27 adult respondents. Oil processing, separate constipation change and controlled attribution were absent.

grapeseed oil enema and colon tissue injury in rats — Microscopic lesion score was 0.88 after grapeseed oil enema and 2.67 in untreated colitis. Bowel frequency and constipation were unreported, and the oil route was rectal.

oral combined grapeseed oil carrier and colitis stool composite — The carbon-60 and grapeseed oil combination lowered a disease activity composite containing loose-stool and bleeding scores (p < .05). The study had no oil-only arm or constipation outcome.

chives on a Parkinson pilot diet menu and composite motor score — The Appendix A menu names chives and the pilot reports changes in UPDRS III. It gives neither chive preparation nor an ingredient-specific stride measure.

fermented red cabbage blend and DASS depression in healthy adults — No between-group DASS depression difference (p=.607). Within-group stress and total scores improved. Product also contained beetroot and caraway and was fermented.

repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking — Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.
oral red cabbage anthocyanin extract in aging mice — Cognitive benefit reported; depression was not measured. Exposure is an enriched extract.
sumac extract in Parkinson-derived fibroblasts — The extract changed cellular measurements. No participants ingested sumac and bradykinesia was not measured.

Recorded void frequency in a likely overlapping healthy-adult publication series — The 2014 and 2018 reports share the 105 participants' sample design, preparations and days. Voids increased relative to baseline in all dose groups at day 10. Neither report measured sudden urgency or had a separate control group or Parkinson cohort.

Self-reported urinary volume symptom after brewed leaf tea — Four of 11 reported polyuria after a single dose. This uncontrolled observation provides neither a sudden-urge measure nor a Parkinson cohort.

eight-oil oral blend during acute cystitis and measured void count — All three observational groups reported less frequent urination. The original abstract does not give a standalone urgency or brewed leaf comparison.

Placebo-controlled concentrated leaf extract with kidney endpoints — The registered Thai comparison reports safety and biomarkers after oral capsule dosing in CKD, without brewed tea or a Parkinson urinary urgency measure.

reported asparagus avoidance and perceived choking risk — Parkinson family focus groups described avoiding stringy asparagus. The report does not identify a steamed preparation, observed exposure or measured change in swallowing severity.

asparagus exposure and acute allergic dysphagia in an occupational case — A cook with positive sensitization tests reported difficulty swallowing after eating asparagus. The acute allergic case and unknown preparation leave the steamed-asparagus claim open.

asparagus-and-chicken soup in a sensory tasting by older adults with dysphagia — The dysphagia pilot includes an asparagus-and-chicken soup among foods rated for liking. It does not isolate asparagus or assess a change in swallowing severity.
asparagus in a tube complication — Citing clinical literature describes undigested asparagus at a knotted PEG-J tube. The accessible material gives no oral swallowing outcome for steamed asparagus.

low — The thesis separately reports contralateral forepaw use after injected carvacrol and a unilateral rat lesion. The lower dose did not clearly differ from sham and the higher dose still did. The source does not report a significant treatment-versus-lesion control comparison for this endpoint, handwriting, or herb ingestion.
low — An isolated compound reduced forelimb-use asymmetry in a unilateral mouse lesion model. Cylinder wall contact does not measure handwriting size or fresh summer savory exposure.

extra-virgin olive oil in the background diet of a Parkinson case — Reported hypomimia improvement after addition of different foods. The pre-existing oil was extra-virgin and its intake change was unspecified.

dried perilla leaf powder and home systolic pressure in healthy adults — The full-group home-pressure comparison was inconclusive. A subgroup selected by month-six pressure showed lower changes. No standing pressure drop, lightheadedness or fresh leaf estimate was reported.

shrimp scampi and acute dysarthria — One case developed dysarthria after shrimp scampi with confirmed bacteremia and a suspected toxin diagnosis. Cooking method, toxin confirmation and speech intelligibility testing were absent.

mixed raw seafood exposure and dysarthria — One of 27 cerebral angiostrongyliasis cases reported dysarthria after pooled raw or undercooked shrimp or snail histories. The patient's food was unreported.

mixed seafood exposure and confirmed botulism with descriptive speech signs — Shrimp was present in a meal containing roe with the outbreak toxin. Acute toxin-associated speech signs do not attribute an effect to boiled shrimp.

soybean oil-containing pea protein and alginate gel beads designed for oral delivery — The authors report mechanical gel behavior and in vitro release. There is no patient swallowing comparison or known oil grade.

soybean oil vitamin D gel and tested texture classification — Texture and consistency tests place a formulated soybean-oil carrier in IDDSI levels 4–5 according to the authors. No observed swallowing event or refined-oil contrast.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — P1018 describes intravenous soybean oil in propofol or Intralipid and P1121 compares intragastric soy milk with cow milk. These are distinct preparations and neither tests culinary soybean oil in Parkinson disease.

food-related material in an imaging report — The original MR colonography study places excised pig colon specimens in soybean oil for imaging. This is a nonoral laboratory medium with no dose, grade or Parkinson symptom comparison.

soybean oil in both softgel formulations and subjective swallowing adaptation — Some participants reported mild difficulty swallowing large capsules. Oil grade and arm counts were unreported. Both arms contained oil and there was no Parkinson dysphagia comparison.
soybean oil in graded fish-gel formulations — Higher oil concentration reduced measured hardness but affected shape stability. The bench outcomes do not measure patient swallowing.

soybean oil gradient and texture modification for a model dysphagia food — The selected soybean-oil and gum formulation lowered hardness and adhesiveness and the final mooncake met IDDSI texture level 4. It gives no patient swallowing severity result and no oil grade.

separate gastrointestinal conference member and ingredient context — P0635 groups recipients by intravenous soybean or other lipid emulsion. A different member reports soybean sensitization. Neither uses the frozen culinary preparation or Parkinson outcome.
cinnamaldehyde preparation and Parkinson model rigidity and catalepsy — The conference abstract reported less catalepsy and rigidity with pretreatment and did not report dystonic postures.
cinnamon leaf preparations and rotenone rat catalepsy — Bar-test times were lower with some leaf formulations. Ground bark and clinical dystonia were unmeasured.

Ambient grapeseed carrier and PSQI in long-term care — The dissertation reports ambient grapeseed as the control for lavender plus the same oil, with no clear baseline-adjusted arm difference. It does not isolate a grapeseed effect or report processing, ingestion or dream enactment.

Grapeseed massage carrier and generic sleep difficulty — The comparison tested adding rose oil to grapeseed massage and did not isolate grapeseed. Oil refining, dietary exposure, Parkinson disease and dream enactment were unmeasured.

oral grapeseed cookie; healthy adults; registered sleep questionnaire correlation; no posted results — The registry describes 10 g grapeseed oil in daily cookies, and a blood linoleic acid-sleep questionnaire correlation; study lot refining, dream enactment and Parkinson cohort are not established. Official results were absent on 2026-11-15; published lipid outcomes are not sleep outcomes.

Gua Sha and dream enactment outcomes with unspecified oil — The randomized trial measured REM sleep behavior outcomes. The accessible methods did not identify the scraping oil, and the intervention was topical.

Grapeseed inhalation and polysomnography in primary insomnia — The author abstract reports no significant grapeseed-only difference from untreated on listed sleep measures. Whole article tables, refining and oral exposure are unverified. Neither Parkinson disease nor dream-enactment frequency was measured.
sweet potato test bolus in a primate model — Sweet potato served as a shared chewing stimulus. Dyskinesia was outside the experiment.
PD pooled bean category and whole-diet drool association; no pinto exposure estimate — The drool association concerns total MIND score, not canned pinto beans or an ingredient-specific effect.

reported fish intake and aggregated psychotic-like experiences among Swedish women — The published fatty-fish category shows associations in both directions across intake levels, with a broader psychotic-like symptom outcome.

Parkinson clinical charts compare motor-fluctuation groups by reported high-protein meal interaction; hallucination occurrence recorded — The motor-fluctuation subgroup reports less charted hallucination in patients with protein-related motor fluctuations. Food species, preparation, modality and episode frequency are not established, and the retrospective association does not isolate salmon.

Parkinson diet plans list canned and pan-cooked salmon; a visual hallucination event occurred in ketogenic assignment — No grilled preparation or individual salmon consumption is established. Hallucinations resolved after a pramipexole reduction; symptom frequency and meal timing are unreported.
sumac fruit extracts and cholinesterase inhibition in vitro — Water extract inhibited AChE and BChE, with a null dichloromethane result. There was no attention task.

medicinal Rhus javanica galls and exploratory attention measures — ASRS and Tower of Hanoi time favored the gall extract. Number count outcomes were inconclusive. Species, plant part, preparation and population differ from the frozen claim.

injected sumac fruit extract and avoidance learning in adult male rats — The abstract identifies longer dark-compartment entry latency with the lower extract dose. The task did not measure attention after eating ground sumac.
injected sumac extract and avoidance learning in gonadectomized rats — Injected sumac extract lengthened avoidance-related latency in a gonadectomy model. Learning was measured in a shuttle box.

nigella oil in an MPTP mouse study family — The reports contain motor assays and describe a tremor difference. The study did not count gait freezing and the earlier version shares the animal approval.

comparison of refined olive oil and extra-virgin olive oil in mild cognitive impairment — The primary publication identifies refined exposure and reports cognitive and imaging outcomes. It provides no visual hallucination count or oil-free control.

olive oil comparator and aggregate positive symptom outcome — The trial prespecified positive psychiatric symptoms with an olive oil comparator. Oil grade and a visual hallucination endpoint are unverified, and the registry has no posted results.

olive oil in a composite dietary score among older coronary patients — The outcome is reported by Mediterranean dietary score and diabetes status. No grade, oil-specific estimate or Parkinson symptom result was reported.

olive oil comparison arm and psychiatric symptom scale — The trial tested omega-3 against olive oil with antipsychotic treatment in schizophrenia. No visual-hallucination frequency or verified refined grade.
garden chervil leaf and stem chemical analysis — Fresh leaves and stems were lyophilized for chemical measurements with no behavioral testing.
methanol extract of culinary chervil in enzyme and cell assays — Enzyme assays and docking do not determine attention after dried chervil.

canola-containing diet and a measured Parkinson urinary item — Urinary problems favored ketogenic diet by 0.70 points over the low-fat diet listing canola. The broad ordinal urinary item does not count urgency episodes and the oil contribution was not isolated.
whole green cardamom powder in randomized type 2 diabetes trial — Systolic blood pressure fell relative to placebo. The trial did not assess lightheadedness on standing or Parkinson’s.

presyncope and hypotension in a cardamom-containing bun challenge case — The original event included presyncope and a mixed-bun challenge produced hypotension. The findings concern acute allergy, with no orthostatic Parkinson measure.

cardamom food exposure and presyncope in allergy case — Presyncope occurred after a mixed dish in a person with cardamom reactivity. Standing pressure and Parkinson orthostatic symptoms were not measured.

cardamom named in an adverse-event table and case-specific symptoms — Cardamom is recorded with finger numbness. Multiple-herb dizziness and blood-pressure reports are different cases. No specific postural symptom is attributable to ground cardamom.
intravenous crude cardamom extract in anesthetized rats — The extract lowered arterial blood pressure. Lightheadedness on standing was outside the model.
green cardamom powder in hypertension without a comparison arm — Resting systolic pressure decreased over 12 weeks. No standing measurement or Parkinson orthostatic symptom was reported.
green cardamom powder in randomized prediabetes trial — No significant between-arm blood pressure change. Standing lightheadedness and Parkinson’s were unmeasured.

resveratrol combination and total neuropsychiatric score in Alzheimer disease — The NPI total treatment-by-visit estimate was 0.368 (95% CI −0.584 to 1.319). Separate visual hallucination scores were unreported. Both groups received red grape juice and neither received grapeseed oil.

cardamom listed in multicomponent Parkinson diet and composite UPDRS III — The composite improved and includes a speech item. The authors did not report speech intelligibility separately or isolate cardamom.

Recovered Japanese pepper bark fraction source with injected animal motor-tone and toxicity outcomes — Original full Methods link the tested precursor to crude bark preparation rather than culinary fruit. Table 1 and adjacent prose disagree for akinesia at one dose. Reduced tone and convulsions were recorded in different toxicology contexts and give no clinical rigidity direction.

Parkinson case with baseline rigidity and walking follow-up — The report describes severe baseline rigidity and improved walking under the formula and daily rehabilitation. It does not provide a repeat rigidity outcome.

acute Parkinson medication syndrome and combination therapy — Clinical recovery after fecal impaction involved oral daikenchuto and intravenous levodopa. The report supplies no isolated ground-pepper comparison or rigidity estimate.
PD pooled beans and motor symptom aggregate including handwriting — Generic bean intake and motor aggregate do not establish boiled pinto intake or a small-handwriting effect.

spinach extract and practiced peg running — The spinach group showed greater improvement in normalized peg running with repetition but no clear difference in actual running times. Steamed spinach and Parkinson balance were untested.

registered balance with spinach extract and exercise — Both the registry and the same-cohort thesis planned baseline and follow-up balance. The strength publication and the thesis give no located balance result, and the placebo is described as sucrose and maltodextrin in different documents.
spinach extract chow and aging rat balance measures — Blueberry outperformed spinach on the rod and rotarod. The paper did not report a clear spinach-versus-control balance advantage.

oral Parkinson trial vehicle and communication domain — The placebo group communication change was zero and groups were not clearly different. No speech intelligibility measure is available, and oil exposure was shared.

oral tarragon extract and spatial learning in chronically restrained rats — The extract improved Morris water maze performance under stress. The experiment measured spatial learning and memory without isolating executive function.

injected tarragon extract and mouse open-field distance — Figure 3 generally found unchanged travel, with a reduction at 100 mg/kg. An injected extract and aggregate exploration do not estimate gait speed after fresh tarragon in Parkinson’s.

oral tarragon extract and a composite weakness scale in EAE mice — The ordinal weakness and paralysis score fell in the extract group. The outcome was not gait speed and the mice were not a Parkinson model.
ground soybeans with levodopa and carbidopa — Acute crossover found longer on time and lower dyskinesia scores. Cooked edamame and rigidity were not isolated.

isolated eugenol and gait-related tasks in MPTP mice — Eugenol pretreatment improved narrow-beam crossing and post-treatment worsened it. The rodent task and constituent provide no estimate for ground allspice in people.

seed extract and narrow-beam walking in a rat model — The author abstract reports better motor behavior on an assay set including narrow-beam walking. Gait-freezing episodes and grated nutmeg were unmeasured.

pooled acidic fruit intake and incident urgency incontinence outside Parkinson disease — The adjusted comparison had a wide interval across both directions. Peach-specific exposure and urgency episode frequency were not analyzed.
peach odor and a composite urinary score — The urinary domain association with identifying peach odor had q = .371. The model used no peach ingestion or separate urgency-frequency outcome.

isolated DHA compared with placebo for Parkinson levodopa-induced dyskinesia — Preliminary poster found 3/15 versus 7/15 cases by 12 months with no reported peak-severity difference. The posted forceplate denominator differs. Neither contrast estimates walnut oil or alpha-linolenic acid.
cold-pressed walnut oil in a rotenone fly model — Oil with rotenone improved fly climbing compared with rotenone alone; the study does not measure human dyskinesia severity.

enzymatic brown-rice protein hydrolysate and SPPB in older adults — SPPB total (p=.04) and chair stand (p=.02) favored active. Separate standing balance and cooked whole-brown-rice results are unavailable.

germinated brown rice pretreatment and open-field ambulation and pole task after rotenone — Ambulation improved and mobility duration was inconclusive. Only the non-rice positive control showed clear improvement in both pole times. Rat motor assays and unresolved cooking method.

cooked ground brown rice feed during iron exposure and fly climbing — Figure 2A reports better negative geotaxis than iron alone. The test is short-distance climbing in flies. Behavioral denominator differs across Methods and caption.

brown rice after iron exposure and fly motor outcome — The primary abstract reports improved motor function after a different exposure schedule. Details of cooking and motor test remain unavailable. No patient, pull-test or postural instability estimate.

chewed and swallowed named nigella seed and measured salivary pH — Salivary pH was higher after eating Nigella seed than after paraffin. No toasting method, salivary output measure, or severity of drooling in Parkinson disease was reported.

oral oil gavage and salivary output after irradiation in mice — Oil-treated irradiated mice had more salivary output at day three than water-treated irradiated mice. The difference had resolved among survivors at day 60. The experiment did not test toasted seed or oral saliva leakage.

cold-pressed oil rinse and reported saliva volume in healthy adults — Reported one-minute volume was 4.89 mL with cold-pressed oil and 1.43 mL with saline. Both rinse and saliva were collected, and the adjustment for retained rinse was unspecified. The fixed-order study gives no clinical drooling or toasted-seed result.
summer savory extract and forced-swim immobility after stress — Higher dose shortened immobility in stressed rats. The outcome gives no clinical fatigue measure.
savory extract and time moving after cisplatin — Intermediate extract dose attenuated cisplatin-related movement decline. The experiment gives no Parkinson fatigue estimate.
cumin fruit extract in MPTP mice with motor task outcomes — The extract improved later balance and open-field tasks. Neither muscle tone nor an orally eaten toasted spice was assessed.

multi-ingredient cumin formula and anthropometric measures — LBP4.128 reports anthropometric outcomes from a multi-ingredient cumin-containing formula. It does not isolate culinary cumin, its preparation or the frozen symptom.
ground soybeans with levodopa and carbidopa — Acute crossover found longer on time and lower dyskinesia scores. Steamed edamame and olfaction were not isolated.

fine ground bay leaf oral capsule without constipation endpoint — The four-arm trial documented the ingredient and adult oral preparation. Its endpoints were glucose and lipids, with no itemized constipation assessment.

aqueous leaf extract and slower rat gastrointestinal transit — Injected extract slowed a charcoal meal and separate tests found antidiarrheal effects. These disease and route differences leave clinical constipation unresolved.

ground bay leaf powder in oral cookies with short digestive assessment — Participants reported no digestive discomfort in the two-hour crossover. This does not address constipation severity or Parkinson.

human extract tablets and constipation questionnaire — Median constipation scores fell from 2.0 to 1.0 (P=.021) in the extract arm and from 2.0 to 1.5 (P=.086) in placebo. Table 11 gives tests within each arm without a between-arm test or effect estimate. The trial enrolled healthy adults and used an extract tablet.

food-related material in an imaging report — The original MR colonography study places excised pig colon specimens in soybean oil for imaging. This is a nonoral laboratory medium with no dose, grade or Parkinson symptom comparison.

dystonia presentation before a systemic soybean-oil emulsion in a mitochondrial disorder — The Leigh syndrome case names dystonia and describes general response to an intravenous soybean-oil emulsion. Available text gives no dystonia-specific post-exposure finding, culinary refined preparation, or Parkinson disease.

oral refined peanut oil and oral allergy symptoms — No allergic reactions occurred after refined oil in 60 peanut-allergic participants. Crude oil caused oral or throat itching, wheeze or swelling in six. Drooling and Parkinson disease were not measured.

oral pumpkin seed oil added to tadalafil in chronic pelvic pain — The abstract reports an advantage only in the pain domain, while overall improvement was 11 of 25 with the oil combination versus 12 of 25 with tadalafil. Exact domain data and oil processing remain open.

solvent-extracted pumpkin seed oil and evoked mouse pain — Hot-plate latency increased and chemical writhing decreased. These measures ran opposite to the worsening hypothesis in a non-Parkinson model using solvent-extracted oil.

cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil combined with Solcoseryl for cancer-treatment oral mucositis — The matching 2024 paper reports lower aggregate PROMS with a topical combination containing 10% cold-pressed oil versus benzydamine. A mouth-pain item is part of the scale and was not reported separately. Solcoseryl and the adverse comparator prevent isolated attribution.

registered one-arm oral Cucurbita pepo oil pilot and pelvic pain/urgency composite — Manufacturer describes the named product as cold pressed. The registry records completion and 40 enrolled with no posted results. The composite is broader than pain alone and no Parkinson or oil-free comparison was assigned.

local pumpkin seed oil ultrasound and measured prostatitis pain — Mean pain fell 13.49 points with oil-coupled ultrasound and 12.59 with active ultrasound. The table supplies no pain-specific pairwise uncertainty. Local exposure and pelvic pain do not estimate clinical Parkinson effects of ingested cold-pressed oil.

oral pumpkin seed oil and menopause-related joint pain — Joint-pain median fell from two to one in the oil arm, with no clear 12-week endpoint difference versus wheat germ oil. The processing method and Parkinson pain were untested.

Parkinson diet-adherence whole nut item and planned swallowing outcome — The diet promotes olive oil and lists whole hazelnuts on the adherence tool. The planned nutrition-related motor item numbering and scoring differ from the original MDS-UPDRS. The official record displays Recruiting with an elapsed estimated completion and no posted results. No toasted hazelnut oil was assigned.

whole roasted hazelnut and oral allergy reactions — Five of 17 raw-hazelnut-allergic participants reacted to the whole roasted nut challenge. This acute allergy outcome does not establish the effect of toasted hazelnut oil on swallowing in Parkinson disease.

whole hazelnut challenge and swallowing symptom checklist — Difficulty swallowing was a subjective criterion in the clinical challenge study. The available report provides no specific swallowing estimate after toasted hazelnut oil and enrolled adults with suspected allergy.

compound hazelnut-oil gargle and ex vivo tongue wetting — The combination increased liquid retention and reduced tongue adhesiveness in an ex vivo model. No swallowing function, oral intake or verified toasted oil was tested.

Black pepper leaf tea versus chamomile in adults with insomnia — The comparison used leaf tea rather than ground peppercorns, and insomnia severity and overall sleep quality rather than dream-enactment episodes; no Parkinson subgroup was reported.

black pepper essential oil facial cream versus unscented cream and home sleep staging — Thirty-two healthy adults used 0.0025% pepper oil or control at bedtime. Mean REM duration was 75.8 versus 72.4 min and no significant sleep differences were reported. There was no ground pepper ingestion or dream-enactment outcome.

Black-pepper-fruit-containing multi-botanical oral formula in adults with chronic insomnia — Multi-herb formula and sleep-quality composite cannot isolate pepper or estimate dream-enactment frequency; no Parkinson subgroup was identified.

Oral black-pepper extract and EEG/EMG sleep staging in caffeine-exposed mice — No significant REM-duration difference was reported, but REM duration and bouts do not measure dream-enactment frequency; extract and mouse model differ from culinary ground pepper in Parkinson disease.

low — A case linked aniseed liqueur consumption with episodic tongue swelling and difficulty swallowing and breathing. IgE studies support seed sensitization. This is an allergy-related oral symptom, without a speech intelligibility measure or ground-seed Parkinson comparison.

isolated piperine plus levodopa and rat movement composite — The axial dystonia assessment was included in a total abnormal involuntary movement score, without a separate dystonia estimate. The model intervention used isolated piperine with levodopa.

topical grapeseed comparator and sleep duration — Two-week wrist application showed no clear lavender-versus-grapeseed differences in tracker-derived total, light or deep sleep. There was no oral or untreated comparison, and insomnia severity was unreported.

oral grapeseed oil cookie and registered sleep questionnaire — The oral cookie comparison registered correlations of blood linoleic acid with questionnaire sleep. The published reports do not provide those estimates. No Parkinson participants or insomnia endpoint were identified.

nonoral grapeseed comparison and registered hospital sleep outcomes — Grapeseed oil on gauze was compared with lavender and usual care for planned hospital sleep quality and duration. The terminated study has no posted outcome estimates.

oral grapeseed oil cookie and registered sleep quality — The healthy-adult pilot plans a correlation involving global sleep quality after an oral grapeseed oil cookie. No results are posted, and the study does not measure Parkinson insomnia severity.

high-linoleic cookie and registered insomnia severity — The single-arm study plans an Insomnia Severity Index, actigraphy and EEG in adults with insomnia symptoms. The oil is unnamed. It is not yet recruiting and no results are posted.

oral essential oil and measured whole stomach emptying — Nonsignificant gastric results across baseline and both drug contexts differ from the detected intestinal inhibition. The tested oil had no levodopa or clinical fluctuations arm.
oral fruit tea and clinical postoperative bowel recovery — An earlier return of flatus and bowel movements cannot distinguish gastric emptying or levodopa wearing-off.

fennel oil and anethole in drug delayed emptying — The oil and compound improved experimentally delayed emptying in mice. A normal-baseline anethole comparison did not indicate acceleration. No oral toasted seed or levodopa arm.
oral extract and loperamide delayed stomach emptying — Reduced retention in drug-challenged mice is a relevant mechanistic lead. Whole seeds, levodopa and clinical daily OFF time remain unmeasured.

fennel seed infusion on excised stomach muscle — Proximal relaxation and increased antral amplitude establish distinct regional muscle effects. The protocol cannot estimate whole-stomach emptying or clinical OFF time.
registered external fennel and postoperative ileus — Topical heated fennel and planned ileus outcomes do not estimate oral exposure or Parkinson OFF time. Registry results are absent.
peanut oil as injected carrier in a primate parkinsonism model — Freezing contributes to the composite motor scale. The paper gives no separate freezing frequency or isolated oil comparison.

isolated oral thymol and endurance, grip and coordination in accelerated-aging mice — Treated mouse treadmill distance roughly doubled from baseline and the control average stayed near baseline. Grip strength was near baseline after thymol versus a 36% decline in control. Coordination favored thymol. Single-compound exposure, survivor analyses and no length-of-stride measure. Earlier GSA abstract and mouse work overlap in source lineage.
dried oregano infusion and mouse coordination — Higher-dose infusion reduced rotarod retention and slowed chimney climbing. This leaves stride length following fresh oregano unresolved.

oregano essential oil and rotarod in healthy rats — Rotating-rod retention was inconclusive and high-dose males showed more exploration. Neither result measures stride length after fresh oregano in Parkinson’s.
rice bran emulsion oral spray and TOMASS after head and neck radiotherapy — Swallowing test outcomes were inconclusive, while the separate subjective dry-mouth measure improved modestly.

Authenticated rice oil odor control and measured swallowing in dysphagia — Control repetitive saliva swallowing and both water swallow tests had no clear pre-post changes. Six participants had unspecified neurodegenerative disease, with no subgroup estimate or oral oil exposure.

rice bran oil placebo and composite Parkinson outcome — Registry and conference sources report composite outcomes and no chewing and swallowing item estimate. The placebo oil grade and active formulation carrier are unspecified.
mint-flavored gum and balance performance in Parkinson’s — Balance scores improved during chewing. Falls were not followed and the botanical flavor was unspecified.
standardized spearmint extract and reactive agility — Some sensor task results improved and others were null. The study did not measure falls or fresh leaf ingestion in Parkinson’s.

cruciferous vegetable recalls and estimated indole intake — The study includes broccoli, cauliflower and kale within a food inventory. Neither constituent exposure nor a symptom effect is established for a particular preparation.

mixed garden produce distribution — The garden reported distribution of green beans, kale, chard and watermelon within a mixed harvest. The evaluation concerns program delivery without an ingredient-specific intake or clinical symptom measurement.

cooked kale in a calcium questionnaire and falls in an education trial — The education arm had fewer reported falls by rank, with a median of zero in both arms. The study did not estimate roasted kale intake or effects.

oral canola oil and a paced tapping imaging task — Motor BOLD decreased after canola oil during instructed tapping. No separate tapping-performance result, refined-oil confirmation or Parkinson sample.

canola crossover and monitored paced finger-tapping rate — Tapping was 2.09 ± 0.27 Hz SEM across trials with no significant variation at the paced target. Speeded dexterity or accuracy and refining were unverified.

canola oil in mixed oral diets with limb motor measures — Canola oil was 10 g/kg in control feed and absent from both alternate formulas. The motor results concern whole chow diets in mice and no oil grade was reported.

Crisco canola hand-arthritis comparator with invalid grip measurements — Grip data were discarded because the instrument failed. Product composition was reported without confirmed processing or a dexterity result.
other whole oily fish and manual dexterity — Herring and mackerel meals modestly improved nondominant-hand peg test time relative to meat in children. The dominant-hand comparison was inconclusive.

Chives listed in multi-ingredient Parkinson diet, preparation and actual individual amount unclear; no drooling result — Baseline UPDRS II total is not a reported saliva item or intervention comparison; the published follow-up reports UPDRS III total and cannot determine the effect of dried common chives on drooling.

pooled legume intake according to self-reported swallowing status — Reported intake was higher among people with existing swallowing disturbances. Neither drooling severity nor canned kidney beans was measured.

pediatric kidney bean allergy and cross-reactivity — The children experienced immediate hives or facial swelling following ingestion. The observations do not measure Parkinson drooling or visual hallucinations.

pooled legume or bean intake and whole-diet drooling scores — Table 2 reports drooling against whole diet scores. Table S4 evaluates pooled bean or legume intake against aggregate symptom burden and does not identify species or preparation.

oral allergic symptoms after a mixed meal and laboratory reactivity to canned kidney bean extract — The mixed chili provoked oral and systemic allergic symptoms. Extract from canned kidney beans showed IgE reactivity, while preparation and drooling after kidney bean ingestion remained untested.

mixed thyme tablet and patient urgency intensity — Urgency intensity changed from 1.357 to 1.26 with p=.705. The uncontrolled mix does not separate fresh thyme, urgency frequency or Parkinson outcomes.

thyme essential oil and ex vivo bladder contractility — Thyme oil decreased evoked tension but showed a concentration-dependent reversal in spontaneous variability in longitudinal guinea pig bladder strips. No urgency counts or culinary intake.
Thymus vulgaris oil in a multi-oil cystitis comparison — The original abstract records void frequency after eight oils, with no separate urgency outcome or fresh thyme comparison.
oat milk-associated acute allergy and dysphonia — Case records acute dysphonia with laryngeal allergy after oat milk. Loudness, ordinary rolled oat consumption and Parkinson disease were not studied.

distinct oat milk hypersensitivity case with acute dysphonia — A distinct adult presented with dysphonia during acute allergy to oat milk. Neither speech loudness nor an ordinary rolled-oat effect in Parkinson disease was measured.
oatmeal and total Parkinson symptom burden — The survey did not specify rolled oats or report acoustic voice volume.
