objective voice measures during Parkinson medication challenge — Levodopa ON and OFF testing provides endpoint context but no oat exposure.

oral concentrated tarragon extract and female rat grip strength — Lower female forelimb grip at 10 and 1000 mg/kg/day, p < .05. The middle dose and global activity offered no corresponding signal. Extract gavage and strength differ from culinary dried herb and manual dexterity.

oral Angelica/tarragon blend and mouse forelimb grip — Example 3-4 reports increased grip force in a dexamethasone-atrophy mouse model. The blended exposure gives no estimate for tarragon alone and grip force differs from manual dexterity.

injected essential oil and mouse motor coordination — Acute i.p. oil reduced rotarod retention and was associated with sedation. Concentrated oil, injection and gross coordination differ from the frozen exposure and endpoint.

cold-pressed walnut oil comparator and mouse learning — Enzyme-extracted oil led to shorter escape latency and more active avoidance than cold-pressed oil. The abstract does not give group estimates or a cold-pressed versus vehicle contrast.

ground whole walnuts in bread and verbal reasoning in healthy students — Verbal inference improved by 1.0 point (95% CI 0.3 to 1.7), while overall verbal critical thinking and working-memory sequencing were inconclusive. The 2016 mood report uses the same cohort. No walnut oil, clinical executive impairment or Parkinson comparison.

Mediterranean mixed whole nuts and corrected frontal cognition composite — Corrected Table 4 adjusted changes were +0.03 for mixed whole nuts, +0.23 for the olive-oil diet and -0.33 for control. Pairwise mixed nuts versus low-fat advice was inconclusive. The olive-oil diet comparison was clearer. This is a PREDIMED subgroup without walnut oil or a Parkinson-specific endpoint.

acute walnut oil milkshake and conditioned fear learning — Existing trial reports faster fear extinction in young volunteers, with pressing method unverified. Fear prediction and executive-function impairment are distinct endpoints.

oral walnut oil and spatial memory in developing rats — Higher tested levels shortened water-maze escape latency in young rats without a clear difference in swimming speed. The experiment gives no clinical executive-function comparison.

oral walnut oil and mouse spatial learning — Walnut oil improved water-maze performance in scopolamine-treated mice. The assay measures spatial learning rather than executive impairment in Parkinson disease.

walnut oil and delayed maze performance in rats — There was no clear difference between diet groups in completion time or errors on the delayed test. The control group worsened relative to its training values. This rodent task cannot establish clinical executive function.
turmeric-containing formula and motor complications — The ZAZ2 formula arm had a lower UPDRS Part IV score at week 13. The publication does not report daily OFF hours or isolate turmeric.
phospholipid curcumin and OFF examination — The study examined motor function while medication was OFF. It did not measure time spent OFF in ordinary daily life.
nanomicelle curcumin and registered MDS-UPDRS — The registry and accessible primary abstract give aggregate outcomes without a specific item 4.3 or daily OFF duration estimate.
anise extract and exploratory habituation — Maintained exploration at the highest dose suggests altered habituation. The study does not establish a directional attention effect or test ground seed.

eugenol odor pulses during animal REM recordings — Odor produced state-sensitive cortical field-potential responses. No eugenol-specific loss-of-atonia or dream-enactment outcome was assessed and allspice was not eaten.

low — The primary rodent study imposed REM deprivation and then measured startle, prepulse inhibition, and rotarod learning. Its clove-oil nanoemulsion and oral isolated solution came from a eugenol delivery experiment. Dream enactment frequency and ground allspice were unmeasured.
ground raw Carum carvi capsule; pulmonary tuberculosis; GI outcomes — Ground-caraway study did not assess voice volume or Parkinson disease; exposure as a capsule differs from culinary use.
ground bay leaf capsules in a type 2 diabetes trial — The metabolic trial tested ground bay leaf and excluded neurologic disease. Swallowing difficulty was unmeasured.

culinary laurel leaf and acute swallowing difficulty — An intact culinary laurel leaf lodged during a soup meal. Symptoms resolved after removal. Species and ground exposure were unverified and Parkinson disease was unreported.
whole bay leaves removed from pharynx — Two meal-associated cases identify intact leaves in the pharyngeal pouch or hypopharynx. Neither establishes a ground-leaf Parkinson effect.
whole bay leaves with marked dysphagia or airway obstruction — The first page describes four cases and marked dysphagia in two. Ground exposure and Parkinson diagnosis were unreported.
homeopathic celery proving and acute hoarseness reports — One 6C or 30C prover had hoarseness with other respiratory symptoms. Fresh leaf identity, arm comparison and voice volume remain unverified.
celery named in a Parkinson diet with speech in its motor scale — No separate voice volume measure, isolated celery arm or fresh leaf detail.
rocket-associated compound in Parkinson mice — The injected erucin intervention partially improved induced rotations. The study did not test face movement or raw food.
rucola on a bundled Parkinson diet menu — The intervention measured aggregate motor severity. It supplies neither a raw-leaf comparison nor a separate facial-expression effect.

pearled barley within one assigned multi-food home dinner and postprandial pressure — In spinal cord injury, home-meal maximum systolic fall showed no clear diet effect. A separate laboratory comparison did not include barley. The study did not isolate boiled barley or orthostatic lightheadedness.

meal and different Parkinson blood pressure measures — The supine post-lunch pressure drop was larger in Parkinson participants. The orthostatic pressure drop was smaller after the meal, and neither boiled barley nor lightheadedness was specified.

summer savory essential oil and smooth gut contractions — Contractions of isolated rat ileum were reduced with concentrated summer savory oil. This is a distinct tissue, route and endpoint from clinical muscular rigidity.
isolated carvacrol and motor performance after rotenone — Oral carvacrol improved aggregate motor performance in mice. The original abstract gives no fresh summer savory rigidity result.

acute inability to speak during confirmed buckwheat allergy history — The case involved anaphylaxis and airway symptoms. The report gives no cooked-groat matrix, Parkinson cohort, or motor speech estimate.

low — The diabetes case series recorded four reports of hoarseness during peripheral neuropathy after an unspecified Tartary buckwheat product. There was no cooked-groat exposure or speech intelligibility assessment.

multicomponent supplement containing unspecified mint — The combination group had a lower 12-month mean fatigue score. The trial neither specifies the mint species or fresh preparation nor isolates its effect.

commercial gum chewing and workday fatigue in non-Parkinson adults — A workday fatigue reduction appeared in one design and did not replicate within participants. Neither workday study isolates fresh spearmint.

permitted spearmint and fatigue testimonials in a lifestyle program — The protocol explicitly permits spearmint. Fatigue testimonials occur in other diagnoses, with no verified fresh spearmint use or Parkinson-specific fatigue estimate.
spearmint extract and mood subscales — Individual mood comparisons did not show significant pairwise placebo differences. The study did not measure fresh spearmint’s effect on Parkinson fatigue.
extract blend and Profile of Mood States fatigue outcome — The adjusted fatigue comparison spanned zero. No fresh spearmint or Parkinson fatigue was tested.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — Anxiety severity was not measured by individual dried herb exposure.
confirmed ingestion of toxic look-alike — The original German case confirmed aconitine after a substitution. It gives no anxiety severity estimate for culinary lovage.

topical cayenne in kaolin and human seated balance — The preliminary crossover comparison reported no change in seated wobble-board centre-of-pressure measurements. The exact spice appeared in a topical treatment, without oral exposure or clinically measured Parkinson postural instability.

unidentified oral spice and acute static sway in seven healthy adults — Aylward, Korf, Colleti and Haworth reported seven healthy adults aged 18–25 who completed balance testing at baseline and after two oral spice conditions. The abstract gives mean BTrackS sway of 19.57 ± 4.47 cm at baseline, 17.29 ± 4.57 after the lower-heat condition and 16.71 ± 4.72 after the higher-heat condition. It reports omnibus p > .05 and nominal pairwise p = .043 and .035. Limits-of-stability ...
summer savory ethanol extract and protein aggregation — The assay gives no behavioral endpoint and tests an Alzheimer-associated protein.
summer savory essential oil and enzyme inhibition — The biochemical assay gives no executive-function outcome.
isolated carvone; mouse locomotion; no dystonia outcome — Locomotor activity in mice does not establish the effect of toasted whole caraway on human Parkinson dystonia.
Clove extract in intestinal transport experiments — Rat alanine transport and jejunal enzyme activity were measured. No levodopa concentration or time in motor OFF was obtained.

Isolated oral eugenol in a levodopa-treated lesion model — The journal and grant reports examined post-dose behavior over a short observation and striatal dopamine depletion. The study has no daily OFF diary, human comparator or food exposure.

A clove-bud-containing eight-herb formula with levodopa in mice — Motor tasks and abnormal involuntary movement outcomes depend on the whole formula and levodopa setting. The animal comparisons do not estimate hours of daily OFF in people.

Human Parkinson olfactory training trial reporting MDS-UPDRS Part IV totals — Figure 6 gives a motor complications subscale total. No separately extracted 4.3 time-spent-OFF estimate or diary appears, and the trial combined inhaled scents.
Fresh oral leaves and informal oral symptom observations — The report describes halitosis and suggests more saliva without instrumented swallowing, comparison arm, cooked leaves or Parkinson disease.

Fresh leaf oral contact and saliva pH — The intervention was chewing and expectorating fresh leaves and the outcomes were pH and tongue coating. The trial did not measure dysphagia or cooked leaf ingestion.

Heated ground curry leaves in steamed bread and texture measures — The original tests mouthfeel and instrumental firmness after adding ground leaves to cooked idli. Human clinical swallowing and bolus safety were unmeasured.
mint-flavored gum and Parkinson motor tests — Timed walking did not change significantly and stride length was unreported. No brewed spearmint exposure.
brewed spearmint and walking performance in knee osteoarthritis — The test measured distance over six minutes without an effect on stride length or a Parkinson cohort.

peppermint leaf extract and measured stride in rotenone mice — Figure 2C: 6.05 versus 4.27 cm for extract with rotenone versus model control (p<.001). Hybrid peppermint and ethanolic extract differ from brewed spearmint.
cardamom listed in multicomponent Parkinson diet and composite UPDRS III — The composite improved and includes a speech item. The authors did not report voice volume separately or isolate cardamom.

isolated sesamol and rat-pup open-field or maze behavior — Isolated constituent improved several behaviors in a juvenile MSG exposure model. Mixed behavioral tests do not establish clinical attention after culinary toasted oil.
sesame oil cake solid-residue extract in a memory trial — Memory trial reports verbal learning effects and states that attention was not assessed. The extract is separate from edible sesame oil.

combined astaxanthin plus sesamin supplement with human attention subtests — Small per-protocol pilot reported differences in speed measures. Descriptive attention means did not favor the supplement at 12 weeks, with no inferential attention finding, separate sesamin arm or toasted oil.
sesame oil vehicle and sustained concentration — The sustained-concentration item worsened with added CBD and THC. Both randomized groups received sesame oil and its processing is unspecified.

contamination differential from safety surveillance — Reported disorientation and visual disturbance with mydriasis have a documented foreign botanical exposure. Formed hallucinations and ingested toasted fennel in Parkinson’s were not measured.

native and thermally oxidized canola diets in a developmental rat experiment — Greater impairment was observed in motor testing after heated oil feeding. The effect is a heat-status comparison outside a Parkinson model with no confirmed pressing grade.

rapeseed and peanut mixed oil versus peanut-only in two mouse balance tasks — Only the low-platform retention outcome clearly differed. Elevated test, grip and endurance did not. The oil changed alongside composition and had no verified cold-press grade.

canola vehicle and motor assays in a Parkinson model — Canola served as the drug vehicle in a lesioned rat study with bridge and rotarod testing. The study varied diphenyl diselenide and did not estimate a stand-alone oil or Parkinson instability effect.

canola-containing diet and postural-stability measurement domain — The trial scored Part III, which includes a postural-stability item. Only the total comparison was available, with no isolated cold-pressed oil or balance result.

canola comparator and quantitative walking balance in healthy older adults — The canola control walking-balance index was 34.7 at baseline and 31.3 after three months, within p=.410. MCT versus control differed, p=.009. The control was ungraded and the cohort healthy with no pull-test result.

canola control and timed up and go during an exercise intervention — The canola comparator improved by 0.6 seconds at 12 weeks. All arms received exercise and there was no significant between-arm difference. This was a mobility proxy outside Parkinson disease.

1908 account of drowsiness and stupor in earlier nutmeg poison cases — Cushny summarized Wallace’s cases and adverse poison effects. This is historical evidence of acute toxicity rather than a separate ordinary-serving trial.

nutmeg fruit syrup and pre/post alertness task — Precision moved lower and response time difference was inconclusive. The material was fruit syrup, with no verified ground seed, control group or measured daytime sleepiness.
inhaled essential oil and mouse activity suppression — Wheel activity decreased after inhalation. This animal surrogate does not estimate daytime sleepiness after eating ground nutmeg.
nutmeg poison-center calls with descriptive drowsiness — A drowsiness case included coexposures. No standardized daytime sleepiness estimate or usual culinary dose comparison was available.

acute nutmeg overdose and somnolence in a human case — Somnolence occurred during observation after deliberate overdose. The acute toxic exposure and concurrent medicines preclude inference about ordinary culinary exposure.

suspected accidental excessive nutmeg in food and next-morning drowsiness — The patient reported adding more ground spice than intended and also drank alcohol. Drowsiness arose with other poisoning symptoms. No ordinary-serving or Parkinson estimate.

pooled fresh vegetables and Parkinson motivation — Higher pooled vegetable frequency was associated with greater motivation (absolute r = 0.166368). The baseline analysis supplies no kale-specific estimate or uncertainty interval.

repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking — Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.

whole sweet pepper frequency and handgrip in adults — The fully adjusted handgrip trends for sweet pepper were p=.55 in men and p=.77 in women. The paper supplied no grilling, clinical Parkinson group or fine dexterity measure.

whole sweet pepper in two Parkinson diet menus and overall Part III motor examination — The pepper-containing diets improved the aggregate motor score. The report gave no hand-dexterity result or independent exposure to grilled peppers.

paprika vegetable in a Parkinson diet with finger taps and hand movements — Finger taps and hand movements contributed to total UPDRS III, which improved after the dietary program. Separate hand-motor results, preparation and independent paprika exposure were unavailable.

sweet pepper food frequency and dynamometer grip within composite sarcopenia — A 2021 study gave a lower adjusted OR for composite sarcopenia under more frequent sweet pepper consumption. The related 2019 abstract gave a nonsignificant sweet pepper association. The reports provide neither a separate sweet pepper coefficient for grip nor fine dexterity results.

isolated capsiate and total bench-press weight — A 6 mg capsiate dose increased bench weight compared with placebo in healthy trained men (p=.039). The 12 mg dose provided no improvement. Upper-body resistance performance does not measure fine hand dexterity.

isolated dihydrocapsiate and upper-body resistance exercise — A 25-person triple-blind trial found no significant change for bench and squat outcomes under 12 mg dihydrocapsiate (all p≥.703). The study did not test hand dexterity, grilled pepper, or Parkinson disease.

named red bell pepper in a dietary recall and older adult grip outcome — The exposure analyzed for the handgrip-based sarcopenia outcome was total polyphenols. Red bell pepper contributed to that estimate and no separate intake effect, preparation comparison or fine-dexterity measure was supplied.

oral macadamia oil comparator and executive-control tests — Stroop and Symbol Digit treatment-by-time effects were not clear (p = .4683 and .9121). The study compares macadamia oil capsules with krill oil capsules in officers and cannot estimate macadamia oil versus no oil.

Parkinson survey recording cumin use with aggregate nonmotor measures — Cumin intake was recorded and exploratory nonmotor comparisons were inconclusive after correction. No preparation or cumin-specific daytime sleepiness estimate is reported.

whole pomegranate fruit and acute saliva measurements in children — The pomegranate group reported higher stimulated saliva at 30 minutes than unstimulated baseline. Flow was not separated by fruit or juice form. The collection conditions, population and endpoint differ from the claim.

nanoemulsified pomegranate seed oil and planned Parkinson saliva outcome — The planned NMSS contains a saliva item. No results or realized enrollment were verified. The intervention is a nanoformulated oil capsule.

unstimulated salivary flow in Parkinson disease without a food intervention — Parkinson participants had reduced unstimulated secretion compared with matched controls. Salivary flow and patient complaints about excess saliva do not provide a food-specific drooling result.
pomegranate extract rinse and saliva chemistry in healthy adults — Salivary protein and enzyme outcomes changed. No raw aril exposure or clinical drooling outcome.

swallowed pomegranate extract and pediatric salivary measures — Methods mention collecting salivary flow. Published tables give pH and dental outcomes without a separate flow or drooling estimate. The intervention is an extract in children.

caraway and coriander in food with acute allergic hypotension — The case measured 76/52 mmHg during anaphylaxis and attributed the reaction to two spices in a mixed food. This did not measure orthostatic lightheadedness or toasted caraway exposure.

oral caraway water extract and seated blood pressure outside Parkinson disease — Seated blood pressure had no clear between-group change. The 2013 and 2014 reports describe a likely shared cohort. Standing pressure, lightheadedness and toasted caraway were untested.

summer savory extract and cisplatin rat behavior — An intermediate dose attenuated tail-suspension changes. Authors warn that anxiety and movement complicate the depression proxy. The related 2019 behavior and 2018 tissue papers may share the cohort.

oral smoked and unsmoked paprika and supine blood pressure — Mean systolic pressure changed little in the two exposure periods. Participants were healthy and the study did not measure a standing response or orthostatic symptoms.

paprika xanthophyll capsules and exercise blood pressure — Completed eight-week double-blind trial with 23 enrolled and outcomes pending. Ramp-test blood pressure is planned. Neither an orthostatic pressure test nor lightheadedness is specified.

Randomized oral seed comparison and a fatigue statement about a different arm — The author abstract credits cumin with systemic symptom reductions including fatigue and dill seed with pain relief. It provides no dill-arm fatigue estimate or leaf exposure.

Anethum tablets and a potentially fatigue-related adverse complaint — Malaise or tiredness occurred among reported complaints in the Anethum tablet arm. Frequency, comparative magnitude, preparation and Parkinson fatigue severity cannot be recovered from the available original abstract.

Mixed Anethum powder formula with a fatigue comparison — Acute COVID Table 1 reports 16/30 versus 10/30 with P=.118 despite an abstract claim of significant fatigue reduction. Multiple ingredients and unspecified dill plant part preclude a dill foliage estimate.

Actual mixed soup consumed during severe COVID with repeated weakness and lethargy ratings — The recipe allows fresh or dried dill and actual form was not recorded. Combined weakness and lethargy fluctuated across multiple foods and treatments without a comparator.

Dill-labelled pickle brine with an exercise exhaustion time comparison — Nine healthy men reached similar mean cycling exhaustion times across brine, saline and water (P=.40). Dill dose and plant part are unknown and endurance time is distinct from symptom severity.
permitted dill and fatigue testimonials in a lifestyle program — Dill weed is listed. Non-Parkinson testimonies describe fatigue changes without individual dried-dill intake or separate effects.

Parkinson protein redistribution and peak-dose dyskinesia — Peak-dose dyskinesia often worsened even as off time fell in responders. The exposure was a protein-redistribution diet with no chive-specific comparison.

chives in a mixed Parkinson diet with unreported dyskinesia outcome — Baseline UPDRS IV appears in Table 1 for the case-control cohort. The intervention follow-up reports total UPDRS III and supplies no dyskinesia result or chive comparison.

topical bitter almond oil vehicle and facial expression observations — A topical apomorphine vehicle lists bitter almond oil and a separate example describes Parkinson facial expressions; no isolatable oral oil comparison, confirmed case join, hypomimia item result or cold-pressed formulation.
summer savory extract and awake locomotion — Distance and time moving favored one dose after cisplatin. The tests did not score freezing events.
oral summer savory essential oil and rotarod retention — Rotarod improved in lead-exposed rats. No episode-based gait freezing measure.

chervil in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome — The menu lists chervil and the motor examination includes speech. The paper does not establish fresh chervil exposure or report individual speech intelligibility change.

plasma alpha-linolenic acid and the Parkinson handwriting item — UPDRS handwriting ρ = .094 (p = .581) adjusted for age and .031 (p = .854) adjusted for sex. Handwriting size and oral cold-pressed oil were not separately assessed.

commercial cardamom food essence used as a sniffed smell-test item — Correct identification occurred in 36 of 87 Parkinson cases and 49 of 58 controls. This is an assessment stimulus with no ground cardamom ingestion contrast.

cardamom odor threshold measured in Parkinson participants — Table 5 gives recognition-pressure thresholds at three stimulus concentrations. The protocol assessed nasal odor detection. The effect of eating ground cardamom remains open.
cardamom essence in an endocrine smell identification test — Cardamom was one of ten fixed diagnostic odors. Cross-sectional score differences do not test oral cardamom or Parkinson olfactory change.

confirmed cardamom odor in a post-traumatic rotating regimen — The 2024 companion Methods verify cardamom in month two of the rotating program. The 2021 outcomes concern the complete multi-odor training in post-traumatic olfactory impairment.

natural cardamom odor identification in Parkinson case-control test — Cardamom identification did not differ significantly between groups in this test. It did not assess olfactory change after oral ingestion.
cardamom odor stimulus — Odor assessment evaluated an existing impairment. No effect estimate from eating cardamom.
caraway seed extract and mouse rotarod retention — There was no clear change in gross motor coordination after injection. The study did not measure fine hand or paw dexterity.

rapeseed bread crossover and objective selective attention — Selective attention and working memory differences were inconclusive. Lipid-free bread was faster for psychomotor response time than all lipid meals. This is distinct from a selective attention effect.

conventional canola diet and planned neuropsychological tests in peripheral arterial disease — The thesis says cognitive tests were collected and remained available for further analyses. No numerical attention estimate was found.

commercial canola and selective attention after test meals — The canola–coconut score estimate was −3, 95% CI −14 to 9. A supplier sheet identifies one refined product under the trial brand. The study batch and Parkinson population are unverified.

canola spread comparator with measured TOVA in children — Table 5 gives −0.45 ± 2.51, within-arm p=.418. The abstract gives −0.42. Contrasts compare fatty-acid formulations without a verified refined-oil or Parkinson effect.
rapeseed-containing comparator in a childhood EPA trial — Teacher-rated inattention favored EPA, while total Conners scores were inconclusive. No oil-only or verified refined canola effect.

dietary canola oil and working memory in an Alzheimer mouse model — Canola-fed transgenic mice had lower spontaneous alternation. The outcome is an animal working-memory assay. Parkinson attention and refining grade were unmeasured.

oral capsaicin stimulation and evoked salivary output — Saliva output increased after isolated capsaicin stimulation in 18 healthy adults. Participants spat it out. The study measured secretion and did not test smoked paprika or drooling.
ground dried chili in food and saliva incorporation — Pungent ground dried chili increased saliva in the food bolus. It did not measure the escape of saliva from the mouth or study smoked paprika.

historical paprika and salivary response study — The authorized preview confirms the general prior salivary-effect claim and research aim. Outcome pages remain gated. The preview cannot verify smoked preparation, specific results or drooling.

safflower oil changed in oral feed with forelimb measures — Safflower rose from 10 to 17 g/kg within the high-DHA feed. No clear differences in cylinder forelimb contacts or adjusting steps were reported. No isolated oil grade or hand-dexterity effect was measured.

safflower oil in mixed oral diets with limb motor measures — Safflower oil was 0, 25 and 19 g/kg across three formulas. The varied motor results cannot identify an isolated safflower or refining-grade effect on human hand dexterity.

safflower oil changed in a diet with a forelimb endpoint — Safflower and corn oil amounts both decreased as DHA was added. Only the combined DHA and exercise group improved stepping asymmetry. There was no separate refined safflower oil arm.

lovage in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome — The menu lists lovage and the motor examination includes gait and bradykinesia. The paper does not establish dried leaf exposure or report walking speed.

PD synthetic butylphthalide; off-medication motor composite; no OFF duration — Overnight medication withdrawal for examination is not daily OFF time; synthetic seed-derived compound is not dietary dried celery leaf.
strain-defined fermented milk — The trial supplied no clear change in the motor examination composite and no matched preparation-specific estimate.

diet history and clinical facial signs in corticobasal degeneration — A corticobasal case had hypomimia recorded in 2013 and a later diet history naming milk and occasional chicken. No timed food exposure contrast, preparation-grade information or causally attributable facial outcome.

low — In the 28-day rodent study, drowsiness and reduced spontaneous motor activity were recorded only at the highest oral aqueous seed extract dose. There is no affected animal count, time-of-day estimate, or Parkinson group. The filtered extract differs from culinary ground seed.

oral tarragon tincture and rodent wake behavior with unresolved drug-induced sleep assays — The proceedings report higher early exploration and rearing under oral tincture. The dissertation synopsis labels sedation and references drug-induced sleep experiments without tarragon-specific timing results. Neither evaluates fresh tarragon or clinical daytime sleepiness.
healthy-adult soy-protein tarragon complex and general adverse-event monitoring — The registry has no posted results and the protocol does not name a sleepiness outcome.
acute sedation after concentrated tarragon oil in mice — Some anticonvulsant doses caused sedation. The study used concentrated oil and did not measure clinical daytime sleepiness.
crustacean shell chitosan and human stool — Eight healthy men showed inconclusive weight and moisture differences in a sequential shell chitosan study.

food-related material in an imaging report — One maxillofacial ultrasound case identifies a retained shrimp anatomical fragment in the floor of the mouth. This is a food-related foreign-body observation with no bowel endpoint or stated cooking method.

shell chitosan and constipation events — Defecation frequency was similar across groups and early constipation reports did not differ clearly in pairwise comparisons. The intervention used extracted chitosan.

fish and shrimp fall within a food pattern associated with constipation — Higher southern dietary-pattern score had lower Rome II constipation odds. Fish and shrimp were pooled inside the pattern, alongside many foods. No shrimp-specific association or preparation estimate.
mixed shrimp surimi and mouse constipation — Pellet counts increased with composite shrimp and krill diets and with the fiber-only diet. The model was loperamide constipation rather than Parkinson’s.

clinical case or dietary history without a matched ingredient comparison — An infection case reports debris-cleanup exposure to soft-shelled shrimp. The contact context differs from ingestion and supplies no matched clinical Parkinson outcome.

diagnostic tarragon skin tests and a separate occupational airway reaction — Cutaneous tests verified sensitization to tarragon. Glottal edema followed occupational mugwort exposure. The publication supplies no oral tarragon or speech intelligibility outcome.

measured stride in a multiherb and multimodal regimen — Stride length first increased before the formula containing ginger started and later fell. The case cannot isolate ginger from the other treatments.

ginger-containing mixed decoction and measured stride in a case series — A patient with unconfirmed Parkinson disease and prior infarct increased stride during a formula containing fresh and dried ginger. The confirmed Parkinson case had both stride measurements before its ginger formula.
standardized ginger powder tablets and total MDS-UPDRS — The registry shows recruitment complete and gives no results or separate stride-length measure.

ginger root extract dose comparisons in cohorts including Parkinson disease — Change in MDS-UPDRS Parts I–IV is listed among its other outcomes. No separate stride-length measure, inactive comparator or posted results were verified.
ginger-containing ethanol extract and general mouse motor tasks — The combined extract improved some motor tasks. Stride length and ginger alone were untested.

ginger-containing decoction and stride in a Parkinson mouse model — CatWalk Figure 3L shows longer stride in medium and high whole-decoction groups than MPTP controls. The nine-component recipe includes ginger rhizome and has no isolated ground ginger group.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — The mixed diet study did not report dystonia severity by chervil intake.

topical and diffuser almond oil and actigraphic sleep in memory care — The recovered regression table estimates 371.37 modeled sleep minutes with almond and 413.83 with lavender, difference 42.46 (p = .0084). It supplies no polysomnographic REM or dream-enactment estimate.

whole almonds and REM architecture outside Parkinson disease — Whole almonds versus control in adults with poor sleep showed adjusted REM duration of 37.30 versus 36.43 minutes (p=.776) and REM latency 158.17 versus 158.20 minutes (p=.998). The population lacked a Parkinson or REM sleep behavior disorder requirement, and whole almonds and REM architecture cannot speak directly to swallowed oil and dream enactment.

rapeseed versus palm in a female mouse offspring anxiety assay — Authors reported less anxiety-like behavior in the rapeseed group versus low-ALA palm in the elevated plus maze. The abstract concerned pre- and postnatal developmental diets with pressing unverified.

high-oleic canola and ordinary rapeseed rat anxiety behavior — The Japanese report describes greater anxiety-like behavior for the rapeseed diets versus sunflower comparators and no clear yogurt effect in the high-oleic canola arm. Oil preparation remained unverified.

47 percent rapeseed comparator and measured anxiety in hospital nurses — At 26 weeks the HADS anxiety contrast was +0.13 points (95% CI −0.91 to 1.16). GAD-7 was also inconclusive. The comparison did not isolate rapeseed and oil pressing was unspecified.

optional canola within two Mediterranean diet arms and planned anxiety measures — The 2026 preliminary report supplies metabolic and adherence outcomes, with the planned anxiety comparison still open. Canola is an option within a diet bundle and oil pressing is unspecified.

hydrogenated rapeseed excipient in active microalgae formulation and clinical GAD-7 — Figure 6A gives no significant time or between-group anxiety effect in a low-baseline-anxiety sample. The recorded hydrogenated excipient varies along with the active microalgae compound and is not cold-pressed oil.

developmental diets with engineered high-GLA canola oil vs borage and later maze behavior — Elevated-plus-maze performance showed no significant differences in male mouse offspring. The tested material and developmental design do not estimate the frozen Parkinson claim.

fluoxetine plus rapeseed placebo in a three-arm major-depression trial — Nine of 16 analyzed participants in the fluoxetine plus rapeseed placebo arm reported anxiety, versus one with EPA and three with the combination. Concurrent drug differences prevent an oil-specific interpretation.

anxiety-related behavior after a high-fat prenatal canola diet — Offspring of the two maternal high-fat groups showed anxiety-related behavior on elevated plus maze testing. The reported comparison varied prenatal fat amount and composition and gives no cold-pressed Parkinson contrast.

fortified rapeseed oil and anxiety behavior in metabolic-syndrome mice — The fortified diet improved spatial memory and showed no improvement in anxiety-related behavior. The diet combined multiple additives and used a db/db model.

whole tarragon essential oil and abnormal gait during mouse toxicity observations — Abnormal gait and ataxia were noted during acute injection toxicity screening. No freezing episodes were defined or counted, and the test did not use fresh leaf ingestion.

oral isolated estragole and mouse coordination — Oral estragole and its inclusion complex produced no reported clear change in gross rotarod and selected open-field measures. The study did not score gait freezing or test fresh tarragon.

fatigue and a branded capsule with uncertain study-era oil content — A 232-person functional-fatigue trial favored the supplement over placebo. A later Irish label names refined arachis oil, but study-era excipients and placebo constituents remain unverified.

shared oral peanut oil and binary post-COVID fatigue — The oil-only arm had fatigue at 63/73 at entry and 28/73 at both follow-ups. Both arms got oil. The interaction p=.46 compares added vitamin D, not the oil. Pressing grade is unknown.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The peanut entry describes refined oil used as a drug solvent and residual meal used in feed. Its fungal hazard attaches to kernels or meal, with no tested culinary oil endpoint.

peanut-oil carrier and vehicle controls in a related rat experiment — The published methods list vehicle-injected controls. The comparison addresses corticosterone-related biochemical outcomes and does not estimate oral peanut oil or Parkinson fatigue. Cohort overlap with the meeting abstract remains open.

intraperitoneal peanut oil as the carrier for corticosterone in rats — The verified poster measures hippocampal choline uptake and acetylcholine release. The oil is a non-oral vehicle, with no separately measured oil result for Parkinson fatigue.

injected ungraded oil comparator and stimulated tongue fatigue resistance — Testosterone reduced stimulated tongue muscle endurance against injected peanut oil, while the oestrogen comparison was inconclusive. There was no self-reported or Parkinson fatigue outcome.

peanut-oil vehicle for nanoparticle dopamine in a rat model — Fatigue is clinical background. The oil is the carrier for formulated dopamine, with no independent oil arm, specified pressing method or measured fatigue effect.

oral peanut oil vehicle and stimulated posttetanic muscle response in hens — Potentiation was stable or slightly higher in the oral vehicle group and fell variably after toxicant exposure. The study has no oil-free comparison, verified cold pressing or Parkinson clinical fatigue endpoint.

ethanolic green cardamom fruit extract in induced amnesia models — Maze and avoidance results reflect learning or memory. The experiment does not measure Parkinson attention after consumption of the ground spice.
cardamom oil and memory tasks in rats — Cardamom oil improved memory or locomotor tasks in an aluminum neurotoxicity model. Neither ground spice nor Parkinson attention impairment was evaluated.

14-day black cardamom fruit-extract attention measures — Some early attention estimates favored the extract in healthy adults. Species, formulation and clinical population differ from ground green cardamom in Parkinson’s.

lemon balm extract and computerized reaction tasks outside Parkinson disease — Accuracy changes and inconclusive attention-speed results concerned computer button responses, with no handwriting measure.

dried lemon balm leaf and computerized reaction tasks outside Parkinson disease — Timed tasks measured computerized memory and attention. No letter size or progressive reduction in handwriting was recorded.

daily whole avocado and self-reported nighttime duration-derived score — Damani and colleagues’ ancillary analysis of NCT03528031 found a 3.20-point avocado-versus-habitual-diet change in the nighttime-duration-based Life’s Essential 8 sleep component (95% CI 0.38 to 6.02). oral avocado oil plus mint comparator and measured daytime sleepiness — The avocado comparator arm rose from 1.9 to 2.6 on the Stanford Sleepiness Scale. avocado oil within an oral placebo blend and adverse somnolence — Three somnolence reports occurred in the mixed-oil placebo arm and five in the cannabinoid arm. One placebo participant withdrew with somnolence and other symptoms. The trial contains no oil-specific clinical contrast.

oral adolescent avocado oil protocol family and limited adverse event reporting — ReBEC RBR-255fy6v links an adolescent oral avocado oil trial to the 2024 preliminary report through ethics identifier 61242122.3.0000.0062. dried celery stems and leaves and seated blood pressure — Table 5 lists lower seated medians in both groups, despite conflicting Results prose. Between-arm change p=.334 systolic and p=.751 diastolic. No standing symptoms or Parkinson cohort, and side-effect reporting lacks symptom-level counts.
celery decoction and blood pressure in adults with hypertension — The original abstract reports lower pressure after intervention. Orthostatic lightheadedness and Parkinson’s were not measured.

celery leaf decoction in hypertension under amlodipine — No serious complaints such as dizziness were described, without a separate event count or posture link. The study compared a different leaf decoction and did not involve Parkinson disease.

dried celery-containing mixtures and combined dizziness and headache — Both randomized arms contained dried whole celery and five other herbs. Figure 4 gives disappearance by 27 versus 21 days. The grouped symptom was not linked to standing, and the contrast does not isolate celery.

celery seed extract and the Beck anxiety dizziness item — The primary abstract reports a favorable dizziness item change (p<.001), but supplies no clear between-arm item estimate, posture or Parkinson cohort. Seed extract differs from dried leaf. Full tables remain an access gap.
hydroalcoholic celery leaf extract and fructose-induced hypertension — The rat study reports blood pressure reduction and gives no measure of posture-linked lightheadedness.

cold-pressed hazelnut oil and pentobarbital sleep duration in liver-injured mice — Pentobarbital sleep was shorter with cold-pressed oral hazelnut oil than injury alone in a liver injury assay. The methods and table disagree on oil volume. The experiment measured no daytime sleepiness, toasted oil or Parkinson cohort.
arugula extract in a vascular crossover — Healthy participants showed vascular changes after extract. The intervention did not measure clinical fatigue.

repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking — Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.
raw arugula allergy context — An acute salad-associated reaction presents a different pathway and endpoint. It supplies no Parkinson fatigue outcome.
rocket salad beverage and blood pressure in healthy adults — The beverage changed blood pressure. No fatigue score or Parkinson cohort was reported.

intranasal whole pumpkin in sesame oil and PSQI daytime dysfunction — Among 74 analyzed after 100 were randomized, daytime dysfunction improved by 1.33 points versus 0.00 with paraffin (p < .001). This includes staying awake and enthusiasm, with no item-level estimate. Parkinson was excluded, and comparison did not isolate sesame or test toasted pumpkin seed oil.
oral oil and self-reported anosmia during COVID-19 — The open-label study reported shorter anosmia duration with oil. It did not measure smell-test performance, ground seed or Parkinson disease.
nigella and histology of aged rat olfactory structures — Oral nigella was associated with thicker epithelium and selected structural changes. No odor detection or Parkinson measure was reported.
seed capsules and anosmia prevalence during COVID-19 — The day-10 between-group comparison was inconclusive (p=.529). The study concerned acute infection with self-reported smell loss.

injected isolated carvacrol and reserpine-associated catalepsy — Carvacrol decreased reserpine-associated catalepsy and chewing while open-field activity remained low. It does not measure clinical dystonia or a dried oregano intervention.

injected isolated carvacrol and haloperidol-associated catalepsy — Catalepsy was shorter in two carvacrol groups. Deaths and replacements affect the study sample, and the readout does not estimate dystonia after culinary oregano in people with Parkinson disease.

injected aqueous rosemary extract and mouse rigidity scores — The higher groups had lower rigidity scores and fewer rotations. Rigidity and dystonia are distinct, and the exposure was injected extract.

oral pasteurized watermelon juice and cognitive tasks in postmenopausal women — The cognition companion found no clear cognitive effect and did not measure clinical apathy. The intervention used pasteurized juice outside Parkinson disease.

isolated injected capsaicin and fall reporting — Fall adverse events involved 4 of 189 on capsaicin and 2 of 136 on placebo, with the same event counts. This does not estimate a ground-cayenne or Parkinson fall prevention effect.

oral chili challenge and measured hypotension and bradycardia — Challenge reproduced a marked pressure and pulse decrease. The discussion calls the pepper cayenne without verifying the preparation. No measured falls or Parkinson cohort.

oral chili and an observed brief syncopal event — The original confirms seated syncope after mole poblano without falling to the floor. Systolic pressure and pulse were lower at the nearest half-hour reading. Ground-cayenne exposure and Parkinson fall frequency were unverified.

extract of a related Allium species and measured bowel outcomes in mice — Oral ethanolic extract of A. mongolicum increased fecal excretion and carbon-powder transit in loperamide-treated mice. The study did not expose people with Parkinson's to fresh common chives.

chives in a mixed Parkinson diet with baseline stool form — Bristol Stool Scale results belong to the baseline case-control comparison. Stool collection during the diet was for microbial analyses without a chive-specific constipation severity estimate.

low — A human sensory test estimated thresholds to detect individual carvacrol and thymol odorants in sunflower oil. The study did not test olfactory impairment before and after dried summer savory or enroll a Parkinson cohort.

low — Trained technologists gave different odor-quality ratings at higher lyophilized extract concentrations. A product quality score and a cooked food extract do not measure a clinical change in Parkinson olfactory impairment after dried herb.
fresh sage triturate and urinary urgency sensation — The author's uncontrolled account describes acute increased urge in a subgroup. Frequency and Parkinson exposure are unspecified.

fresh sage tip extract and composite urogenital scale — The Menosan scale contains a bladder-problems item but does not separately report it or urgency frequency. The urogenital composite had no clear between-arm difference. The intervention was fresh-tip extract.

different Salvia species root extract and urinary urgency ratings — An early urgency comparison favored the higher root-extract dose. Week 12 urgency comparisons were inconclusive despite a favorable composite and broad abstract wording. Ground common sage was absent.

different Salvia species root extract versus saw palmetto, urgency item — The 12-week separate urgency contrast was inconclusive (p=.257). Composite storage and frequency favored root extract. Culinary botanical and Parkinson exposure were absent.

pooled bean consumption and self-reported sleep duration or quality — The Chinese cohort found favorable associations for pooled beans. The separate insomnia analysis uses genetically proxied preferences. Canned black beans and Parkinson-related insomnia were not isolated.

PD dietary score including generic beans; insomnia; no canned-black-bean estimate — Whole-diet score is not an intervention or ingredient-specific estimate and cannot establish an insomnia effect of canned black beans.

nasal mustard constituent and acute odor thresholds in healthy volunteers — Detection thresholds for two odors fell after nasal allyl isothiocyanate in a study of 20 healthy adults. Route, population and exposure differ from the frozen claim.

ground white mustard in a combined Parkinson tea and an illustrative smell trajectory — The illustrative subject recorded smell severity zero before and throughout treatment. The 17 selected follow-up cases do not supply a group smell estimate. Ground white mustard was combined with broccoli seed and never compared on its own.

mustard-labeled odor in an early Parkinson comparison — The primary methods name a diluted mustard odor and the published analysis pools odor scores. No mustard-only recognition estimate or ingestion effect is provided.

mustard flavor recognition in Parkinson disease — In the flavor test, 34% of Parkinson participants versus 39% of controls identified the mustard item (p=.809). This measures recognition rather than changing clinical smell impairment after ground seed.

combined broccoli and ground white mustard tea and Parkinson smell reports — The June report describes no improvement in self-reported loss of smell. Smell testing and a mustard-only comparison were absent.

gavage of aqueous cumin fruit extract and rotarod balance in MPTP mice — The extract showed no clear day-5 contrast and longer day-20 rotarod retention. The result concerns a concentrated extract and rodent coordination, with no toasted cumin or clinical postural measure.
Parkinson menu includes a different squash name — The appendix lists Muscat pumpkin and no roasted butternut identification. No separate voice result is given.
identified butternut squash skin contact — The case reports localized hand symptoms after contact. It provides no roasted ingestion or voice measurement.

butternut squash handling and individual oral exposure history — One patient reported contact dermatitis and no cutaneous or systemic reaction when eating either squash. Vocal intensity was unmeasured.

Clove oil gargle and an observed throat symptom composite — Hoarseness is one element of the severe sore-throat grading rule. The human study does not report comprehensibility ratings, dysarthria or a ground-clove meal.

dysarthria temporally associated with concentrated clove oil in one adult — One adult had dysarthria and weakness after an exposure to concentrated clove oil. The original case proposes toxicity without testing the oil and supplies no Parkinson diagnosis, culinary ground clove, or listener intelligibility comparison.
Parkinson trial with inhaled eugenol and clinical scale aggregates — No individual speech item or listener-rated intelligibility appeared in the report. The exposure combines four odorants.

dill as one odor in a post COVID smell-training trial — Forty post-COVID participants were allocated in a protocol that lists dill among 11 odor stimuli and measures smell. No posted results, separate dill arm, culinary leaf preparation, or ingestion were established.

dill pickle odor recognition in Parkinson disease — People with Parkinson disease identified dill pickle odor less often than controls. The later same-group study linked a combined odor score to dopamine transporter measures. The odor served as a test stimulus and the studies did not examine fresh dill consumption.

crushed fennel infusion and combined subjective memory and focus — Among ten infusion recipients with menopausal symptoms, a questionnaire item combining memory, concentration and focus rose from 0 to 12 points (p = .014). Controls did not complete the symptom questionnaire. There was no isolated attention performance test, ground seed ingestion or Parkinson diagnosis.
cardamom listed in multicomponent Parkinson diet and composite UPDRS III — The composite improved and includes rigidity. The authors did not report rigidity item results or isolate cardamom.

Indexed traditional dysphonia indication — A named species and a dysphonia indication are indexed. The primary historical page and preparation remain pending, and clinical voice volume was unmeasured.

boiled named curry leaves and traditional hoarseness use — The original species entry records boiled leaves for hoarseness. It reports no Parkinson cases, vocal intensity, comparative response or clear administration details.
sumac extract in Parkinson-derived fibroblasts — The study measured cellular responses rather than postural stability after consuming sumac.

ground anise and SF-36 vitality in functional dyspepsia — Week-12 mean vitality was 74.5 with anise powder versus 35.7 with cornstarch, after baselines of 51.3 and 52.8. Substantial control deterioration and distinct population and vitality endpoint limit transfer to Parkinson apathy.
anise extract and rodent immobility proxies — Swim and suspension immobility fell, but the outcomes are depression-related proxies and do not measure apathy.

grouped romaine or leaf lettuce and physical function — Higher combined intake was associated with fewer gross physical impairments (HR 0.88). The endpoint excluded handwriting, with no isolated raw romaine or Parkinson result.
raw romaine in a healthy-adult crossover — No handwriting or fine-motor endpoint.

combined anise oil softgel and a premenstrual insomnia item — The insomnia item declined in both arms. Table 5 gives between-group p=.810. The comparison neither isolates anise nor uses ground seed or a Parkinson cohort.

low — Ground anise fruit was tested in menopausal women. The supplement explicitly identifies an MKI insomnia symptom score, with no released arm-level estimate. Total MKI and post-treatment classification cannot identify its direction.

low — Oral seed-oil pretreatment shortened pentobarbital-induced sleeping time in mice and the authors describe no hypnotic effect of pretreatment alone. Drug-induced duration differs from insomnia and the intervention was concentrated oil.

anise seed in a honey mixture evaluated in people with Parkinson disease — Sleep disturbance was recorded as a broad survey symptom. No post-exposure insomnia comparison or ground-seed preparation was reported.

peach juice common carrier in APSEP healthy-volunteer crossover with published tapping and fine motor tests — Mas et al. reported 25 completers. Risperidone impaired finger tapping compared with placebo and haloperidol. Both drugs impaired the fine motor test versus placebo. All arms used 250 mL peach juice. The registry has no posted results, and the published comparisons estimate drug effects.

Eight-week Parkinson diet pattern includes optional peach or persimmon, with composite motor assessment — Original low-fat recipe slices or chops peach in mixed meals; actual food choice and individual intake, hand item outcomes, and peach-specific contrast are not reported.

Parkinson vegetarian diet appendix lists peach; UPDRS III encompasses hand items — Peach intake, raw preparation, individual hand scores, and an ingredient-specific comparison are not reported; outcome is multi-food composite.

injected carvacrol and experimentally elicited oral movements — Carvacrol prevented the increase in vacuous chewing in reserpine rats. It did not restore open-field activity. The experiment differs from dietary fresh thyme and levodopa-related clinical dyskinesia.

luteolin plus palmitoylethanolamide and peak-dose dyskinesia case — A Parkinson case report describes resolution after four months with a combined product and carbidopa/levodopa. Neither fresh thyme nor the separate component effect can be inferred.

mixed oral corticosterone carrier and skilled forelimb reaching — Skilled reaching recovery was poorer with the corticosterone mixture than in lesion controls. Oil grade and contribution were unavailable, and handwriting size was unmeasured.

dietary peanut oil and general motor coordination in mice — Elevated rotarod and grasp outcomes had no significant differences. Low-rotarod retention differed and was interpreted as task behavior or motivation. Rapeseed replaced a portion of peanut oil, oil grade was unspecified, and there was no handwriting or Parkinson outcome.
solid lipid curcumin and manual dexterity — Nine-hole pegboard change did not clearly differ in healthy adults. It was not a handwriting-size or Parkinson outcome.
nanomicelle curcumin and handwriting in a composite scale — Part II includes handwriting, but the report does not provide the item effect or measured lettering size.

safflower oil mixed-meal crossover with peripheral biomarkers — Healthy participants received meals containing safflower oil, cocoa butter or no added fat. The abstract does not give an isolated contrast for the safflower arm, specify pressing method or measure the frozen Parkinson symptom.

safflower crossover and joint mobility and strength in Friedreich ataxia — Strength, joint mobility and stiffness as resistance to passive movement are different outcomes. There was no Parkinson rigidity measurement or cold-press confirmation.

safflower oil and Huntington rigidity scale component — UHDRS includes arm rigidity, but total scores cannot determine the direction of that item. The trial has no pure-oil-versus-background-diet arm and no Parkinson group.

safflower-derived flavonoids in a Parkinson rat model — The intervention was a standardized extract. A 2026 corrigendum remains an open source trail and the study does not identify a culinary oil rigidity effect.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — Prunus domestica occurs in a leaf and seed hazard context and as a species definition. The historical phloridzin attribution and plum-colored names do not test plum consumption.

plum and prune extracts in a rotenone midbrain culture — Neither extract clearly reduced dopaminergic cell loss in the primary rotenone model. There was no poached plum, levodopa or dyskinesia outcome.

plum extract under two toxin conditions in midbrain cultures — Plum extract increased dopaminergic cell survival under paraquat and showed an inconclusive trend under rotenone. These are culture results without whole fruit or dyskinesia.

plum and levodopa in a bench observation — The clinician observed darkening after mixing levodopa powder with pieces of plum. The reported patient had consumed banana. No poached plum ingestion, pharmacokinetic value or dyskinesia outcome.
processed seed-derived glucoraphanin; broad PD outcomes — The compound intervention is not roasted kale and no speech intelligibility result is posted.

Kale juice and caregiver-reported speech in another condition — A caregiver reported more fluent speech and kale-containing juices in a person with dementia and prior strokes. The combined program did not test roasted kale, Parkinson speech or measured intelligibility.

Conference case describes visual hallucinations during use of a rosemary-containing oral multi-herb weight-loss product — The woman had no reported Parkinson disease; product contains several botanicals, fresh culinary leaves and dose are unverified, hallucination frequency is unreported, and concurrent antipsychotic treatment prevents attribution.

Adult case reports visual hallucinations while using multiple supplements including a product listing rosemary extract — No Parkinson diagnosis, fresh culinary rosemary, separate frequency or isolated rosemary exposure was reported; five concurrent supplements and medication started at cessation prevent attribution.

macadamia and olive oil mix with measured gastrointestinal transit — In Markey Chapter 6, macadamia plus olive oil arm gastric half-time averaged 219, 195 and 201 minutes and mouth-to-caecum transit 281, 248 and 276 minutes across control, high-fat and deadaptation. Neither measure showed a significant unadjusted overall trial or trial-by-group result. Clinical constipation and Parkinson disease were outside the study.

whole macadamia nuts and stool frequency and type in a crossover — Bowel frequency did not clearly differ. Bristol type p=.049 lacks direction and phase estimates. The companion and its supplements give no missing bowel data. Whole nuts and cold-pressed oil are different preparations.

intragastric macadamia oil and gastric emptying — Free oleic acid emptied more slowly than macadamia oil emulsion in nine healthy men. The study used an intragastric preparation and measured gastric emptying, not constipation.

pressed macadamia oil and composite colitis stool signs in mice — The gavaged oil lowered a colitis disease activity index including stool consistency and bleeding. The model measures acute colitis and loose stool, with no clinical constipation outcome.

blackberry intake and general sleep difficulty — Blackberry intake including recipe ingredients was associated with lower odds of general sleep difficulty (OR .63, 95% CI .40–.97). The analysis has no REM dream enactment measure or Parkinson subgroup.

Chives listed in multi-ingredient Parkinson diet, preparation and individual amount unclear; no apathy result — Baseline UPDRS I total and a motor follow-up total do not establish an apathy item change or isolate chive exposure; apathy direction remains unknown.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S1.97 models a spinach-derived peptide and S6.409 examines spinach thylakoids. Neither tests raw spinach consumption or dyskinesia.

isolated peptide in a mouse anxiety test with a different exposure and endpoint — The original Hirata abstract reports elevated-plus-maze responses to rubiscolin-6. There is no Parkinson model, whole spinach arm or dyskinesia measure.

low — A ketogenic diet menu offered an uncooked spinach-or-kale salad; one participant in that arm had worsened dyskinesia and medication reductions. The report lacks participant-level spinach consumption, an isolated food contrast and dyskinesia-specific group scores. Composite motor complication changes do not estimate spinach effect.

spinach and okra intake history and oxalate nephropathy — More oxalate-rich vegetables were consumed before kidney injury in a post-bypass patient. No single-food comparator, spinach preparation, dyskinesia or visual hallucination endpoint was reported.
pooled spinach and leek intake in a Parkinson cohort — The weekly intake category pools both vegetables and reports no raw spinach or dyskinesia effect estimate.
raw carrot and stool bulk in healthy volunteers — Wet stool weight rose 142 to 177 g/day, but transit stayed at 3.0 days. Uncontrolled, raw preparation and no constipation severity.

reported food categories and overeating — LBP2.005 includes carrot as a named candidate in Table 1. Neither group reported an overeating occurrence for carrot. Its thermal preparation and the frozen symptom were not assessed.
constipation in a case reporting unusually high carrot intake — The single case describes co-occurrence during extreme intake with no standard preparation or comparative symptom estimate.

randomized Parkinson constipation comparison with a Mediterranean diet — Both arms improved, and the between-arm symptom change was inconclusive (p=.60). There was no isolated steamed carrot exposure.
concentrated carrot fiber and stool weight — Reported 59% greater stool weight, no carrot-arm sample or constipation symptom estimate in the abstract.
carrot preparation and measured stool bulk in controlled feeding — Fecal weight increased with raw or processed carrots. Steamed carrots and clinical Parkinson constipation severity were not studied.

safflower oil mixed-meal crossover with peripheral biomarkers — Healthy participants received meals containing safflower oil, cocoa butter or no added fat. The abstract does not give an isolated contrast for the safflower arm, specify pressing method or measure the frozen Parkinson symptom.

safflower comparator safety reporting in Huntington disease — Diarrhea is the only EU event term listed. The safety timeframe and comparator labels limit attribution, and no fall-specific count was available.

safflower and fish-oil crossover with lipid and inflammatory endpoints — The later publications and official protocol represent one study family. Some biomarker directions differed by oil, with no swallowing, falls or anxiety measure and no verified cold-pressed grade.

USP oil and systematic falls collection in Friedreich ataxia — Five of 32 on safflower and seven of 33 on RT001 had a fall in 12 months. The comparison uses an active drug and no baseline fall frequency. Parkinson and cold-press grade remain unresolved.

oral safflower comparison in a progressive supranuclear palsy trial — US registry names safflower and the EU record lists global study end. No pressing method, fall count or posted comparative results.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — No herb-specific depressive symptom outcome was reported.
individual Parkinson symptoms and diet scores — A Healthy Diet Indicator association was reported without a fresh chervil contrast.
multi-ingredient preparation and total motor score — The registered formula includes ginger. The planned motor score is aggregate and no results were located.

measured rigidity in a multiherb and multimodal regimen — Rigidity was unchanged in the last measurement interval after adding the formula containing fresh ginger. The uncontrolled case leaves attribution unresolved.

ginger-containing multi-ingredient formula and pooled swallowing outcomes — One participant had Parkinson in the mixed ten-person series. No participant-specific outcome or rigidity result was reported. The formula does not isolate grated ginger.

ginger extract and listed MDS-UPDRS Parts I–IV — The official registration lists a scale that includes rigidity, with no separate item outcome or posted results. Both dosing arms receive ginger root extract capsules.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — P-862 reviews ginger and weight or fat loss, without a frozen Parkinson endpoint.

original study or review context for the exposure and endpoint — The review's constituent evidence describes persisting post-levodopa abnormal movements in mice and other model outcomes. No grated ginger rigidity comparison.

ginger-containing extract and pharyngeal reflex latency — Recovered journal text gives an assessor-blinded comparison of a five-plant extract versus lactate. Reflex latency improved within the extract group; rigidity and grated culinary ginger were untested.

isolated zingerone and post-levodopa hindlimb stiffening in mice — The linked journal and investigator grant report concern the same constituent-in-lesion protocol. With injected levodopa, oral zingerone did not clearly suppress observed post-dose hindlimb stiffening. No arm-level stiffness counts, quantified rigidity scale or clinical grated-ginger result were provided.

ginger extract and shoulder hardness in healthy adults — The mechanical comparison was inconclusive. Subjective stiffness improved in one age/sex subgroup. Distinct from Parkinson passive rigidity and grated ginger.

isolated 6-shogaol and catalepsy in a rotenone model — The Figure 4 data show shorter forelimb withdrawal latency than rotenone controls. The sentence about increased inflexibility conflicts with the figure. It is an isolated compound and animal proxy, with no clinical rigidity outcome.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The peanut entry describes refined oil used as a drug solvent and residual meal used in feed. Its fungal hazard attaches to kernels or meal, with no tested culinary oil endpoint.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — The arsenic model compares a chelator in peanut oil with a saline carrier. Peanut agglutinin is a separate laboratory reagent.

peanut-oil carrier and vehicle controls in a related rat experiment — The published methods list vehicle-injected controls. The comparison addresses corticosterone-related biochemical outcomes and does not estimate oral peanut oil or Parkinson rigidity. Cohort overlap with the meeting abstract remains open.

intraperitoneal peanut oil as the carrier for corticosterone in rats — The verified poster measures hippocampal choline uptake and acetylcholine release. The oil is a non-oral vehicle, with no separately measured oil result for Parkinson rigidity.

Parkinsonian primate rigidity with an injected drug vehicle — All three later treated monkeys developed rigidity after MPTP. There was no isolated rigidity effect after the drug in peanut oil and no oral oil comparison.
rocket aroma and flavor ratings by genotype — Some taste genotypes rated the product's aroma less strongly. General olfactory impairment in Parkinson disease was outside the study.
fresh salad rocket aroma as sensory stimulus — Assessors rated fresh leaf aroma. The comparison does not measure improvement in clinical smell function after eating arugula.
common bean pod extract and rat memory tests — Memory-task changes followed methanol pod extract under pharmacological challenges. Cooked green pods and clinical executive function were untested.

mixed garden produce distribution — The garden reported distribution of green beans, kale, chard and watermelon within a mixed harvest. The evaluation concerns program delivery without an ingredient-specific intake or clinical symptom measurement.

cooked market common bean feed and rodent memory and beam testing — The original does not identify immature green pods and contains a group labeling discrepancy. Animal tasks do not measure human executive impairment.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — The arsenic model compares a chelator in peanut oil with a saline carrier. Peanut agglutinin is a separate laboratory reagent.

peanut-oil carrier and vehicle controls in a related rat experiment — The published methods list vehicle-injected controls. The comparison addresses corticosterone-related biochemical outcomes and does not estimate oral peanut oil or Parkinson dystonia. Cohort overlap with the meeting abstract remains open.

intraperitoneal peanut oil as the carrier for corticosterone in rats — The verified poster measures hippocampal choline uptake and acetylcholine release. The oil is a non-oral vehicle, with no separately measured oil result for Parkinson dystonia.

dystonic postures in a levodopa-treated primate model — The narratives document dystonia and dystonic postures. Drug in subcutaneous oil changed combined dyskinesia severity, with no separate dystonia effect or matched oil-only arm.

depleted Syrian oregano stems in a bay leaf trial comparator — The 25-person Origanum syriacum stem comparator changed from 50.32 to 50.76 on the paper's STAI measure (reported p=.8846). The study compared it with bay leaf and did not include a no-oregano comparator. Species, plant part, depletion and population limit transfer to culinary dried oregano in Parkinson disease.

reported oregano use and global nonmotor measures in a Parkinson cohort — Section 3.5 reports exploratory corrected analyses using HADS total and NMSS. No oregano-specific HADS anxiety estimate, preparation or amount was reported. Table 4 p=.506 compares exposure across ethnic groups.

injected oregano extract and open-maze behavior in rats — Open-arm entries and time increased, while locomotor activity declined. Preparation, route and behavioral endpoints differ from clinical anxiety after dried oregano.

forehead Origanum vulgare oil exposure and depression scales — Mean depression scores declined in a 200-person paired analysis without a concurrent control. Anxiety estimates, oral dried leaves and Parkinson status were outside the reported comparison.

topical marjoram-containing blend and HADS anxiety in rheumatoid arthritis — HADS favored blended massage over usual care. No clear direct difference from almond-oil massage. The earlier and later reports belong to one trial. Matched effect estimates remain inaccessible.
oral six-spice capsule with broad mental health outcome — The trial plans SF-36 mental health and excludes Parkinson disease. There are no posted outcomes and oregano is one of six ingredients.

topical marjoram compared with carrier massage and planned GAD-7 after stroke — The completed pilot plans GAD-7 and PHQ-9 and supplies no posted outcomes. It uses sweet marjoram in a topical carrier and involves stroke survivors.

marjoram tea oxidative biomarkers and published registry date discrepancy — The later report and official registry differ on the dates of conduct. Outcomes are biochemical and no clinical anxiety result is supplied. Participant overlap with the earlier symptom study is unverified.

oregano among suggested culinary herbs — The original protocol lists oregano among suggested culinary herbs. It does not verify participant-level dried preparation or intake. Edited testimonials report outcomes for the combined program without a separate anxiety severity comparison for this ingredient.
original source context with different preparation, outcome, attribution or population — The paper cites eugenol from several sources including oregano. No dried-oregano or clinical anxiety outcome.

oral isolated carvacrol and mouse maze behavior — Abstract reports more open-arm exploration and inconclusive locomotor and sleep assays. Related thesis corroborates the model and route and disagrees on one sample size. Neither source tested a culinary herb.

injected oregano leaf extract and mouse light–dark behavior — 60 mg/kg injection increased time in light by 35% (p = .046). Oral dosing tested a different behavior. Neither establishes the symptom after oral dried oregano.

injected synthetic carvacryl acetate and mouse anxiety-like assays — The original Results report more open-arm behavior and fewer marbles buried. The abstract says more marbles were buried; Figure 4 remains visually unverified. This is a synthetic derivative and no culinary comparison was given.

injected beta-caryophyllene and acute mouse behavior — More open-arm time and less immobility in behavioral tests followed injection of isolated beta-caryophyllene. This does not establish a clinical outcome from the food preparation.

isolated carvacrol and safety measures outside Parkinson disease — The original abstract reports labs and pulmonary measures, without an anxiety analysis. A likely related 2019 paper names a registration and excludes psychiatric disorders. Full safety tables remain open.

strained marjoram tea and total nonmotor and depressive outcomes in Parkinson disease — Among 51 completers, total NMSS and BDI declined within the tea group. The accessible data lack anxiety-specific outcomes and the dried marjoram was strained as an infusion.

oral oregano extract and anxiety-related behavior in chronically stressed rats — Maze and open-field measures ran opposite to the worsening hypothesis in this model. The exposure was an extract and the experiment did not measure anxiety in Parkinson disease.

oregano leaf hexane extract and rat anxiety-like behavior in hepatic encephalopathy — The extract attenuated anxiety-like changes in the toxicant model, which differs from the frozen preparation and disease.

dried ground oregano in healthy soldiers and exercise blood biomarkers — The 500 mg dried plant capsule is close to the named preparation. In 24 healthy soldiers, creatine kinase was lower than starch at 60 and 120 minutes (both p < 0.0001). The study measured no anxiety or patient fatigue scale and did not specify plant part. No symptom direction transfers.
inhaled marjoram oil and human state anxiety — No significant between-arm difference in state anxiety or anxiety VAS. Species, route and population differ.

five-herb oral extract and locomotor-confounded rat behavior — The high-volume mixture gave more open-arm entries (p<.05) but inconclusive open-arm duration (p>.05). Activity also increased. No single-herb contrast or clinical endpoint.

dried oregano leaf infusion and motor-confounded mouse exploration — Leaf infusion reduced mouse hole exploration at 750 and 1000 mg/kg; the higher dose also impaired motor coordination in rotarod and chimney tasks. Sedation or motor impairment confounds behavioral interpretation, and no clinical anxiety was measured.

pomegranate formulation and adverse-event time ordering after stroke — A psychiatric event with auditory hallucinations is reported in one of eight assigned POMx. It began before the first administration. No visual-hallucination outcome, raw arils or Parkinson group.

nanoemulsified pomegranate seed oil and planned Parkinson hallucinations measure — The planned NMSS covers hallucinations and combines frequency with severity. No item-level data or outcomes publication were verified. The intervention is a nanoformulated oil capsule.

aquatic fennel oil and immobility in scopolamine zebrafish — Fennel oil did not clearly change immobility duration in the novel tank assay. The outcome was swimming immobility in a scopolamine cognitive impairment model, without gait, oral seed or Parkinson measurements.

aqueous fennel fruit extract and locomotor tasks in an MPTP model — The conference abstract reports improvement across open-field, rotarod and passive-avoidance results without endpoint estimates. No freezing episodes or toasted seed ingestion were reported.

oral fennel essence and locomotion in reserpine rats — The oil plus reserpine group III had an open-field mean of 332.17 versus 4.25 in reserpine-only group II. The previous 32.50 came from levodopa/carbidopa group IV. This is a descriptive locomotor comparison without a freezing measure or toasted seeds.

fennel seed in shared Parkinson diet and composite motor examination — Appendix A lists fennel seed in a two-week diet offered to both intervention groups. The one-year composite UPDRS III result gives no separate freezing episodes or isolated toasted fennel exposure.

fennel seed methanolic extract and motor coordination in 6-OHDA rats — Peri-lesion gavage improved rotarod and wire-grasp outcomes at day 14 (p < .05), while the course started after the lesion had no clear effect. These tests did not track freezing episodes and the extract was not toasted seed.
culinary sumac extract against bacterial urinary isolates — Laboratory inhibition of urinary bacterial isolates supplies no participant-level urgency data.

fragrant sumac bark pumpkin oil and hop trial with planned urgency diary — Only seven active and two placebo participants received treatment. Early termination left urgency efficacy analysis unreported. The 2019 uncontrolled report is a separate cohort and the bark differs from culinary ground fruit.
fragrant sumach bark in an overactive bladder combination — Urination frequency changed in a noninterventional study of a mixture containing a different Rhus species and bark.
injected sumac extract and mouse open-field activity — No significant open-field activity change was reported. The assay did not measure shortened stride.
