Peach juice carrier in healthy volunteer antipsychotic protocol; planned drug-induced postural instability measure — Juice is used in all drug and placebo arms; no peach contrast, no raw fruit, no idiopathic Parkinson disease, and no posted results.

Multi-food low-fat Parkinson menu includes optional peach and a pre-existing falls case — Composite motor scores and one participant with pre-existing postural hypotension and ongoing falls do not isolate peach or establish a direction for postural instability.

Parkinson vegetarian diet appendix lists peach; UPDRS III encompasses postural stability — Peach intake, raw preparation, individual postural score, and an ingredient-specific comparison are not reported; outcome is multi-food composite.
inhaled seven-oil blend and rotarod gait measures in model mice — The patent does not isolate rosemary. Its models, oil route and behavioral tasks differ from the frozen claim.
isolated rosmarinic acid and Parkinson-model rotarod — Rotarod performance favored pre-exposure isolated rosmarinic acid. No fresh rosemary or clinical postural instability endpoint.
hydrodistilled rosemary oil and healthy-mouse rotarod — Figure 4 shows shorter latency in the highest oil group. The Results prose gives a conflicting direction. The endpoint is rotarod coordination.
whole-leaf infusion and adult perceived stress or anxiety — Tea reduced stress and anxiety in healthy adults compared with depleted oregano-stem infusion. Motivation and apathy were unmeasured.

oral bay leaf decoction and rat exploration or immobility — Higher bay concentration increased swim immobility from control mean 43.87 to 114.6 seconds despite favorable abstract wording. Low concentration outcome and open-field measures differ. No apathy task.

healthy adult inhaled leaf-volatiles and task-related subjective ratings — Higher exposure altered mood and clarity ratings and the questionnaire included activity level. It had no validated apathy measure.

Rosemary extract gargle in postoperative patients; GRBAS hoarseness rather than acoustic loudness — Table 2 and narrative disagree on hoarseness significance; non-PD, nonculinary exposure and different endpoint prevent directional inference.

rosemary in mixed throat spray and composite symptom response — Twenty-minute response 19/26 vs 14/34, p=.019. Three-day comparison p=.42. The published control heading conflicts with Methods and percentages. No separate hoarseness or voice loudness estimate.

Topical rosemary extract in postoperative patients; hoarseness rather than low voice volume — Abstract reports lower hoarseness at 2 and 6 hours, not 24 hours; topical extract, non-PD population and endpoint mismatch preclude inference about dried culinary leaves and low voice volume.

aqueous garlic extract and urinary frequency in prostate disease — Reported void frequencies fell in two uncontrolled prostate disease groups. The paper uses nocturia and daily frequency wording and gives no separate urgency result. The intervention was soaked garlic extract.

habitual garlic intake and benign prostatic hyperplasia odds — Higher frequency of garlic intake was associated with lower case odds. The study measured diagnosis rather than urinary urgency and gives no cooked preparation or Parkinson sample.

Human eugenol exposure and a face-related judgment task — Participants rated trustworthiness in displayed faces after odor exposure. No score captured their own facial expressiveness, Parkinson hypomimia or dietary clove.
Randomized Parkinson multi-odor study with aggregate motor scores — The study gives no result for MDS-UPDRS item 3.2 facial expression. Part III was reported as a whole and no food was provided.

Mixed oral extract, aggregate neurological score and everyday activities — Table 8 NIHSS and Table 9 Barthel feeding or dressing independence do not give a finger-dexterity estimate or a Parkinson comparison.

Actual herb seasoning in test meals for older adults — Meal liking, flavor and protein intake were measured, with no dexterity test. Dill was one of several spices and fresh versus dried was not specified.

injected dill leaf and other extracts in rodent movement tests — Higher leaf and fruit extracts reduced simple locomotion. This neither assesses hand dexterity nor identifies an effect from eating fresh dill weed.

Oral concentrated sowa extract and animal motor coordination — Animal rotarod retention improved in an alcohol-withdrawal assay. It supplies no fresh culinary leaf measure, human dexterity score, or Parkinson diagnosis.

oral avocado oil comparator and timed psychomotor symbol transcription — Correct symbols rose from 65.7 to 71.8 with the avocado arm and from 68.0 to 74.5 with CBD. The journal p=.43 and the registry p=.6331 use different reported analyses. The journal lists a 90-second test, versus 60 in the registry and protocol. No separate dexterity measure, oil-free arm or refined specification.
mixed vegetables and device adverse event — The case describes a bezoar with a jejunal tube. Parkinson symptom severity was reported stable.

groups sofrito and motivation within a Parkinson diet-pattern analysis — Adjusted diet scores were inversely associated with lack of motivation. The sofrito item permits tomato sauce, gives no isolated leek result and was tested against total symptom burden, not an apathy endpoint.

sweet almond oil patch during balance exercise and sway in older adults — In 56 older adults at risk of falling, Thai boxing with an essential-oil patch versus Thai boxing with a sweet almond oil patch differed on eyes-closed postural sway area and center-of-pressure velocity (p=.04 and p=.001). Fear of falling showed no time-by-group difference (p=.32). Actual fall incidence was not measured, and the patch delivered aroma from clothing.

almond skin extract and larval mobility in a 6-OHDA model — An acetonic almond-skin extract in a zebrafish 6-OHDA model gave a nonsignificant lower-dose distance signal and greater immobility with higher-dose co-exposure versus selected control and extract groups. This is a mobility proxy, using almond skin extract rather than dietary oil, with no fall counts.

Multiherb medicine with cardamom fruit in depression, not Parkinson apathy — Patent describes depression composite scores following a multiherb mixture and randomized withdrawal; no cardamom-specific effect, apathy score, or PD population.

MPTP mouse akinesia and abnormal steps with isolated capsaicin — The poster describes abnormal steps and akinesia apparently normalized by pretreatment, with no significant overall gait difference, episode definition, freezing count or ground-paprika exposure.

low — Institutional abstract describes milk and three other beverages in 30 volunteers; sustained-vowel acoustic measures showed no significant differences. The abstract does not report listener speech intelligibility, Parkinson participants, milk processing or full study methods.

low — A longitudinal corticobasal-degeneration case had progressively impaired intelligibility and later a mixed diet including milk when essentially mute. isolated eugenol and bar catalepsy in MPTP mice — Two higher pretreatment doses reduced catalepsy and post-treatment produced no clear improvement. The study did not test allspice or human muscle rigidity.

oral common-chive leaf extract with sensorimotor and memory outcomes in a stroke model — The abstract describes memory and sensorimotor results after oral common-chive leaf extract. It supplies no anxiety outcome.

food-frequency chili intake and composite including timed walking — Usual-pace four-meter walking was measured, and chili intake was assessed separately from sweet pepper. The study published chili estimates for the composite sarcopenia definition, without a chili-specific walking estimate or ground preparation.

oral red chili extract and treadmill endurance — Time to exhaustion was longer with extract. Velocity was set before each graded test, so ordinary walking slowness could not be estimated. The intervention was a formulated extract in healthy overweight adults.

cayenne capsules and electronically measured maximal sprint speed — Nineteen healthy athletes showed similar fastest and average repeated sprint times during commercial cayenne and placebo. Combined gastrointestinal symptoms increased. No ordinary walking assessment or Parkinson sample.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — Lovage is among the menu ingredients with no individual apathy outcome or verified drying status.
individual Parkinson symptoms and diet scores — Apathy associations were inconclusive at the pattern level and no dried lovage item was analyzed.
MPTP mouse model; dried whole-plant methanolic extract; motor tasks — Mouse beam and drag measures do not assess dystonia in people consuming fresh leaves.
rice bran in a multicomponent fiber bar — The open-label study found no clear constipation or bowel-frequency change after the bar. It provides no refined rice bran oil contrast.

defatted rice bran and stool form in adults — Normal stool-form prevalence increased after defatted bran. The formulation is fiber-containing and defatted, and the participants did not have Parkinson disease.

rice bran oil in a four-oil blend and stool measures — The blend improved stool outcomes in loperamide-treated mice. Rice bran oil comprised 26.02%, with no individual oil arm or Parkinson population.

registered fermented rice bran bowel diary trial — The trial follows bowel movement counts and stool consistency, with results unpublished. The intervention is fermented bran food in generally healthy adults.

Pimenta dioica alcoholic leaf extract and motor toxicity in mice — Original oral toxicity observations include sedation and motor incoordination. The authors discuss alcohol. The preparation, animal behavior and lack of a hand task leave the frozen handwriting outcome unresolved.

chive leaf extract and cognition after cerebral ischemia in mice — The experiment reports behavioral changes in a stroke model. It gives no executive-function outcome for people with Parkinson disease who consume fresh chives.

oral oil vehicle and objective REM-atonia measures in a tauopathy model — Among nine PS19 mice with an REM behavior disorder phenotype, DORA-12 lowered percentage REM without atonia relative to peanut oil vehicle (p = .004). The report gives no separate effect of oil or declared grade.

oral drug formulation and REM stage duration in an Alzheimer model — Diphenhydramine increased dark-phase REM time relative to vehicle (p = .0365). Oil was named in the oral formulation, and the study supplies no isolated oil contrast or dream enactment data.

grapeseed nanocapsule core and antipsychotic-related oral dyskinesia in rats — An injected drug formulation with a grapeseed oil core partly attenuated acute involuntary chewing, and all loaded nanoformulations attenuated it after repeated dosing. Dystonia severity and oral culinary exposure were not tested.

injected isolated eugenol and pentobarbital loss of righting — Eugenol prolonged the barbiturate-induced loss-of-righting interval (p=.002). Spontaneous sleep, insomnia and oral ground allspice were unmeasured.

eugenol formulations and behavior after induced REM loss — The rat study measured post-deprivation sensorimotor and learning tasks. It provides no sleep recovery or insomnia estimate for ground allspice.

contrasting associations of serum carrot-associated carotenoids with sleepiness in general adults — In NHANES Table 4 Model 2, sleepiness factors were inversely associated with serum alpha-carotene and positively associated with beta-carotene. Other specifications were inconclusive. No raw carrot intervention, Parkinson cohort or separate Epworth estimate was involved.

diet-pattern scores and excessive sleepiness before diagnosis — Higher pattern scores were associated with lower odds of excessive daytime sleepiness. The cohort excluded diagnosed Parkinson's and the exposure was a whole diet score.
diet-pattern scores and measured Parkinson daytime sleepiness — The Parkinson analysis did not report a significant diet-pattern association with daytime sleepiness or separate raw carrot.

plant-rich and time-restricted nutrition with Epworth scores in people with Parkinson disease — The six-month trial's Table 2 shows Epworth means 6.65 to 6.5 in controls and 6.55 to 6.7 with personalized nutrition, with post-test p=1.000. The whole program had several components and the report supplies no carrot-specific intake or contrast.

isolated eugenol and mouse immobility — The primary abstract describes antidepressant-like performance in forced swim and tail suspension tests, with hippocampal biomarkers. The food exposure and a patient mood outcome remain unmeasured.

oral isolated eugenol and rodent behavior — Fourteen days of isolated eugenol was associated with no significant behavioral changes in a mouse safety study including tail suspension. The design provides no Parkinson or culinary estimate.

isolated eugenol nanoemulsion and rodent behavior — Intranasal delivery using a clove-oil phase changed locomotor and forced-swim outcomes. Motor effects and formulation limit inference for ground allspice or Parkinson mood.

oral isolated eugenol and depression-like outcomes after paraquat — The primary abstract reports improvement in social interaction and tail-suspension immobility after toxin exposure, without numerical behavioral estimates. Literature linkage and culinary Parkinson exposure remain unresolved.

injected allspice leaf extract and rat CNS suppression — Fresh leaf extracts injected in rats decreased general CNS activity. The 14-day oral fraction experiment measured pressure, heart rate and weight. Neither reported depressive behavior or ground allspice berries.
strain-defined fermented milk — The trial found constipation and aggregate nonmotor signals with the specific preparation.

whole walnut snack and short-term salivary flow — Flow did not clearly increase after the walnut snack. This is whole-nut chewing in 12 adults and salivary production, with no drooling score or Parkinson population.

human leaf-volatiles and visual vigilance — Low-exposure inhalation preserved a late true-hit index, and high exposure had a faster reaction time at one time point. Other subjective responses differed.
whole-leaf incense and animal cognition — The exposed scopolamine group had better measures of spatial memory. It did not receive ground leaf by mouth or model Parkinson attention.

bay leaf volatiles and visual vigilance in an earlier controlled human report — At the lower odor load the reported 30-minute contrast had p=.026. The higher load did not clearly differ. Shared team and task leave participant overlap with the later report unresolved. The exposure was inhaled.
nigella-derived melanin and registered reflux endpoints — Registry specifies GERD-Q and general safety, without a distinct dysphagia measure or whole-ground seed assignment. No posted results.

nigella oil mouth rinse and self-reported oral intake during chemotherapy — Table 2 reports favorable early normal-food tolerance and 26/27 versus 20/25 normal-diet counts on day 28 (p=.159). One nigella recipient was on a liquid diet, qualifying the broad abstract assertion. Topical oil in mucositis does not test ingested ground seed or neurogenic swallowing.

self-selected Parkinson records with ground white mustard in a mixed seed tea — The 2024 primary report names ground white mustard in the preparation. Symptoms were self-rated and could be modified. Selected records omit any visual hallucination frequency result and the study did not isolate mustard.

pediatric kidney bean allergy and cross-reactivity — The children experienced immediate hives or facial swelling following ingestion. The observations do not measure Parkinson drooling or visual hallucinations.

pooled legume or bean intake and whole-diet general hallucinations scores — Table 2 reports general hallucinations against whole diet scores. Table S4 evaluates pooled bean or legume intake against aggregate symptom burden and does not identify species or preparation. It does not quantify visual hallucination frequency.

acute gastrointestinal illness after inadequately cooked kidney beans — The outbreak investigation supports an undercooking-related gastrointestinal exposure. It did not monitor hallucination frequency or ordinary cooked kidney bean ingestion in Parkinson's.
fresh green kiwi and subjective waking alertness — Fresh kiwi yielded 53.1 versus 44.2 for water (p = .082) on waking alertness. The trial had no objective attention test or Parkinson cohort.

freeze-dried kiwi and planned computerized cognitive testing — The registry plans COMPASS cognitive testing after evening freeze-dried kiwi in men with poor sleep. No published result, raw kiwi arm or Parkinson population is recorded.

previously frozen green kiwi pulp and attention tasks in healthy adults — The breakfast crossover found no clear treatment or treatment-by-time effect on choice reaction time or Stroop. ACTRN12615001259538 records the same tests. The linked Mishra metabolic report describes 200 g peeled Hayward pulp stored frozen and re-frozen after crushing. The crossover compared cereal meals in healthy volunteers and gives no Parkinson-specific estimate.

green versus gold kiwi meal and porcine brain bioamines — The author abstract and matching dissertation experiment describe 48 pigs, post-meal GABA and other bioamine trajectories by cultivar. Tissue analysis is a biochemical endpoint, not a human attention performance measure. The two cultivar meals also differ in fiber and other nutrients.

hoarseness during supervised whole roasted hazelnut challenges in children — Table 1 records hoarseness in three children during food challenges with finely ground roasted whole hazelnuts. The separate oil-body experiments used immunoblotting. The clinical study provides no cold-pressed edible-oil challenge, acoustic loudness measure or Parkinson cohort.

pooled voice and throat symptoms in a pediatric food-allergy cohort — Dysphonia, pruritus or throat constriction occurred in 22 of 88 children in a pooled food-allergy cohort. Results were not attributable to a single food or separately to reduced vocal loudness. The study did not use cold-pressed hazelnut oil or enroll Parkinson patients.

lipidated curcumin, PSQI daytime dysfunction and older adults — Table S12 shows 1/38 versus 9/38 worsened at week 12 and 1/38 versus 2/38 improved, with p=.018 for the full category comparison. Daytime dysfunction is a combined component and no separate Epworth or item result was identified.
Parkinson curcumin and overall sleep quality — Nanomicelle curcumin improved global PSQI in a small trial. ESS or daytime-dysfunction component scores were not reported.

turmeric-extract combination and registered PSQI daytime dysfunction — Biomarker-selected chronic pain intervention combines turmeric, black pepper, ashwagandha and olive-leaf extracts. Registry adds no observed daytime functioning or sleepiness data.
rhizome capsules and sleepiness reports — EMA's account of the trial describes sleepiness reported across turmeric and comparison groups, with no arm-specific count or validated scale.
turmeric extract and mouse sleep promotion — Oral extract shortened sleep latency and increased non-REM sleep in mice. Daytime sleepiness and Parkinson disease were not assessed.
curcumin and Epworth daytime sleepiness — A randomized curcumin study outside Parkinson found inconclusive Epworth and severity results. Both arms received piperine.

oral aqueous tarragon extract and sprint performance — The recreationally trained men received creatine in both crossover periods. Peak power, mean power and work had no clear group-by-time interaction. Clinical fatigue and dried culinary tarragon were unmeasured.

ethanolic tarragon extract and voluntary exercise metabolism — Obese mice receiving extract had greater fat oxidation during matched wheel-running bouts. The study does not provide a fatigue outcome and the published corrigendum is open.

corn oil vehicle shared by both estradiol comparison arms in rats — The author abstract attributes odor discrimination and recovery differences to the estradiol comparison on a common injection background.

corn oil preference by mouse olfactory-model status — Experimentally altered olfaction preceded the oil-choice task. Normal mice preferred a wider concentration range. The study does not estimate smell changes after oil intake.

corn oil feed and measured canine odor thresholds — Behavioral olfactometry tested corn, coconut and beef-tallow diets with conditioning strata. The reported deterioration concerned unconditioned dogs on coconut oil. Trial results do not establish corn-induced worsening.

maize oil addition and canine odor detection crossover — Maize oil diet improved adjusted near-threshold detection against a distinct high-fat diet. Comparisons with the original low-fat maintenance diet and tests of absolute odor thresholds showed no clear differences. Refining and Parkinson disease were unmeasured.
corn oil injection sham in mouse olfactory training — The reported pellet-finding times separate injury and training arms from an injected sham. No oil-only dietary comparison.

injected corn oil vehicle and measured mouse olfaction — The control and toxin groups had matched injected corn oil. Olfactory differences reflect toxin or training contrasts on a shared vehicle background.

low — The original supplement shows total UPDRS III trajectories at fourteen days. It does not supply a hand-task, pegboard, oil-grade, or individual oil intake comparison in the Parkinson diet trial.

low — Mung bean extract prepared in heated pumpkin oil was compared with separate soybean oil extracts and other treatments. The authors report wire-hanging and falls during the task. Neither arm isolates oil, and suspension endurance differs from hand dexterity.

low — A Cucurbita extract improved rat rotarod coordination in a cuprizone model. The primary abstract does not identify culinary oil. Rotarod performance and the demyelination model differ from hand dexterity in Parkinson’s.
dried marjoram as a sensory stimulus — Only 31% recognized the single odor despite some participants reporting culinary use. This does not compare a change in general olfaction after ingestion.

dried marjoram diagnostic smell identification — Workbook counts are 1/34 Parkinson and 5/53 controls. The paper found no clear group difference for marjoram. The test used sniffing and gives no clinical result after eating dried marjoram.

topical fresh dill preparation and hemodialysis sleep quality — The trial reported lower follow-up Pittsburgh sleep scores with topical dill than with comparators, with inconsistent baseline reporting. The route, preparation, sleep measure and dialysis population differ from the frozen claim.
reduced spontaneous locomotion after injected dill extracts — Dose-dependent locomotor changes are described as sedative, with no direct sleep or insomnia assessment. Part and preparation differ.

oral dill tablet and premenstrual sleep quality — The study reported better Pittsburgh sleep scores for dill tablets than placebo. Plant part was unreported, and general sleep quality in premenstrual syndrome does not measure Parkinson insomnia.

dill extract beverage and registered sleep quality outside Parkinson disease — The official record lists Thai PSQI as a six-week secondary outcome and gives no published arm results. This is sleep quality under an extract beverage.

related Zanthoxylum oil inhalation with exercise and postural sway — The eyes-closed velocity comparison favored intervention at four weeks and follow-up. Dynamic reach and fear of falling had inconclusive interactions. Related species and inhalation do not identify ground Sichuan pepper.

related pepper species and animal coordination proxy — Distilled Japanese pepper given intranasally increased time on the rotating rod in mice. The study did not measure Parkinson postural instability after culinary exposure.

oral soybean-oil placebo and measured vocal tremor modulation — The essential voice tremor crossover quantified sustained-vowel amplitude modulation during the soybean-oil placebo and active periods. The methods omit oil grade and the study does not estimate habitual vocal loudness in Parkinson disease.

Injected cineole and non-cardamom leaf oil in mice; haloperidol catalepsy rather than dystonia — Potentiated experimental catalepsy is not evidence ground culinary cardamom worsens Parkinson dystonia; primary abstract only.

Oral cyclodextrin-complexed isolated cineole in reserpine mice; bar catalepsy rather than dystonia — Reduced induced catalepsy in a different model, formulation and route cannot establish a change in clinical dystonia after ground cardamom.

hoarseness with competing anatomical cause in one adult who ate blueberries — Hoarseness progressed despite blueberry cessation and imaging found an anterior mediastinal mass with partial tracheal compression. The case supplies no verified berry preparation, acoustic voice-volume measure, causal allergy challenge, or Parkinson cohort.
blueberry powder in juice and different outcome — A possible preliminary gait report was located. No voice-volume estimate is available.

mixed diet allows frozen blueberries; aggregate motor score — Menus allow frozen berries but actual selection is unverified; motor total does not separately quantify voice volume or blueberry effects.

isolated green-leaf chalcone and behavior in a 6-OHDA mouse model — Intracerebral DDC improved broad behavior measures and reduced neuronal loss. The available report gives no specific rigidity outcome or dietary leaf exposure.
strain-defined fermented milk — The trial provides composite motor and nonmotor data for a distinct intervention.
firm yogurt used as a diagnostic bolus — The study compared existing swallowing performance in patients and controls. Strained yogurt and handwriting were untested.
yogurt drink used as a diagnostic bolus — The test evaluated whether a voice change indicated airway penetration or aspiration. The report supplies no handwriting effect.
yogurt as a diagnostic comparator — Yogurt was a diagnostic comparison material and no separate effect on handwriting was measured.
yogurt as a diagnostic swallowing bolus — The mixed neurological sample used a diagnostic bolus. The study did not estimate strained yogurt and handwriting change.

pediatric peanut allergy series with labial oil testing and generic hoarseness — The report gives two positives among 50 labial oil tests but no oil-specific hoarseness count, processing grade or voice intensity. The authors and clinical site overlap with the 1997 report.

blinded peanut oil versus olive oil oral challenge — Ten participants with prior systemic reactions to peanuts did not react to either challenge oil. Voice volume and Parkinson status were unmeasured.

oral refined peanut oil and acute allergy safety — All 60 peanut-allergic participants tolerated refined oil during the controlled challenge. The allergy outcome supplies no acoustic loudness or hypophonia measure.

oral peanut oil challenge and related refined-oil skin-test reagent — The skin prick extract is specified as derived from refined oil. The oral oil grade was not established, and no lower voice volume scale was used.

thyme-containing mixed diet; aggregate nonmotor score — Both menus use thyme in cooked recipes of unspecified freshness. The report gives MDS-UPDRS Part I totals, which include apathy, but no apathy item or thyme-specific comparison.

common-sage extract chemistry and antiproliferative experiment — The author abstract confirms sage-derived extracts and chemical and cancer cell endpoints. P33 references this same report. It provides no culinary dose or Parkinson symptom comparison.

clinical symptom measurement or proxy without the frozen food preparation — The boxing study reports balance and mobility scores relevant to fall risk. It lacks counted fall events and a ground-sage comparison.

symptom measurement, clinical outcome or comparison without the frozen culinary exposure — The Parkinson cohort records questionnaire-reported fall history. The paper predicts cognitive classification and supplies neither prospective fall frequency nor dried-sage exposure.

symptom measurement, clinical outcome or comparison without the frozen culinary exposure — Most selected hip fractures followed low falls. The study compares outcomes after fracture, without longitudinal fall counts or a dried-sage intervention.
sage extract and mouse footprint geometry — Sciatic function improved. The test supplies no measure of falls.

Parkinson randomized trial administers common sage leaves — Encapsulated dried leaves rather than fresh culinary leaves; the publicly available results summarize cognitive and salivation measures but give no handwriting result, and the referenced secondary-outcome timetable is missing.

single-arm oral lovage-root blend and urinary urgency severity — Mean urgency severity fell by 1.6 and 1.9 points at days 7 and 37 in patients with urinary infection. No control arm, episodes of urgency, separate leaf exposure or Parkinson group. Registry and paper describe one cohort.

lovage root combination and acute cystitis urgency severity — The same phase III cohort showed falling urgency severity in both acute cystitis arms. The herbal arm received a root mixture and the assessment did not measure frequency after dried lovage leaf in people with Parkinson disease.
dried oregano infusion and drug-induced hypnosis in mice — At the higher infusion dose pentobarbital-induced hypnosis was longer. Spontaneous daytime sleepiness was not measured.

standardized oregano extract and overnight polysomnography in healthy men — The patent and 2012 conference abstract describe one crossover cohort. Sleep architecture showed no apparent change and the experiment did not measure clinical daytime sleepiness.

oral avocado oil and systemic pressure in hypertensive rats — Systolic and diastolic pressure were lower in treated hypertensive rats. The study measured neither an orthostatic response nor subjective lightheadedness.

oral avocado oil and pressure in hypertensive and normotensive rats — Avocado oil lowered pressure in hypertensive rats and had no clear effect in normotensive rats. This does not measure orthostatic symptoms or the frozen refined-oil exposure.

oral avocado oil and blood pressure in adults with metabolic syndrome — The official result says blood pressure did not clearly change compared with soybean oil. It supplies no postural pressure, symptoms, Parkinson cohort or refined-oil designation.

Four Parkinson participants reported clarity of writing — Table 15 writing-clarity scores remained 0, 0, 1 and 1 across all conditions. Character size was not measured and the exposure was inhaled or topical oil.

bok choy grouped with dark-green vegetables in a prospective falls cohort — The questionnaire listed bok choy in a combined dark-green vegetable category. Among 953 Taiwanese postmenopausal women, 183 fell and 25 had low-impact fractures. The report gives no separate effect for bok choy, no cooking detail and no Parkinson postural testing.

thyme-containing mixed diet; aggregate motor daily living score — Both menus include thyme in cooked recipes; Part II contains handwriting but no item-specific micrographia or fresh thyme effect is reported.

low — Oral essential-oil pretreatment worsened mouse motor coordination under midazolam challenge. Rotating-rod motor performance after a sedative drug differs from a hand dexterity test, and whole ground seed remained untested.

enriched rice bran oil and rat stride length — Footprint stride length improved in treated haloperidol rats. Chamuangone and oil were assigned together, with no plain refined oil arm or human stride result.

cod fillet hydrolysate and grip strength in older adults — A blinded older-adult trial found no clear grip-strength difference with the hydrolysate. It did not test handwriting size, grilled cod, or a Parkinson group.

PD low-fat mixed menu includes raw cucumber as replaceable salad ingredient; individual consumption and posture item unavailable — No cucumber-specific effect or postural-instability estimate is reported; the trial only reports the total motor scale and allows courgette substitution.

PD mixed ovo-lacto vegetarian diet with cucumber among menu ingredients; some participants also received enemas — Raw preparation, individual cucumber intake and postural-instability item are not established; no cucumber-specific effect can be isolated.

Aqueous cucumber fruit extract in lead-exposed rats; motor tests unnamed in accessible abstract — Non-Parkinson animal toxicity model and aqueous extract differ from raw cucumber consumption and human postural instability; original full methods unavailable.

Millet porridge in both groups of a labor analgesia study; pain measurement but no millet comparison — Pain differences compare epidural selection, not millet intake; species and preparation details are unspecified and population does not have Parkinson disease.

Millet flour bread contaminated by monocrotophos; acute abdominal pain in an outbreak — Pain is associated with measured pesticide contamination rather than ordinary boiled millet; no Parkinson sample or clean control.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S7.519 discusses physical treatment of millet crops and root development. No ingestion or symptom outcome was tested.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The Pennisetum entry identifies pearl millet and a reported association with agalactia in sows. Other millet names identify different grasses. There is no culinary or Parkinson motor comparison.

millet among several allowable grain choices — The original protocol lists millet among several allowable grain choices. It does not verify participant-level boiled preparation or intake. Edited testimonials report outcomes for the combined program without a separate pain severity comparison for this ingredient.

dissolved powdered ginger and resting pressure in older women — Hypertensive water and ginger groups showed comparable resting systolic changes of −2.70 and −3.28 mmHg. No standing challenge, Parkinson cohort or fresh-grated ginger.

Ginger rhizome extract given to healthy volunteers with acute cuff blood pressure measurements — Systolic pressure declined from the higher-dose arm baseline at two hours. The recorded posture, controlled contrast and standing lightheadedness are unverified; the extract differs from culinary grated ginger.

Fine-chopped ginger as an assigned food in 22 healthy men; postprandial cuff pressure — The primary paper reports no matched ginger-versus-control difference for the named standing symptom. Postprandial cuff measurements, fine chopping and non-Parkinson participants limit fit.

Parkinson randomized mixed diets both include minced ginger and record lightheadedness safety events — Individual ingestion and grating were not established. Safety event counts do not identify on-standing severity or attribute the events to ginger.

Single-arm ginger extract capsule study with ambulatory pressure averages in type 2 diabetes — Reported declines are pre-post ambulatory averages; no standing challenge, symptom-specific severity, matched dietary preparation or Parkinson population.

human Parkinson grapefruit juice with cabergoline pharmacokinetics — Five people receiving cabergoline had about 1.7 times the plasma concentration with grapefruit juice coadministration. The abstract gives no raw whole-fruit comparison, stride result or observed motor change.

grapefruit-derived vesicles applied at the tendon and objectively measured mouse stride — The authors report stride nearer to healthy mice after a local grapefruit-vesicle microneedle treatment for tendon injury. This is neither a Parkinson model nor raw grapefruit ingestion.
grapefruit essential oil aroma in a mixed population — The planned measures do not isolate a raw grapefruit effect on stride length. The registry gives no results.

oregano extract and in vitro monoamine oxidase activity — The patent reports MAO-A and MAO-B inhibition by extract in an enzyme assay. No daily OFF hours, food preparation contrast or human regimen was studied.

oregano on a shared Parkinson diet and levodopa-equivalent dose — The diet includes oregano among many seasonings. The reported daily medication dose changes are distinct from daily OFF time, and Table 4 values differ from the narrative.

separate Origanum species tea and Parkinson motor examination — The Parkinson pilot measured UPDRS III and reports a within-arm p of .069. Filtered dried marjoram tea differs from eating fresh oregano and the paper gives no daily OFF duration.
sumac extract in Parkinson-derived fibroblasts — The study measured cellular responses and did not measure muscle rigidity after sumac ingestion.

soybean oil changed in oral feed with stepping and locomotion measures — Soybean oil went from 30 to 0 g/kg as other feed components changed. Stepping and open-field results did not clearly differ by diet. Oil grade and an independent human bradykinesia effect remain unknown.

soybean oil in mixed oral diets with timed motor measures — Soybean oil was 10 g/kg in control feed and absent in the alternate formulas. There is no separable oil effect and timed pole performance is a mouse motor proxy.

soybean oil comparator with slower rat motor behavior after interesterified fat — The interesterified-fat offspring group showed lower adult locomotion. This developmental rat comparison gives no independently measured refined soybean oil or clinical bradykinesia effect.

soybean comparator in a mouse pole test — The rotenone soybean group took 7.83 seconds versus 4.73 in unlesioned mice on the same soybean diet. Middle and high perilla outperformed rotenone soybean, with no isolated refined oil or clinical bradykinesia estimate.

soybean oil in an enteral formula and concurrent levodopa treatment — The combined tube formula contains soybean oil of unspecified grade. No isolated bradykinesia measure or soybean oil exposure comparison.

PD Sargol powder tablet; planned Part II; no drooling-item outcome accessible — Part II includes saliva and drooling item 2.2; its planned assessment and total scores cannot establish an effect on drooling severity.

egg-yolk oil as adjunct in hemiplegia dysarthria — The deposited abstract reports a larger change in a broad Robertson measure with an egg-yolk-derived product. Original route, individual speech measures and full methods are open. The comparison uses hemiplegia and an oil intervention.

eggs in a Parkinson diet intervention and composite motor score — The intervention menu lists eggs and the motor scale includes speech. The study gives no egg preparation, actual exposure, or outcome specific to speech intelligibility.

whole walnuts and mouse rotarod latency to fall — 6% walnut diet did not clearly affect rotarod latency (p=.9999). Walnut plus housing enrichment improved performance, with no enrichment-only arm. Whole nuts, experimental latency and aged mice.

whole walnut diets and latency to fall on rod or plank — Aged rats had task-dependent longer latency at 2% or 6% and shorter latency on the large plank at 9%. Several tasks were null. Whole nuts and challenge latency differ from oral oil and everyday falls.

whole walnuts with matched training and postural sway — Selected mediolateral dual-task interactions favored walnuts plus training. Anteroposterior significance differs between Table 4 and prose. Healthy older men, whole nuts and no clinical fall counts.
enriched rice bran oil and rat motor coordination — Ladder and hanging measures improved, without a hand dexterity test or plain oil arm.
extracted rice bran oil and rotarod coordination — The oil group showed less haloperidol-induced rotarod impairment, with grade, individual digit dexterity and clinical Parkinson outcomes unverified.

Oral exposure to dill in cooked food and observed oropharyngeal allergy — Tongue and throat swelling and oral irritation were reported. Neither drooling severity nor saliva production was measured and fresh material was documented for skin testing only.
Authentic dried dill leaf capsules with gastrointestinal symptom tracking — Esophageal symptoms were captured in a type 2 diabetes trial. Drooling and salivary flow were not separate endpoints.

The registered controlled pilot followed 10 PD participants and 10 household controls completing a four-week multi-food and lactulose intervention. The menu included optional green beans. The reported composite scores and adherence measure do not supply a fall count or a bean-specific effect.

Leaf extract and drug-induced involuntary rat oral movements — The tested leaf extract and alkaloid fraction addressed involuntary oral movements following prolonged neuroleptic exposure. The study gives no scored facial expressiveness or cooked leaf intervention.

Hoarseness observed after contaminated rice bran oil exposure — Hoarseness appeared in a long-term study of a poisoning outbreak. It has neither an acoustic volume measure nor an effect attributable to ordinary rice bran oil.

Rice oil odor comparison with wet-hoarse voice in a swallow rubric — The modified water swallowing test includes cough or wet-hoarse voice in one grade. The study did not grade voice loudness or change after ingesting oil.
Oral rice bran oil placebo and Parkinson motor examination — The primary clinical study provides no vocal intensity or component speech scores, no oil refinement specification, and no oil-free arm.

Millet listed among foods in a multi-ingredient Parkinson diet; no separate dyskinesia result — Preparation, individual millet intake and millet-specific comparator are unspecified; the reported motor total cannot estimate dyskinesia severity.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S7.519 discusses physical treatment of millet crops and root development. No ingestion or symptom outcome was tested.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The Pennisetum entry identifies pearl millet and a reported association with agalactia in sows. Other millet names identify different grasses. There is no culinary or Parkinson motor comparison.

ginger odor threshold measured in Parkinson participants — Table 5 gives recognition-pressure thresholds at three stimulus concentrations. The protocol did not compare olfactory severity after eating grated ginger.
ginger in four-aroma sensory training — 24 weeks vs conventional odors gave no clear TDI contrast. The regimen combined exposures and did not test ingestion.

dried ginger in six-aroma inhalation regimen — Identification change favored training versus mometasone among completers. Nonrandomization, unbalanced attrition and the multi-aroma exposure leave ginger oral effects untested.
herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu — The menu and composite motor outcome cannot quantify freezing episodes after dried lovage leaf.

source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S1.97 proposes parsley as a possible dietary source of related Rubisco peptides while modelling spinach-derived rubiscolin. No parsley isolate, dose or Parkinson outcome is measured.

veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison — The Petroselinum crispum entry describes furanocoumarins and primary photosensitization. The broader common-name cross-reference includes other genera. No frozen culinary or Parkinson symptom result appears.

Parkinson dietary menu with parsley and reported medication use — The source lists parsley among many ingredients. Neither the herb's form nor an item-level dyskinesia or time-with-dyskinesia estimate is available.

Verified oral dried powdered leaf preparation in people — Metabolite absorption was measured in healthy men. The trial gives no levodopa-induced dyskinesia observation and the formulation included yogurt.

A parsley-associated isolated flavone in a Parkinson-like motor model — Coordination, gait and molecular endpoints in an animal model do not measure levodopa-induced abnormal involuntary movements or a dried herb effect.

oral tarragon supplement and systolic blood pressure — The 2020 result posting gives week-12 systolic means 113 and 125 mmHg for extract and placebo. Its p values compare within-arm changes. A between-arm baseline-adjusted estimate, postural protocol and orthostatic outcome remain unreported.

oral extra-virgin avocado oil and rat recognition and spatial memory — Recognition and spatial tasks favored the oil groups in an ovariectomy and D-galactose model. The preprint and publication describe one study. The report did not assess Parkinson executive function.

whole-fruit mixed menu and unreported executive outcomes — The same trial registration and publication planned or collected executive tasks. The article and supplement give no result for cognition, and the exposure is whole avocado plus mango.

whole avocado and executive-task MRI and NIH Toolbox registration — No posted results in available official update, which shows Unknown status. The trial excludes Parkinson disease and assigns fruit rather than oil.
whole avocado crossover with prespecified cognitive measures — Secondary CANTAB and flanker outcomes are registered without results. The study assigns whole fruit in prediabetes.

maternal avocado oil and rat offspring recognition memory — Recognition memory improved in offspring of supplemented dams. Developmental exposure and recognition memory do not establish adult clinical executive function.

oral cold-pressed avocado oil and mouse recognition memory — Oil-fed obese mice preferred the novel object. Figure 3A reports within-group recognition, with no direct treatment contrast shown. It does not test clinical executive function.

avocado-oil mayonnaise in a ketogenic sample menu and narrative executive change — One Down syndrome and Alzheimer case describes executive change during a mixed diet without an isolated oil comparison, oil processing or quantified executive outcome.

flaxseed oil compared with corn oil and registered executive composite — The mild cognitive impairment pilot defines a composite using Trail Making, digit span and category fluency. No posted results, pressing method or Parkinson intervention.

oral Pazze flaxseed oil chow and fear extinction — The dissertation reports a diet main effect p = .726 during fear extinction. The task concerns aversive memory and cannot estimate Parkinson executive function.

pooled omega-3 supplementation and cognitive trajectories by matched observational groups — MMSE, ADAS-Cog13 and CDR-SB had faster decline in pooled supplement users. No separate flaxseed oil estimate or processing specification. Observational confounding and whole-scale outcomes limit transfer.

flaxseed table oil and executive function in healthy older adults — The flaxseed arm improved 0.30 on phonemic fluency versus 0.03 with corn oil (p = .049), with lower baseline fluency in the flaxseed arm. The total Frontal Assessment Battery comparison was p = .142. The trial had no Parkinson participants or documented pressing method.

self-reported Parkinson urgency with mixed broccoli and white mustard tea — The 2021 eight-completer pilot reported better urgency and frequency. The 2024 report gives 13 of 14 with urgency attenuation and transient worsening in some participants exceeding the usual schedule. Participant overlap is unknown. Neither uncontrolled report isolates mustard or quantifies urgency frequency attributable to it.

mustard constituent and voiding interval in rats — Intravesical allyl isothiocyanate increased voiding frequency. The experimental direction opposes the premise at the proxy level, but the direct bladder route did not measure human urgency or ground mustard ingestion.

freeze-dried blackberry powder and executive-related tests in older adults — Fluid cognition composite p=.04 without a specified arm contrast. The poster reports no significant treatment effect on virtual-maze flexibility. An executive-domain estimate and independent reproduction remain open.
blackberry diet and spatial working memory in aged rats — Short-term Morris water maze performance improved. The source is an aging animal model and exact diet preparation remains open.

mixed thawed blackberry smoothie and executive task outcomes — Task switching had a treatment-by-session response-time interaction p = .001, but no clear treatment main effect. The healthy-adult drink used four fruits.

multicomponent capsule including blackberry and executive testing — The capsule includes blackberry among numerous dehydrated fruit and vegetable ingredients. Favorable within-period TESEN changes do not isolate blackberry, a frozen preparation, or diagnosed Parkinson disease.
aqueous marjoram extract and drug-induced catalepsy — Extract reduced time on the forced posture assay. The test does not rate dystonia severity in Parkinson disease.

paprika xanthophyll and athlete endurance rather than everyday fatigue — Full-sample xanthophyll-alone versus placebo did not separate the lactate or heart-rate endpoints. Low-baseline-NAD subgroup findings are endurance proxies. The paper gives no subjective everyday-fatigue estimate or raw pepper intervention.

red paprika xanthophyll drink and perceived postexercise fatigue — Subjective fatigue after treadmill exercise declined more with the extract in 14 athletes. Neither raw pepper nor Parkinson fatigue was tested.

isolated capsinoid crossover and exercise metabolism — The preprint and journal abstract report a shift toward fat oxidation after exercise and inconclusive glycogen restoration. The strongly matched registry and publications describe one likely cohort and give no participant-rated clinical fatigue estimate.

repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking — Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.

food-pattern scores and self-reported fatigue — The study compares cross-sectional MIND and Mediterranean diet scores and individual fatigue ratings in the MVP cohort. The inputs do not isolate bell pepper.

purified dihydrocapsiate in canola carrier and perceived exercise fatigue — A crossover compared 12 mg dihydrocapsiate in canola oil to cellulose placebo during cycling in adults with overweight or obesity. No perceived-fatigue difference was reported. This provides no raw bell pepper or isolated canola oil estimate.

paprika xanthophyll with preregistered fatigue outcome not reported — The registry lists fatigue VAS as a secondary measure. The accessible respiratory report with 21 participants gives no separate fatigue estimate.

paprika extract and everyday fatigue in a completed trial — The official registry lists 23 enrolled rather than its target 30, 9 mg daily extract or placebo for eight weeks, and an everyday fatigue VAS. Neither arm results nor a matching original report could be verified.

walnut oil in a Parkinson diet menu with composite motor score — Appendix A names walnut oil and the motor examination includes bradykinesia. The paper gives no preparation, isolated oil exposure or bradykinesia item result.

dietary cold-pressed walnut oil and locomotion in toxin-exposed flies — Cold-pressed walnut oil improved climbing relative to rotenone alone at both follow-ups, a movement signal opposite the frozen clinical direction in this model. The assay does not measure bradykinesia in people.

cold-pressed topical coconut oil and childhood enuresis — A pediatric trial reported fewer bedwetting episodes with topical coconut versus paraffin. The trial excluded urgency and abnormal frequency. Its topical procedure and population differ from the frozen claim.
self-reported coconut oil frequency and total Parkinson symptom score — The cross-sectional composite association specifies no virgin oil and does not count urinary urgency episodes.

virgin coconut oil in a whole diet with a Parkinson urinary item — A ketogenic menu naming virgin coconut oil had a 0.70-point larger decrease on a multi-symptom urinary item. The trial did not resolve an independent oil effect or count urgency episodes.

low — An infant exposed to mixed green anise and star anise infusion had acute systemic illness with seizures and nystagmus. The mixture and pediatric setting provide no ingredient-specific result or visual hallucination frequency in Parkinson’s.

self-reported coconut oil use and overall PD symptom progression — Unreviewed observational preprint gives mixed-model total PRO-PD progression association, not an oil-grade or dream-enactment estimate; co-use and multiple tests limit inference.
unspecified coconut oil and the self-rated REM behavior item — Inverse sign in the displayed baseline pair. The item gives no episode count, grade or within-participant change.
self-reported coconut oil frequency and total Parkinson symptom score — The cross-sectional composite association gives no oil grade or dream-enactment frequency and cannot establish causation.

ketogenic diet and one participant's reported sleep behavior; oil exposure unverified — Participant 008 reported ongoing episodes and little overall diet change, while a companion perceived less movement. The report identifies coconut or avocado oil use for participant 019, not 008; no virgin-oil exposure or before-after event count is established.

thyme oil constituents and experimental cholinergic measures — The original abstract concerns synaptic and receptor effects of thyme oil and constituents. It supplies no human attention score or effect of fresh thyme consumption.

isolated thymol and attention-related behavior in a juvenile rat model — The original author abstract describes favorable behavior. Task estimates, original methods and the 2023 correction content remain unresolved.
dried thyme and perceived memory — The trial reports a self-rated memory score. There was no objective attention task, fresh preparation or Parkinson’s subgroup.

isolated thymol and Y-maze alternation after propionic acid in rats — Isolated thymol increased spontaneous alternation 35% relative to model controls, a working-memory proxy. No fresh thyme or clinical attention measure.

pinto among cooked bean rotation and signed stool changes — The pooled whole bean group more often reported increased stool frequency and short-term softening than rice; it also reported bloating. Pinto-specific constipation severity, Parkinson diagnosis and dietary attribution remain open.

canned pinto and canned green bean crossover and stool-change questionnaire — The small crossover found no clear difference in combined stool changes. The preparation was canned and there was no clinical constipation direction or Parkinson group.

mixed cooked pulses and constipation severity — An apparently linked conference abstract reports lower constipation severity after a rotation including pinto beans. This single-arm study cannot separate individual pulses or provide a Parkinson comparison.

canned pinto beans and participant-reported stool changes — Pinto phases produced reports of stool changes, combined without a dependable constipation direction. The beans were canned and participants were outside Parkinson cohorts.

canola, olive and fish oil feasibility trial and registered pain VAS — Official record links a design matching the existing P49 report. Result fields are empty and dose wording differs. Registry adds methods, not an independent trial.

oral liquid canola oil and osteoarthritis pain — The three-arm 30-person feasibility study found no clear between-group difference in secondary measures that included pain. The abstract does not state cold-pressed grade.

Sunola fish oil blend and clinical pain, plant identity unresolved — Primary report names Sunola and changes fish oil dose. Lead investigator used canola in an interview. Product plant identity remains unresolved.

shared collection original source context — Bot's rapeseed/MCT capsule and the Jazayeri rapeseed/fluoxetine comparator are separate families. Their depression endpoints and unverified oil processing supply no frozen effect estimate.

shared collection original source context — Rapeseed oil is a component of the multi-food SYSDIET comparison; ALA source discussion is supplementary. It is not an isolated grade-specific contrast for the frozen symptom.
rapeseed and other foods in a Mediterranean diet with rheumatoid arthritis pain — Pain VAS favored the bundle. Cooking oils, formulated spread and foods changed together. No pressing grade.

canola active comparator and osteoarthritis pain — Original abstract and secondary extraction distinguish the inconclusive COAT pain contrast and missing primary table. Grade and oil-free comparator unavailable.
raw, steamed and boiled Brussels sprout volatiles — Sulfides changed with preparation, but roasting and human smell ability were not tested.
thawed Brussels sprout sampling and retronasal flavor — The sprouts were not roasted. Change in liking did not track retronasal intensity for this vegetable; olfactory impairment was not assessed.
microwave-cooked Brussels sprouts in healthy sensory panel — Retronasal odor liking related to food liking. No roasted exposure or clinical olfactory impairment.
raw and cooked Brussels sprout volatiles — Food volatile differences do not measure the ability to smell after eating.

oral avocado oil comparator and written symbol-count task — The timed symbol substitution test reports accuracy and completion, with 90 seconds in journal Methods and 60 in the registry and protocol. Scores increased in both arms. The report gives no character size or clinical micrographia measurement and no refined oil specification.

black pepper oil odor and whole saliva secretion — The author abstract reports higher saliva output after black pepper oil odor. Sixty healthy students were randomized to oil odors or water. The complete tables, clinical drooling and culinary ingestion remain outside the verified result.

whole pepper aroma and combined capsaicin care — Combined treatment was stopped in one patient after drooling increased. No Parkinson diagnosis, cracked pepper ingestion, or independent pepper effect.

spinach-enriched chow and conditioned eyeblink learning — Aged rats showed better conditioned eyeblink learning after spinach-enriched chow. This reflex is distinct from spontaneous facial expressiveness.

spinach listed in a mixed Parkinson diet and total motor score — The menu lists spinach but gives no individual intake or cooked preparation. Total UPDRS III includes facial expression, while no separately reported item or isolated spinach result is available.

chervil in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome — The menu lists chervil and the motor examination includes rigidity. The paper does not establish fresh chervil exposure or report item-level rigidity change.

pooled fish intake and overactive bladder — Higher fish intake was associated with lower odds of a composite overactive bladder outcome in NHANES. Grilled sardines and urgency without leakage were not separated.

oily fish category and Parkinson urinary score — Parkinson clinical records include pooled oily fish and the SCOPA urinary domain. The paper does not estimate a fish-specific association or separate urgency.
oat bran comparator with cognition measurements — Official protocol lists oat bran powder and a different active comparator. No posted results, cooked whole oats or separate hand dexterity test.
oatmeal and total Parkinson symptom burden — The survey reports an inconclusive composite association and no separate dexterity measure.
green oat extract and computer tracking in healthy adults — Some cursor-tracking results favored extract, without clinical dexterity testing or cooked oats in Parkinson's.

combined flaxseed-derived omega-3 and vitamin E with Parkinson total score — The aggregate change favored the combination. The first public registry omitted UPDRS and specified a different dose and clinic. The 2019 revision postdates the paper. No rigidity item, verified cold pressing or oil-only comparison.

independent combined flaxseed-derived omega-3 and vitamin E trial in Parkinson disease — Part III mean changes were −1.9 and +3.1, with p=.05 as printed and no clear part-level benefit in the authors’ interpretation. No separate rigidity, verified oil pressing or oil-only estimate.

plasma alpha-linolenic acid and the examiner-rated Parkinson rigidity item — Rigidity correlated inversely with ALA in the age-adjusted analysis (ρ = −.331, p = .046), with a weaker sex-adjusted estimate (ρ = −.278, p = .096). The small cross-sectional cohort provides no oil ingestion comparison.

possible cold-pressed flaxseed blend in an uncontrolled combined Parkinson regimen — Case 4 describes less rigidity and Case 5 less arm stiffness after an oral and intravenous regimen. Product exposure at case level and an independent oil effect are unresolved.
baked eggplant acute adverse case with a different endpoint — The reported acute allergy supplies no dystonia outcome and does not isolate roasted eggplant.
eggplant extract in a rotenone cell model — Oxidative and cell-survival results do not measure dystonia or roasted eggplant exposure.
raw carrot aroma stimulus and trained panel ratings — Characterizing raw carrot aroma did not test a change in eater olfactory impairment.

clinical olfaction and nutrient-density comparison in newly diagnosed Parkinson disease — The case-control study assessed smell identification and dietary nutrient density without isolating raw carrot as an exposure.

carrot frequency model and independent rhinitis-olfaction model — The carrot odds-ratio text is inconsistent, and the separate rhinitis-to-smell association does not establish a carrot effect. Preparation, temporality and Parkinson applicability remain unresolved.

coriander listed among seasonings of a mixed Parkinson vegetarian diet — The diet lists coriander without confirming plant part, dried preparation or consumption; there is no post-treatment drooling outcome or isolated ingredient effect.

living coriander plant exposure and salivary analyte concentrations — There was no ingestion or reported salivary flow or clinical drooling measure; biochemical saliva concentrations are different outcomes.
pea protein in a mixed sachet and registered walking speed — Plant blend, whey and control sarcopenia protocol specifies six-meter walking speed. No posted results or sample taking cooked peas alone.

pea proteins among several active ingredients and gait within SPPB — Completed prototype powder trial with separate ingredients and no posted results. Does not test whole cooked peas or Parkinson gait.

pea beverage and registered walking tasks after resistance exercise — Three beverages combined with exercise and timed gait assessments in older adults. Recruiting and no posted results. No cooked-pea Parkinson comparison.

isolated pea lectin and forced stepping in rats — The paraquat plus pea lectin group had a lower forced-stepping score. The lectin-only group had no clear decrease. No cooked peas or human walking speed were tested.
isolated lectin and forced forelimb placement — The combined paraquat and lectin arm developed forelimb placement deficits. No cooked peas or human walking velocity was measured.
individual Parkinson symptoms and diet scores — The study gives a whole-diet fatigue association without a dried chervil estimate.
garden chervil leaf and stem chemical analysis — Lyophilized chervil material was evaluated in chemical and cell assays, without fatigue measurements.
source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits — S7.519 describes sweet cherry among fruit trees used for grafting work. No dietary cherry or measured neurologic symptom is present.

sweet cherry extract and movement in rotenone-exposed flies — Extract-treated flies showed better spontaneous and induced movement during rotenone exposure. This assay did not measure dystonia or test dried cherry.

systemic capsaicin and motor activity in rats — Spontaneous activity declined in intact rats and levodopa-elicited activity declined in reserpine rats. Walking speed and culinary smoked paprika were unmeasured.

intraperitoneal capsaicin and locomotor activity in 6-OHDA rats — The authors report improved locomotor measures, opposite the proposed direction on that surrogate. No walking-speed estimate after smoked paprika was available.
systemic capsaicin and levodopa-elicited motor activity in rats — Capsaicin reduced the measured high motor activity. The study did not quantify clinical dyskinesia or test paprika.

intraperitoneal capsaicin and abnormal involuntary movements in 6-OHDA rats — Abnormal involuntary movements decreased in the model. Exposure and endpoints differ from culinary paprika and Parkinson clinical dyskinesia.

oral almond oil vehicle across estradiol and lesion comparisons in rats — The matching dissertation confirms oral almond oil in all four groups. Basal cardiovascular and baroreflex measures did not clearly differ. No oil-free contrast or clinical orthostatic-lightheadedness outcome was available.

thyme-containing mixed diet; aggregate nonmotor score — The Part I total includes hallucinations and psychosis but does not isolate visual hallucination frequency; individual thyme intake and effects are unreported.
blueberry powder in juice and different outcome — A possible preliminary gait report was located. No speech-intelligibility estimate is available.

blueberry-containing diet in a corticobasal degeneration case — One patient with autopsy-confirmed corticobasal degeneration was essentially mute at a visit when the diet included blueberries. Preparation and earlier intake are unspecified and there is no causal or idiopathic PD comparison.

mixed dietary patterns include optional uncooked blueberries; aggregate motor score — The total motor score provides no listener-scored intelligibility or blueberry-specific comparison, and individual berry intake is unverified.

whole hazelnuts offered and Parkinson motor composite includes facial expression — The dietary Appendix lists hazelnuts with nuts and seeds. The motor score contains facial expression, without a published separate facial result or a hazelnut oil assignment.

potato-fiber buns in a crossover with appetite and stool outcomes — In the full report, satiety increased with one preparation. Stool form and fecal fat did not differ across groups, and sleep was not assessed. The poster, trial and publication share one comparison.
combined potato preparations and sleep efficiency — Completed official trial, no posted results. Protocol pools baked, boiled and mashed potato and registers sleep efficiency.

boiled or mashed potatoes and prospective sleep duration — Adjusted sleep duration was +0.9 minutes/day per 80 g/day (99% CI −0.6 to +2, p=.1). The questionnaire did not report a roasted-potato category, an insomnia scale or a Parkinson-specific result.

genetically proxied potato preference and insomnia — Two-variant preference instrument has OR 1.17 (95% CI 1.10–1.25). No measured intake, culinary preparation, Parkinson population or insomnia severity result.

clinical case or dietary history without a matched ingredient comparison — Two original clinical histories report potatoes or chips as part of highly restricted diets. The form is incompletely characterized and a food-specific direction is absent.
nigella oil and forelimb skill learning in healthy mice — Reaching success increased late in training in the oil group. This is skill acquisition with an oil exposure and no Parkinson impairment.

ground culinary shiso as an odor stimulus in healthy women — Smelling steam from rice with ground shiso increased pleasantness ratings. The study did not test impairment of smell after eating dried leaves or Parkinson disease.
isolated inhaled perillaldehyde and required smell pathway — Induced anosmia prevented the compound's forced-swim response. It was an experimental manipulation and not a restored-smell endpoint.

isolated capsiate and willingness to invest effort in healthy men — The publisher abstract reports no change in readiness to invest effort during repeated cycling after 12 mg capsiate. No published arm estimates, clinical apathy rating, or roasted pepper exposure.

Parkinson dietary crossover with baseline apathy and no identifiable bell-pepper contrast — Interviewed participants described pre-existing apathy as a barrier. The trial registered a Starkstein scale, and the report gives baseline prevalence without a post-diet group response and with no assigned roasted bell pepper.

baked sweet pepper in Parkinson menus and Part I apathy item within a total score — The ketogenic menu bakes stuffed sweet peppers and the low-fat plan bakes capsicum as a topping. Published item-level results did not include apathy. The diet comparison cannot distinguish a pepper effect.

purified nonpungent Capsicum and POMS2 vigor-activity in older adults — The randomized older-adult sample produced no significant between-arm vigor-activity comparison. The study used extract, supplied no apathy-scale result and excluded motor disorders.

motivation or initiative within Parkinsonism symptom score and vegetable groups — Motivation or initiative was included in the patient-reported symptom checklist. Regression results for vegetables targeted the total score and provided neither a roasted pepper exposure nor an individual apathy item estimate.

individualized plant-rich timed diet and rated apathy in a Parkinson cohort — Apathy changed from 13.65 to 9.0 in the diet group and 13.05 to 13.6 in controls. Narrative and tabulated post-treatment comparisons conflict. The intervention did not quantify roasted bell pepper exposure.
Parkinson case with formula during levodopa treatment — The report is a levodopa and Japanese-pepper combination lead. It gives no recorded dyskinesia outcome or ground Sichuan pepper exposure.
related Japanese pepper in an animal motor model — The intranasal preparation was evaluated with pole and rota-rod tasks. The experiment contains no levodopa-induced dyskinesia endpoint.

topical macadamia carrier and composite hand sensation in cervical myelopathy — Right-hand grip was higher by week eight in one uncontrolled case. Subjective rating bundled fine tasks with other complaints. The regimen combined hands-on treatment and essential oils and the oil was applied topically.

topical macadamia carrier and qualitative fine hand tasks in carpal tunnel syndrome — Writing and pinch tasks were reported to improve with mixed treatment in one patient. Figure 1 gives a descriptive right-grip increase of 0.8 kg. This is a different route, condition and intervention with unspecified pressing.

planned postmeal psychomotor vigilance after oral macadamia oil — The registry plans psychomotor vigilance testing for alertness after liquid or powdered oil meals in healthy adults. No results are posted, and a vigilance task does not measure Parkinson manual dexterity.

spearmint among suggested culinary herbs — The original protocol lists spearmint among suggested culinary herbs. It does not verify participant-level fresh preparation or intake. Edited testimonials report outcomes for the combined program without a separate depressive symptom severity comparison for this ingredient.

aqueous spearmint extract and POMS depression/dejection in older adults — Day-90 changes were +.30 placebo, +.81 at 600 mg and −1.51 at 900 mg with overall p=.0862. Dose and baseline differences limit inference. The trial used extract in a non-Parkinson population.
extract blend and depression scales in adults with sleep complaints — Both adjusted depressive symptom comparisons spanned zero. No fresh spearmint or Parkinson population.

peppermint extract and tail-suspension immobility in male mice — Peppermint extract plus rotenone produced 183.67 seconds mean immobility versus 251.48 with rotenone alone (p<.001). The same animals improved locomotion. This is a different species, extract, animal assay and exposure from fresh spearmint in people.

topical macadamia oil control and anxiety assessment in fibromyalgia — The five-person fibromyalgia analysis found no clear difference in STAI state or trait anxiety between topical macadamia oil and the same oil plus geranium (p = .09 and .63). The 2021 registry and university dissertation are earlier reports of the same crossover. The study did not test ingestion or an oil-free comparator.

macadamia oil active comparator and state anxiety — State anxiety did not differ clearly between macadamia oil and krill oil (group p = .8611). Both groups received oil and no Parkinson cohort or oil-free comparator was studied.

canine hindlimb paresis after raw or roasted kernels — Thirteen dogs had acute hindlimb paresis, recumbency or joint pain after kernel exposure. Freezing of gait and expressed oil were outside the case series.

acute hindlimb weakness and ataxia after macadamia kernels in dogs — Canine field cases showed ataxia and experimental dogs became too weak to stand normally. The experiment exposed dogs to roasted kernels and did not count Parkinson freezing episodes.

plasma piperine and total MDS-UPDRS Part III in PD — In 13 patients with both genetic variants r=−.466, p=.108. The direction is descriptive. Exposure source and particle size are unknown and there was no reported isolated hand-dexterity estimate.

preliminary drug-induced sleep assay of tarragon tincture — The 50 mg/kg behavior-study dose was selected in preliminary induced-sleep testing. Drug names differ between report and dissertation Contents, and no tarragon sleep values are accessible. Parkinson insomnia and ordinary sleep remain untested.

injected essential oil and acute mouse sedation — Overt sedation and reduced rotarod performance followed some doses of intraperitoneal essential oil. The study provides no baseline insomnia, sleep duration or spontaneous sleep measure.

combined cruciferous vegetable frequency and drooling measured in a Parkinson cohort — The original dietary abstract pooled cauliflower and broccoli. The likely overlapping journal report supplies a clinical drooling scale and no relationship to cauliflower or its preparation.

injected drug with peanut-oil carrier and later visual hallucinations in recurrent mania — The original Methods and case describe the peanut-oil vehicle and visual hallucinations after active drug withdrawal in the same study. It gives no isolated oil effect, oral cold-pressed exposure or Parkinson symptom-frequency estimate.

historical topical drug exposure and observed visual behavior — The 1947 letter describes apparent visual behavior and separately identifies arachis oil as the contemporary vehicle. Exact batch and oil grade are unverified. The drug poisoning, topical route and non-Parkinson population preclude attribution to edible oil.

Cinnamon appears in both multi-food PD diet plans; Part II composite rather than handwriting-size result — A combined activities-of-daily-living score cannot identify handwriting change, and the diet comparison cannot isolate ground cinnamon.

commercial watermelon juice and supine blood pressure — Ten young adults in a crossover. Two-hour estimate -13.1 mm Hg (95% CI -24.09 to -2.11, p=.02); the overall interaction was p=.91. No measured lightheadedness or postural test.

fresh diced watermelon and resting pressure in a fixed-order comparison — The Results and Table 1 show no clear within-watermelon pressure change. Cookie-phase pressure rose. The study did not measure standing pressure or lightheadedness.

oral pasteurized watermelon juice and vascular outcomes in postmenopausal women — The companion paper found no clear ambulatory pressure or vascular difference. The trial did not measure orthostatic pressure or lightheadedness.

watermelon flesh beverage and ambulatory pressure in adults with elevated pressure — The 24-hour, daytime and nighttime comparisons were inconclusive. No postural test or lightheadedness endpoint was reported.

incidental watermelon mention and orthostatic blood pressure in a dementia case — The original letter reports 130/84 mmHg supine and 114/79 mmHg standing during medication review in a posterior cortical atrophy case. The watermelon episode illustrates a visual error. The report gives no ingestion time or change in lightheadedness after a food intervention.

oral peanut oil comparator and grip strength in sarcopenic older adults — The standard-care control arm had no clear physical-function change. The trial measured grip strength rather than dexterity, excluded Parkinson disease and had no matched oil-free arm.

mixed meal containing caraway and acute allergic oral symptoms — The case describes oral burning and respiratory symptoms after a meal containing caraway seasoning. It did not measure swallowing performance or specify ground caraway.

Human Parkinson study with rice bran oil placebo and global score — Global MDS-UPDRS results were reported without Part II handwriting item 2.7, objective letter size or oil-grade data. The active oil carrier is unspecified.

acute upper-airway reaction with macadamia kernel and prior topical oil exposure — A child had coughing, lip swelling and severe hoarseness after chewing and spitting out a kernel. The earlier oil contact was topical. The primary report does not document oral oil or formal swallowing testing.

drooling in anaphylaxis after macadamia-containing ice cream — A three-year-old developed excessive drooling, generalized erythema and hypotensive shock after eating ice cream containing macadamia nuts. There was no formal swallowing exam or isolate of cold-pressed oil.
filtered marjoram tea and motor examination in Parkinson — Accessible report gives no facial expression score or fresh-leaf comparison.

cold-extracted pumpkin seed oil and diastolic pressure in a cardiometabolic cohort — Mean diastolic pressure declined about 3.3 mmHg in the oil group and 0.6 mmHg in controls. The primary analysis does not establish an adjusted change between groups. No orthostatic outcome was measured.

oral pumpkin seed oil and weekly tail-cuff pressure in hypertensive rats — At week 8 the oil group was at 134.20 versus 149.40 mmHg in hypertensive controls. The abstract cites a week-5 control. Cold pressing and orthostatic symptoms are unverified, and the Methods describe one oil administration inconsistently.

regulatory adverse-event table for a commercial ethanolic seed extract — The assessment names hypotension in a 2,245-patient uncontrolled seed-extract series without event counts or orthostatic context. The 2000 author abstract likely overlaps and does not enumerate adverse event types. No cold-pressed oil or Parkinson comparison.

pumpkin seed oil capsules and blood pressure in premenopausal women — The completed record lists systolic and diastolic pressure changes at 12 weeks. No results were verified and no orthostatic symptom was specified.
